notice_text: Avis de sollicitation de manifestations d’intérêt pour le recrutement d’un Consultant (Firme) pour l’Évaluation Environnementale et Sociale Stratégique (EESS) du Schéma Directeur d’Assainissement et Drainage (SDAD) et l’Étude d’Impact Environnemental et Social (EIES) du Plan Local d’Urbanisation (PLU) et Plan Particulier d’Aménagement (PPA) dans la Ville de Kananga, Province du Kasai Centrale en République Démocratique du Congo. AMI N°                                      : ZR-PURUK-543648-CS-QCBS Date de publication : 11 juin 2026 Date de clôture : 25 juin 2026 Source de financement               : Banque mondiale (Crédit IDA N° 72160-ZR) 1. Le Gouvernement de la République Démocratique du Congo (RDC) a obtenu un prêt de la Banque mondiale (BM) à hauteur de 100 millions USD pour financer le Projet d’Urgence et de Résilience Urbaine de Kananga (PURUK). Le Ministère de l’Urbanisme et de l’Habitat, à travers l’Unité de Gestion du Projet PURUK, envisage d’utiliser une partie de ces fonds pour couvrir les paiements relatifs au recrutement d’un consultant cabinet ou firme en charge de l’évaluation environnementale et sociale stratégique (EESS) du Schéma Directeur d’Assainissement et Drainage (SDAD) et l’Étude d’impact Environnemental et Social (EIES) du Plan Local d’Urbanisation (PLU) et Plan Particulier d’Aménagement (PPA) dans la Ville de Kananga. 2. Les prestations du Consultant consistent à : ( i) Réaliser une Évaluation Environnementale et Sociale Stratégique (EESS) du Schéma Directeur d’Assainissement et Drainage (SDAD) Ville de Kananga, et (ii) élaborer une Étude d’Impact Environnemental et Social (EIES) du Plan Local d’Urbanisme (PLU) et Plan Particulier d’Aménagement (PPA) de la Ville de Kananga . 3. L’Unité de Gestion du Projet PURUK invite, par le présent avis d’appel à manifestation d’intérêt, des candidats firme éligibles à manifester leur intérêt à fournir les services décrits ci-dessus. Les Candidats intéressés doivent fournir les informations démontrant qu’ils possèdent les qualifications et l’expérience pertinente requises pour exécuter la mission. 4. Les critères pour l’établissement de la liste restreinte sont : (i) le consultant doit être une société, un cabinet ou un bureau d’études spécialisé dans les évaluations environnementales et sociales, (ii) disposer d’au moins dix (10) ans d’expérience dans les études environnementales et sociales, (iii) il (elle) doit prouver document à l’appui qu’il (elle) a déjà réalisé, seul ou en tant que chef de fil d’un groupement, au cours de sept (7) dernières années (2019-2026), au moins deux (2) missions similaires (EESS) de programmes ou stratégies de développement urbain et au minimum trois (3) EIES de projets financés par les partenaires techniques et financiers. Une expérience en RDC sera très fortement valorisée. 5. La durée de la mission est de cent (100) jours. 6. L’attention des consultants intéressés est attirée sur la Section III, paragraphes 3.14, 3.16 et 3.17 des règlements de passation des marchés pour les emprunteurs sollicitant le financement de projets d’investissement (FPI), cinquième édition, septembre 2023, qui énoncent la politique de la Banque mondiale en matière de conflits d’intérêts. 7. Un consultant sera sélectionné selon la méthode de Sélection Fondée sur la Qualité et le Coût telle que décrite à la Section VII, paragraphe 7.3 du règlement de passation des marchés pour les emprunteurs sollicitant le financement de projets d’investissement (FPI), cinquième édition, septembre 2025. Les consultants peuvent s’associer avec d’autres firmes pour améliorer leurs qualifications mais ils doivent indiquer clairement si l’association prend la forme d’un groupement et ou d’une sous-traitance 8. Les candidats intéressés peuvent obtenir des informations supplémentaires (les termes de références) à l’adresse ci-dessous de 9 heures à 16 heures locales et sur le site Media Congo. 9. Les manifestations d’intérêt, écrites en langue française doivent être déposées à l’adresse ci-dessous en personne, par courrier, accompagné d’une version électronique en format Word ou PDF copiable sur une clé USD ou envoyé par courrier électronique en format PDF copiable aux adresses : ugpuruk@gmail.com, jeanmichelmbungu@gmail.com et spm.puruk.cosmos@gmail.com au plus tard le 25 Juin 2026 à 00h00', Heure locale de Kananga (TU+2), et porter clairement la mention : AMI N° : ZR-PURUK-543648-CS-QCBS – Recrutement d’un consultant cabinet ou firme en charge de l’évaluation environnementale et sociale stratégique (EESS) du Schéma Directeur d’Assainissement et Drainage (SDAD) et l’Étude d’impact Environnemental et Social (EIES) du Plan Local d’Urbanisation (PLU) et Plan Particulier d’Aménagement (PPA) dans la Ville de Kananga en République Démocratique du Congo. L’adresse est l’Unité de Gestion du Projet d’Urgence et de Résilience Urbaine de Kananga « UG-PURUK », A attention de : Monsieur Jean Michel MBUNGU NGUMBA, Coordonnateur ai. 601, Avenue Gécamines, Quartier Malandji, Commune de Kananga, Ville de Kananga, Province du Kasaï Central, République Démocratique du Congo (RDC), Téléphone : +243 992905752 / +243 823 041 704. Fait à Kananga, le 11 juin 2026 MBUNGU NGUMBA Jean Michel Coordonnateur ai de l’UG-PURUK

For this contract, the Borrower shall process the payments using the Direct Payment disbursement method, as defined in the World Bank’s Disbursement Guidelines for Investment Project Financing The implementing agency, Unidade de Gestão de Projectos Especiais (UGPE), now invites sealed Bids from eligible Bidders for Works of rehabilitation of the quay and surrounding adjacent areas, including upgrades and support works for Tarrafal Beach. notice_text: KINGDOM OF CAMBODIA Nation Religion King   MINISTRY OF PUBUC WORKS AND TRANSPORT (MPWT) Project Management Unit   Cambodia Regional Connectivity Improvement Project Phase 1 ( CRCI) Project No.: P510547 IDA Credit No.: 8012-KH & 8013-KH   REQUEST FOR THE EXPRESSION OF INTEREST International Individual Consultant (Intermittent) Strengthening the Internal Audit Capacity of the Ministry of Public Works and Transport Cambodia Regional Connectivity Improvement Project Phase 1   The Ministry of Public Works and Transport (MPWT) of the Royal Government of Cambodia (RGC) has applied for financing support from the World Bank's (WB) International Development Association (IDA) to implement the Cambodia Regional Connectivity Improvement Project (CRCI) with and duration of six (6.5) years starting in early 2027. The CRCI consists of the following 4 components: Component 1: Road Corridor Improvement Component 2: Institutional Capacity Strengthening in Logistics and Trade Facilitation Component 3: Phase 1 Project Management and Phase 2 Preparation Component 4: Contingent Emergency Response   MPWT is responsible for overall technical supervision, execution and management of the Project.   The CRCI seeks to enhance transport connectivity along Cambodia's segment of Asian Highway 21 (AH21), a key east-west corridor linking Cambodia and Viet Nam. Upgrading this section will promote economic growth in Cambodia's northeastern provinces and strengthen trade relations with neighboring countries. The project aims to improve community road access to essential services, including health centers, referral hospitals, schools, and markets, by upgrading climate-resilient national roads. Additionally, it will lower transportation costs and mitigate risks of road disruptions, thereby supporting the efficiency of agricultural supply chains and promoting tourism development within the project area. The CRCI will use the Output and Performance Based Road Contract (OPBRC) approach to support upgrade, climate resilience, safety, and maintenance for parts of NR 64, NR 62, all of NR 9, sections of NR 7 and NR 78.   Objective of the Assignment: The objective of this consultant assignment is to support MPWT to strengthen its internal audit capacity for establishing and operationalizing a sustainable, risk-based internal audit function in MPWT that delivers: Risk-based audit programs and execution, focusing on high-risk areas of CRCIP Practical audit tools and manuals, aligned with GDIA and IIA standards Staff training to enhance detection and reporting of fraud and integrity risks, including red flag identification. Support improving internal regulations for Improved quality and consistency of internal audit outputs, supported by basic quality assurance mechanisms.   Consultant Profile and Qualifications: The selected Individual Consultant should meet the selection criteria set out below: Advanced degree in Accounting, Auditing, Finance, Economics, or related field with 15 years of general experience. Professional certification such as Certified Internal Auditor (CIA), CPA, ACCA, or equivalent is strongly preferred. Minimum 10 years of relevant international experience in internal audit, financial management, or related assurance functions, preferably in the public sector. Demonstrated experience with min. 3 projects in building internal audit capacity in government institutions, including developing audit manuals/SOPs and delivering training/coaching. Strong knowledge and hands-on application at least 5 years of international internal audit standards and good practices (IIA/IPPF), including risk-based internal audit planning and QAIP. Experience at least 3 projects with externally financed projects (e.g., World Bank, ADB or other development partners) and familiarity with financial management and procurement risk areas in donor-funded operations is an advantage. Strong analytical, communication, report writing, and stakeholder engagement skills, and ability to work effectively with government counterparts. Ability to work in hybrid mode (on-site and remote) and deliver outputs within agreed timelines.   The RGC, through the Ministry of Public Works and Transport (MPWT) and its Project Management Unit (PMU), is seeking to engage one (1) qualified International Individual Consultant to support the PMU-CRCI during the project preparation phase 1. KINGDOM OF CAMBODIA

Nation Religion King

 

MINISTRY OF PUBUC WORKS AND TRANSPORT (MPWT)

Project Management Unit

 

Cambodia Regional Connectivity Improvement Project Phase 1 (CRCI)

Project No.: P510547

IDA Credit No.: 8012-KH & 8013-KH

 

REQUEST FOR THE EXPRESSION OF INTEREST

International Individual Consultant (Intermittent)

Strengthening the Internal Audit Capacity of the Ministry of Public Works and Transport

Cambodia Regional Connectivity Improvement Project Phase 1

 

The Ministry of Public Works and Transport (MPWT) of the Royal Government of Cambodia (RGC) has applied for financing support from the World Bank's (WB) International Development Association (IDA) to implement the Cambodia Regional Connectivity Improvement Project (CRCI) with and duration of six (6.5) years starting in early 2027. The CRCI consists of the following 4 components:

Component 1: Road Corridor Improvement

Component 2: Institutional Capacity Strengthening in Logistics and Trade Facilitation

Component 3: Phase 1 Project Management and Phase 2 Preparation

Component 4: Contingent Emergency Response

 

MPWT is responsible for overall technical supervision, execution and management of the Project.

 

The CRCI seeks to enhance transport connectivity along Cambodia's segment of Asian Highway 21 (AH21), a key east-west corridor linking Cambodia and Viet Nam. Upgrading this section will promote economic growth in Cambodia's northeastern provinces and strengthen trade relations with neighboring countries. The project aims to improve community road access to essential services, including health centers, referral hospitals, schools, and markets, by upgrading climate-resilient national roads. Additionally, it will lower transportation costs and mitigate risks of road disruptions, thereby supporting the efficiency of agricultural supply chains and promoting tourism development within the project area. The CRCI will use the Output and Performance Based Road Contract (OPBRC) approach to support upgrade, climate resilience, safety, and maintenance for parts of NR 64, NR 62, all of NR 9, sections of NR 7 and NR 78.

 

Objective of the Assignment:

The objective of this consultant assignment is to support MPWT to strengthen its internal audit capacity for establishing and operationalizing a sustainable, risk-based internal audit function in MPWT that delivers:

  1. Risk-based audit programs and execution, focusing on high-risk areas of CRCIP
  2. Practical audit tools and manuals, aligned with GDIA and IIA standards
  3. Staff training to enhance detection and reporting of fraud and integrity risks, including red flag identification.
  4. Support improving internal regulations for Improved quality and consistency of internal audit outputs, supported by basic quality assurance mechanisms.

 

Consultant Profile and Qualifications:

The selected Individual Consultant should meet the selection criteria set out below:

  • Advanced degree in Accounting, Auditing, Finance, Economics, or related field with 15 years of general experience. Professional certification such as Certified Internal Auditor (CIA), CPA, ACCA, or equivalent is strongly preferred.
  • Minimum 10 years of relevant international experience in internal audit, financial management, or related assurance functions, preferably in the public sector.
  • Demonstrated experience with min. 3 projects in building internal audit capacity in government institutions, including developing audit manuals/SOPs and delivering training/coaching.
  • Strong knowledge and hands-on application at least 5 years of international internal audit standards and good practices (IIA/IPPF), including risk-based internal audit planning and QAIP.
  • Experience at least 3 projects with externally financed projects (e.g., World Bank, ADB or other development partners) and familiarity with financial management and procurement risk areas in donor-funded operations is an advantage.
  • Strong analytical, communication, report writing, and stakeholder engagement skills, and ability to work effectively with government counterparts.
  • Ability to work in hybrid mode (on-site and remote) and deliver outputs within agreed timelines.

 

The RGC, through the Ministry of Public Works and Transport (MPWT) and its Project Management Unit (PMU), is seeking to engage one (1) qualified International Individual Consultant to support the PMU-CRCI during the project preparation phase 1. notice_text: REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)     Kazakhstan Transport Resilience and Connectivity Enhancement Project (P500565) Jezkazgan–Karagandy Section of Trans–Caspian International Transport Route (Middle Corridor)   Loan No.: IBRD-97350 Assignment Title: Construction Supervision Consultant for the Jezkazgan–Karagandy Road Section under OPBRC Contracts Reference No . (as per Procurement Plan): KZ-KAZAUTOZHOL-562877-CS-QCBS   The JSC “NC “KazAvtoZhol” has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Transport Resilience and Connectivity Enhancement Project (P500565) Jezkazgan–Karagandy Section of Trans–Caspian International Transport Route (Middle Corridor) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.   The assignment covers the provision of Construction Supervision Consultant (CSC) services for the rehabilitation and long-term performance-based maintenance of approximately 457 km of the Jezkazgan–Karagandy road section, forming part of the Trans-Caspian International Transport Route (Middle Corridor). The road works are structured under four Output- and Performance-Based Road Contracts (OPBRC) following the World Bank's applicable Standard Procurement Documents for OPBRC. Works are being carried out under four separate OPBRC contracts, all of which have been signed in July 2026 and are currently under implementation, as follows:   Lot 1 km 783 – km 905 122 km Lot 2 km 683 – km 783 100 km Lot 3 km 583 – km 683 100 km Lot 4 km 448 – km 583 135 km Total   457 km   The CSC will be responsible for supervising all four lots under a single contract with KazAvtoZhol, following the World Bank's applicable Standard Procurement Documents for OPBRC. The CSC's responsibilities include review of contractor designs, supervision of civil works during the construction, contract administration, and reporting. The assignment also encompasses environmental and social supervision obligations under the World Bank's Environmental and Social Framework (ESF), including monitoring of resettlement, biodiversity impacts (including saiga antelope migration corridors), and implementation of the project's Sexual Exploitation and Abuse/Sexual Harassment (SEA/SH) prevention measures. The total estimated input is 473 person-months across 9 Key Expert and 13 Non-Key Expert positions The initial duration of this time-based contract is expected to be approximately 24 months.  The extension and expansion of the services may be considered subject to the Consultant’s satisfactory performance.   The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment is attached to this request for expressions of interest.   JSC NC KazAvtoZhol invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to express their interest in providing the above-mentioned services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Assignment. The main criteria for shortlisting Consultants are as follows: 1. Experience in Supervision of Road Construction Experience in completed contracts under which the firm acted as the lead supervision consultant for road works involving road sections of at least 30 km each. Such contracts must have been completed within the last fifteen (15) years. 2. Experience with OPBRC / DB (Design-Build) / DBO (Design-Build-Operate) / PBM (Performance-Based Maintenance) / EPC (Engineering, Procurement and Construction) / PBC (Performance-Based Contract) Contracts and International Financial Institution-Financed Projects At least one (1) completed or substantially advanced assignment involving the supervision or administration of an OPBRC, DB (Design-Build), DBO (Design-Build-Operate), PBM (Performance-Based Maintenance), EPC (Engineering, Procurement and Construction), PBC (Performance-Based Contract), or similar type of contract; or experience in at least two (2) contracts financed by multilateral development banks, such as the World Bank, the Asian Development Bank (ADB), the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD), or the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB), completed within the last ten (10) years. 3. Geographic Experience Demonstrated experience in supervising road works in Kazakhstan or region with similar geographic and climatic conditions within the last ten (10) years, however experience in Kazakhstan is an advantage. Key Experts will be evaluated at the Technical Proposal submission stage. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.15, and 3.16 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” 7th Edition, September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.  In addition, please refer to the following specific information on conflict of interest related to this assignment: any firm (or its affiliate) that participated in the preparation of the OPBRC works contractor bidding documents, the feasibility study, or the detailed design for this road section shall not be eligible to apply, as this would constitute a conflict of interest under paragraphs 3.15–3.16 of the Procurement Regulations.     Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.   A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality And Cost-Based Selection method set out in the Procurement Regulations. The Terms of Reference could be downloadaed following the link: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1aiw0Lnn6iT1IAsOIobF5XTpYeRMxKlq1/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=111479035887858857771&rtpof=true&sd=true  Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours Address: Syganak 60/4, Astana city, Kazakhstan 6th floor Office JSC “NC “KazAvtoZhol” City: Astana , From 09:00 to 1700   Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person, or by mail, or by fax, or by e-mail) by October 30, 2026   Attention: Sagi Sadykuly, Managing Director for Revenue Address: Syganak 60/4, Astana city, Kazakhstan 6th floor Office JSC “NC “KazAvtoZhol” City: Astana Country: Kazakhstan Electronic mail address: qajchief.engineer@gmail.com

The road works are structured under four Output- and Performance-Based Road Contracts (OPBRC) following the World Bank's applicable Standard Procurement Documents for OPBRC. Works are being carried out under four separate OPBRC contracts, all of which have been signed in July 2026 and are currently under implementation, as follows:

 

Lot 1

km 783 – km 905

122 km

Lot 2

km 683 – km 783

100 km

Lot 3

km 583 – km 683

100 km

Lot 4

km 448 – km 583

135 km

Total

 

457 km

 

The CSC will be responsible for supervising all four lots under a single contract with KazAvtoZhol, following the World Bank's applicable Standard Procurement Documents for OPBRC. The CSC's responsibilities include review of contractor designs, supervision of civil works during the construction, contract administration, and reporting. The assignment also encompasses environmental and social supervision obligations under the World Bank's Environmental and Social Framework (ESF), including monitoring of resettlement, biodiversity impacts (including saiga antelope migration corridors), and implementation of the project's Sexual Exploitation and Abuse/Sexual Harassment (SEA/SH) prevention measures. The total estimated input is 473 person-months across 9 Key Expert and 13 Non-Key Expert positions

The initial duration of this time-based contract is expected to be approximately 24 months.  The extension and expansion of the services may be considered subject to the Consultant’s satisfactory performance.

 

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment is attached to this request for expressions of interest.

 

JSC NC KazAvtoZhol invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to express their interest in providing the above-mentioned services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Assignment. The main criteria for shortlisting Consultants are as follows:

1. Experience in Supervision of Road Construction

Experience in completed contracts under which the firm acted as the lead supervision consultant for road works involving road sections of at least 30 km each. Such contracts must have been completed within the last fifteen (15) years.

2. Experience with OPBRC / DB (Design-Build) / DBO (Design-Build-Operate) / PBM (Performance-Based Maintenance) / EPC (Engineering, Procurement and Construction) / PBC (Performance-Based Contract) Contracts and International Financial Institution-Financed Projects

At least one (1) completed or substantially advanced assignment involving the supervision or administration of an OPBRC, DB (Design-Build), DBO (Design-Build-Operate), PBM (Performance-Based Maintenance), EPC (Engineering, Procurement and Construction), PBC (Performance-Based Contract), or similar type of contract; or experience in at least two (2) contracts financed by multilateral development banks, such as the World Bank, the Asian Development Bank (ADB), the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD), or the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB), completed within the last ten (10) years.

3. Geographic Experience

Demonstrated experience in supervising road works in Kazakhstan or region with similar geographic and climatic conditions within the last ten (10) years, however experience in Kazakhstan is an advantage.

Key Experts will be evaluated at the Technical Proposal submission stage.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.15, and 3.16 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” 7th Edition, September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.  In addition, please refer to the following specific information on conflict of interest related to this assignment: any firm (or its affiliate) that participated in the preparation of the OPBRC works contractor bidding documents, the feasibility study, or the detailed design for this road section shall not be eligible to apply, as this would constitute a conflict of interest under paragraphs 3.15–3.16 of the Procurement Regulations.

   

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

 

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality And Cost-Based Selection method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

notice_text:     Renewable Energy Generation and Access INcrease Project (REGAIN) (P181250) Marshall Islands   Request for Expressions of Interest Consulting Services for Implementation Plan for Renewable Energy, Energy Efficiency and E-Mobility under the Energy Act 2025     Grant No.: E331-MH REGAIN Project Reference No. MH-MEC-572983-CS-CQS   October 21, 2026     The Government of the Republic of the Marshall Islands (GRMI) has received financing from the International Development Association (IDA) (the “Bank”) in the form of a grant (hereinafter called “the Grant”), in the amount of US$60 million, toward the cost of the Renewable Energy Generation and Access Increase (REGAIN) Project (P181250), approved and effective as of December 13, 2024, with a closing date of September 30, 2030. The Marshalls Energy Company (MEC), as Employer and implementing agency, intends to apply a portion of the proceeds of the Grant to eligible payments under a contract for consulting services to prepare and support an implementation plan for renewable energy, energy efficiency and e-mobility under the Energy Act, 2025 and the National Energy Authority Act, 2025, excluding petroleum-sector provisions, under Sub-Component 3.1 (Sector Development Assistance) of the REGAIN Project. The assignment shall be carried out in close coordination with the newly established National Energy Authority (NEA) and shall cover all MEC-served systems, including Majuro, Ebeye and the outer islands. The consulting services (“the Services”) comprise proposing activities to be undertaken in the short, medium, and long term and undertaking them to strengthen the capacity of key energy sector stakeholders by focusing on regulation, target setting, monitoring tools, dissemination of progress, feedback, and course correction to promote security, safety, reliability, and sustainability of energy supply (excluding petroleum) in RMI as per the provisions of the EA 2025 and aligned with the National Energy Authority Act, 2025.  Services include, among others: Diagnostic review of the Electricity Sector (in particular RE, EE and E-Mobility) of the Marshall Islands; Strategic review of the applicable RMI’s electricity sector-related international and national commitments and targets; Propose a strategy for addressing the identified gaps; Assessing the Institutional structure and the manpower requirements of the Energy sector; Monitoring, Database and Reporting Framework for RE; Electricity tariff review and recommendations, building on MEC’s existing tariff methodology and extending it to Ebeye; and Addressing the recommendations by preparing, revising, or aligning the policies, regulations, codes, guidelines, and other instruments required to give effect to the relevant provisions of the Energy Act, 2025 and the National Energy Authority Act, 2025, excluding petroleum-sector provisions. The assignment is structured as a lump-sum contract with an estimated duration of 9 months, with an expected start date in January 2027. The selected firm will nominate a multidisciplinary team, including the Key Experts described in the attached TOR, and will report to MEC, coordinating closely with NEA, the World Bank, and other relevant stakeholders. The Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment are attached to this Request for Expressions of Interest. MEC now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.   The shortlisting criteria, as set out in Section 10 of the attached TOR, are: Experience preparing energy-sector legal, policy and regulatory frameworks, or implementation plans for energy legislation, including regulations, codes and licensing (35 points) Experience in electricity tariff, cost-of-service and revenue-requirement studies for small island or multi-system utilities, preferably with high renewable energy penetration (25 points) Experience in the Pacific or other Small Island Developing States (25 points) Technical and managerial capability of the firm, including core business, years in business, organization and availability of relevant expertise (15 points) The Consultant shall demonstrate availability of qualified experts in energy policy and regulation (renewable energy, energy efficiency and e-mobility), legal and regulatory drafting, electricity tariffs and utility finance, and stakeholder engagement. Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.   The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.  In addition, please refer to the following specific information on conflict of interest related to this assignment:   Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all partners shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.   A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Selection based on Consultant’s Qualifications (CQS) method set out in the World Bank Regulations for IPF-Borrowers, September 2025    Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours, 0900 to 1700 hours, Monday to Friday.   Expressions of Interest EOI must be delivered in electronic form to the address below perferably by November 23, 2026, 5:00 pm Majuro time.   MEC: Attn: Steve Wakefield PO Box 1439, Majuro MH 96960 Republic of the Marshall Islands Tel: 692-625-3827/3829 E-mail: swakefield@mecrmi.com   Copy: Jack Chong-Gum, jack.chonggum@mecrmi.net   EOI Submission Requirements: Expressions of Interest should include the following information: Firm profile Organizational Capacity Relevant assignments (maximum 10 projects), preferably including energy-sector regulatory, energy legislation implementation or tariff assignments in small island states. Information addressing each of the shortlisting criteria Company registration documents   Page Limit: Maximum 15 pages excluding registration documents. Submissions beyond the maximum page limit of 15 pages will not be considered.   Yours sincerely,   Jack Chong-Gum CEO , Marshalls Energy Company jack.chonggum@mecrmi.net       Republic of the Marshall Islands Marshalls Energy Company (MEC) Terms of Reference (TOR) Implementation Plan for Renewable Energy, Energy Efficiency and E-Mobility under the Energy Act, 2025 and National Energy Authority Act, 2025, excluding Petroleum Provisions – REGAIN Project Project ID: P181250 Assignment Type: International Firm (Lump sum Contract) Duration: 9 Months Location: Remote with Periodic Missions to Majuro 1. Background The Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI) is one of the world's smallest and most isolated nations. The country consists of 29 atolls and 5 low coral islands situated on about 181 square kilometers (km2) of land mass in the Pacific Ocean. Majuro (the nation's capital) and Ebeye, the country's two largest urban centers, account for about 96 percent of the total population, while the remaining inhabitants live on the outer atolls. The Government of the Republic of the Marshall Islands (GRMI) depends mostly on diesel generation to meet the country's growing electricity needs. The country aims to enhance its energy security through renewable energy generation, improve the reliability of electricity supply, enhance energy efficiency, expand e-mobility, and improve access to electricity. Increased energy resilience will reduce dependence on hydrocarbon fuels, insulate the country from the risks of price rises and supply uncertainties, and equip it with natural disaster-resilient electricity infrastructure.   MEC, the state-owned energy utility, generates and provides electricity to Majuro Atoll, serving 55 percent of RMI's population. MEC also manages three mini-grids in Jaluit, Wotje, Rongrong (Majuro Atoll), and Kili Island, the latter having been recently transferred to MEC from the Kili Bikini Ejit (KBE) Local Government. Following the integration of the Kwajalein Atoll Joint Utilities Resources (KAJUR) into MEC, MEC is also responsible for power generation and distribution in Ebeye, together with the water and sewerage services previously provided by KAJUR. MEC is responsible for executing plans to enhance energy security but lacks the capability to conceive and implement them. It lacks the funds required to implement these plans. The Government of the Republic of the Marshall Islands (GRMI) has partnered with the World Bank through the Renewable Energy Generation and Access Increase Project (REGAIN) – an IDA grant of US$60 million approved and effective as of December 13, 2024, with a closing date of September 30, 2030. The REGAIN project aims to increase renewable energy generation and improve access to electricity while reducing reliance on diesel-based generation through funding and technical support.   RMI’s Electricity Roadmap targets net-zero greenhouse gas emissions and 100% renewable electricity by 2050. As a small and geographically dispersed island nation, RMI remains highly dependent on imported diesel for electricity generation, exposing the country to high energy costs and vulnerability to global fuel price shocks and supply disruptions. To manage this risk, RMI needs to diversify its electricity supply portfolio by integrating more RE, manage demand growth by promoting efficient electricity use, pursue new business opportunities such as EVs, and monitor and report implementation status to the GRMI for appropriate course correction. Ensuring a reliable, clean, and cost-effective electricity supply is therefore critical to achieving national climate commitments, strengthening energy security, and supporting sustainable socio-economic development. The country lacks the legal, policy, and regulatory framework, institutional capability, and the trained manpower required to achieve these objectives. The GRMI has taken some steps in this direction, such as the notification of the Energy Act 2025, which provides a legal, policy, regulatory, and organizational framework to promote security, safety, reliability, and sustainability of energy supply for the benefit of RMI’s economy and citizens and to promote the efficient use of energy and of energy from indigenous sources.   Under Sub-Component 3.1 of the REGAIN project (Sector Development Assistance), MEC plans to seek consultancy support from a firm to propose a roadmap and undertake proposed activities for the Implementation of the Energy Act (IEA) 2025.  In the roadmap, IEA shall propose activities to be undertaken in the short, medium, and long term and undertake them to strengthen the capacity of key energy sector stakeholders by focusing on regulation, target setting, monitoring tools, dissemination of progress, feedback, and course correction to promote security, safety, reliability, and sustainability of energy supply in RMI.   IEA shall be prepared in close coordination with the newly established National Energy Authority (NEA) and MEC.   IEA shall take into account all Acts, policies, regulations, studies and current practices relevant to electricity (all RE included), Energy Efficiency, E-mobility and their funding, including but not limited to:   Energy Act 2025 National Energy Authority Act, 2025 Recommendations contained in Integrated Resource and Resilience Plan 2024-2034 Electricity Roadmap of 2018, which provides a relevant and guiding framework for the sector’s development MEC’s current tariff methodology and tariff model, prepared by MEC’s Supplemental Management and Operations (SMO) consultant under ADB-funded technical assistance, which covers MEC’s operations prior to the integration of KAJUR and on which the tariff review under Task 6 shall build National Targets and the progress achieved against them to date Relevant energy sector programs and studies of other development partners active in the RMI, in particular the Asian Development Bank (ADB), such as the Energy Transition Project, should be taken into account to ensure coordination and avoid duplication.   The assignment will support GRMI, MEC, and NEA in translating the Energy Act, 2025, and the National Energy Authority Act, 2025, into an actionable implementation plan for renewable energy, energy efficiency, and e-mobility. The assignment will identify required policy, regulatory, institutional, monitoring, and capacity-building actions, while excluding provisions related to the petroleum sector. This support aligns with REGAIN’s institutional strengthening objectives and RMI’s need to reduce reliance on diesel, improve energy security, and support the integration of renewable energy. 2. Objectives The objective of the assignment is to prepare a practical, time-bound implementation plan for renewable energy, energy efficiency, and e-mobility under the Energy Act, 2025, and the National Energy Authority Act, 2025, excluding petroleum-sector provisions, and to support the preparation of priority policy, regulatory, institutional, monitoring, and capacity-building instruments required for implementation.   Institutional strengthening for the implementation of RE, EE, and e-mobility provisions. Policy and regulatory framework, guidelines for the development of higher RE integration, EE promotion, and e-mobility uptake. Monitoring and reporting framework for RE, EE, and e-mobility targets, progress, and implementation gaps. Database/reporting arrangements for RE, EE, and e-mobility information. Capacity development strategy for institutions, utilities, and local manpower. 3. Project Description This assignment is financed by the World Bank under the institutional strengthening and implementation support activities of REGAIN. It will support the policy, regulatory, institutional, monitoring, and capacity-building measures required to implement the RE, EE, and E-mobility provisions of the Energy Act, 2025, and the National Energy Authority Act, 2025. 4. Implementation Arrangements  MEC will be the Employer and the contracting authority for this assignment, responsible for approving deliverables and payments. The Consultant may proceed to the next deliverable under MEC's general guidance. NEA, as the statutory authority responsible for regulating the energy sector, shall be responsible for the technical and regulatory approval of policy- and regulation-driven deliverables. MEC, as Employer, retains ultimate authority for administrative and financial approval and for the release of REGAIN project funds, which shall follow NEA's technical sign-off on the relevant deliverable. The responsible ministry and Cabinet shall be consulted where recommendations require policy approval, regulatory adoption, statutory action, budget allocation, or cross-government implementation. MEC shall be responsible for formal approval of all deliverables and payments. The Consultant shall work under the direction of MEC and coordinate closely with:   MEC management and technical staff REGAIN Project Management Services Consultant, as applicable Project Implementation Unit (PMU) within MEC NEA, the national regulatory body, serving as the regulatory interface between MEC and the Consultant Responsible Ministry and Cabinet on policy formulation World Bank on matters requiring no-objection, reporting, or implementation support ADB and other development partners active in RMI's energy sector, as relevant Petroleum-sector implementation matters are excluded from this assignment. 5. Scope of Services The scope of services is limited to the electricity sector, in particular renewable energy, energy efficiency, and e-mobility, including relevant non-petroleum legal, policy, regulatory, institutional, monitoring, enforcement, data, and capacity-building provisions necessary for their implementation. Petroleum sector related provisions of the Energy Act, 2025, are excluded from the assignment. While MEC is the Contracting Employer for the entire assignment, NEA serves as the primary technical Client for Tasks 1, 2, 3, and 7, given their statutory and regulatory content. MEC's approval of these deliverables is administrative and financial and follows NEA's technical acceptance.   Task 1: Diagnostic review of the Electricity Sector (in particular RE, EE and E-Mobility) of the Marshall Islands The Consultant shall review and map the existing institutional arrangement, policy, and regulatory framework against the provisions and the directions contained in the Energy Act (EA) 2025 and the National Energy Authority (NEA) Act 2025 (harmonious reading) for the development of Renewable Energy (RE), Energy Efficiency (EE), and E-Mobility (E-MB). The Consultant will propose a strategy to address misaligned or missing institutional arrangements, policies, and regulatory framework. Review of existing applicable  policies, strategies, plans, and studies in the context of the requirements of EA 2025 and NEA Act 2025, Identify whether the gap is institutional, policy, or regulatory, whether it will be addressed within the existing framework (alignment/modification), or whether a new framework is to be created, and Recommend a broad policy, regulatory, and Institutional framework to address these gaps.   Task 2: Strategic review of the applicable RMI’s electricity sector related international and national commitments and targets The Consultant will undertake a focused review of the GRMI's international commitments, national targets, initiatives for the development of RE, EE, and E-MB, and the progress achieved. The diagnostic and strategic review will include the following: Discussion with the stakeholders and ascertaining reasons for the shortfall in the envisaged progress, The Consultant shall review relevant national targets, international commitments, ongoing initiatives, and selected comparable Pacific/SIDS practices for RE, EE, and e-mobility implementation. The purpose of the review shall be to identify practical options for policy, regulatory, institutional, monitoring, and capacity-building measures suitable for RMI, Identification of implementation gaps, in particular critical legal, policy, regulatory, and institutional gaps, which impacted the achievements of these initiatives and targets, Assess whether these legal, policy, and regulatory gaps stem from implementation shortfall or a missing framework, and Recommend a broad policy, regulatory, and institutional framework to address these gaps.   Task 3: Propose a strategy for addressing the identified gaps  The Consultant will propose a strategy with a time-bound implementation roadmap for addressing the gaps identified in Tasks 1 and 2. The proposed strategy will include the following: Identification of Implementation gaps, i.e., the framework/provision exists but has not been implemented, or there is a shortfall in its implementation, Identification of gaps in the existing framework, i.e., the legal, policy, regulatory, or Institutional framework provides for the enabling provision, but it has not been enacted or notified; indicate whether it is a policy, regulatory, or institutional issue, Identify misalignment (even a section or provision of it) of the policy, regulatory framework, or the institutional framework with the EA 2025 and NEA 2025, Identification of gaps that cannot be dealt with by the existing framework, Recommendation of a strategy to deal with these identified gaps. The proposed strategy will indicate the required interventions (legal, policy, regulatory and institutional), their implementation order, the stakeholders responsible for addressing them and the timelines within which these will be addressed (short term- within 3 months, medium term- within 6 months and long term-within 12 months) duly aligned with the statutory timelines provided in the Acts and related policies, Indicate how the recommended interventions will address the identified gaps. Indicate the way forward for the gaps which cannot be addressed under the existing legal framework, and Develop a comprehensive implementation roadmap considering the recommendations made in Task 2 and in this Task, and compile the recommendations.   The roadmap should indicate: Short-term actions, Medium-term actions, Long-term actions, Responsible institution, Required decision or instrument, Dependency, Level of priority, and Whether the consultant will draft the instrument under this assignment. Task 4: Assessing the Institutional structure and the manpower requirements of the sector The Consultant will examine whether the current institutional structure, including its roles and responsibilities, aligns with those prescribed in the Energy Act and is conducive to the development of RE, EE, and E-MB in RMI. The Consultant will examine the following: Clarity in their role and responsibilities (without any overlap) for the development of RE, EE, and E-MB, The institutional capacity to lead the development of RE, EE, and E-MB in RMI, such as project planning, design, implementation, operation, and maintenance, and Recommendations for addressing institutional alignment of roles and responsibilities, capacity gaps, and the coordination mechanism between them for the development of RE, EE, and E-MB, taking into account the integration of KAJUR’s operations into MEC.   The Consultant will also assess the skills and the manpower required for the development of RE, EE, and E-MB in RMI. The Consultant shall assess: Manpower and the skills available with all important stakeholders, Assess the manpower and the skill requirements considering the national targets and the evolving (proposed Roadmap) legal, policy, regulatory and institutional framework for the development of RE, EE and E-MB for the next 5 years, Indicate the gaps between availability and requirements, and Prepare a strategy to meet this gap, indicating the number, the skill requirements, and how the required skills will be met (contents of the training, how and where the training will be provided, suggestions for international collaboration, certification).       Task 5: Monitoring, Database and Reporting Framework for RE The Consultant will assess the status of the RE database to determine its suitability for publishing a report that records, documents, and shares critical information on RE, EE, and E-MB. The Consultant will: Evaluate the existing database and identify the missing indicators/information gap/data field necessary for various stakeholders to discharge their roles and responsibilities for the development of RE, EE, and E-MB in the country (covering Majuro, Ebeye and the outer island systems), Recommend formats, information to be gathered, sources of this information, reporting institutions, reporting frequency, and validation process, Recommend the structure of the report to be published, and Prepare the first RE encompassing the above recommendations, which NEA can subsequently update and improve upon.   Task 6: Electricity tariff review and recommendations The tariff review shall build on, and not duplicate, MEC’s current tariff methodology and tariff model prepared by the SMO consultant. It shall focus on how that methodology has performed in practice, on areas it did not examine in depth, and on extending it to all systems now operated by MEC, including Ebeye following the integration of KAJUR’s operations into MEC, which was not covered by the earlier work. The review shall also provide MEC and NEA with a clear, evidence-based rationale and supporting calculations for the recommended tariff options, so that they are well prepared to respond to tariff proposals from policymakers, investors and other stakeholders.   The Consultant shall review the existing electricity tariff arrangements and prepare recommendations and an implementation pathway that are consistent with the Energy Act, 2025, and the National Energy Authority Act, 2025. The Consultant shall, in particular: Assess the adequacy of the current tariff level, structure, adjustment mechanisms, billing arrangements and related subsidy or compensation mechanisms; Assess the revenue requirement and efficient cost of electricity service, based on verified utility financial, operational and investment data; Determine the extent to which prevailing tariffs and practices align with the principles contemplated under the relevant sections of the Energy Act; Assess tariff implications of planned renewable energy, EE, E-mobility, battery storage, network, resilience and access investments; Recommend refinements to the existing tariff methodology, tariff structure, adjustment mechanism and regulatory review process that NEA can use in tariff determinations; Review the application of MEC’s current tariff methodology and identify any issues, anomalies or unintended outcomes that have emerged in practice and that may require adjustment; Extend the revenue-requirement and cost-of-supply analysis to Ebeye following the integration of KAJUR’s operations into MEC, including harmonization of KAJUR’s financial, operational and customer data with MEC’s, clear separation of electricity costs from water and sewerage costs, and options and a transition pathway for bringing Ebeye’s electricity tariff into MEC’s tariff framework; Assess the merits and implications of the planned introduction of a single tariff for all customer classes; Assess whether a uniform national tariff should be maintained across all MEC-served systems (Majuro, Ebeye and the outer islands), or whether location-specific tariffs or tariff adjustment factors are warranted, including the resulting cross-subsidies between locations; Using the known sizes and costs of the hybrid and mini-grid systems to be installed in the outer islands, estimate the indicative cost of supply and potential tariff for each location, and assess the implications of any proposal to reduce tariffs in locations with high renewable energy penetration; Assess the practicality, timing and customer impact of reducing or removing existing government subsidies, and the alternatives available; Assess the feasibility of time-of-use tariffs that reflect the different costs of daytime (predominantly solar) and nighttime (predominantly diesel) supply; Recommend tariffs and charging arrangements for electric vehicle charging; Assess feed-in tariff, net-metering and power purchase arrangements for privately owned renewable energy systems seeking to export to MEC’s grid, including pricing based on avoided cost, the grid integration, storage and backup costs borne by MEC, and the volume of such generation the grid can accommodate; Assess the implications of electricity supplied by third parties outside MEC’s networks, such as renewable energy systems at government or private facilities that supply neighboring communities, including the pricing basis and regulatory requirements for such supply, and how differences between their prices and cost-reflective MEC tariffs can be explained and managed; Assess distributional and affordability implications for customer classes, including vulnerable customers, and identify transparent options for any subsidy or compensation that may be required; and Provide practical inputs for preparation and future implementation of the National Electricity Tariff and Billing Code.   Task 7: Addressing the recommendations Based on the approved recommendations and implementation roadmap under Task 3, and working under the technical supervision of NEA, the Consultant shall identify, prepare, revise or align the policies, regulations, codes, guidelines and other instruments required to give effect to the relevant provisions of the Energy Act, 2025 and the National Energy Authority Act, 2025, excluding petroleum-sector provisions. The Consultant shall, in particular: Prepare or align the electricity-sector regulatory instruments identified as necessary under the Acts, including, as applicable, electricity licensing, electricity-sector regulation, Grid Code, service standards, universal service and subsidy-related mechanisms, Prepare or align the instruments required for renewable energy, including, as applicable, grid integration, renewable IPPs, community renewable-energy projects, rooftop installations and renewable microgrids, Prepare or align the instruments required for energy efficiency, including applicable standards, labeling requirements, air-conditioning and cooling energy-efficiency requirements, and other EE measures required to implement the applicable provisions of the Acts, Prepare or align the instruments required for e-mobility, including applicable requirements relating to charging infrastructure, technical standards, charging services, electricity supply and tariff arrangements, and other matters required to implement the applicable provisions of the Acts, and Propose the institutional framework and clearly define the roles and responsibilities of the relevant institutions for implementation.   6. In its proposal, the Consultant shall specify: Each proposed key personnel position, The name of the proposed expert, where available, Role and responsibilities, Minimum and actual qualifications and detailed relevant experience, Whether the input is international or national/local, Whether the input is home office or field-based, Estimated level of effort in person-days or person-months, and Anticipated timing of deployment and deployment location(s). Renewable Energy Generation and Access INcrease Project (REGAIN)

(P181250)

Marshall Islands

 

Request for Expressions of Interest

Consulting Services

for

Implementation Plan for Renewable Energy, Energy Efficiency and E-Mobility under the Energy Act 2025

 

 

Grant No.: E331-MH

REGAIN Project

Reference No. MH-MEC-572983-CS-CQS

 

October 21, 2026

 

 

The Government of the Republic of the Marshall Islands (GRMI) has received financing from the International Development Association (IDA) (the “Bank”) in the form of a grant (hereinafter called “the Grant”), in the amount of US$60 million, toward the cost of the Renewable Energy Generation and Access Increase (REGAIN) Project (P181250), approved and effective as of December 13, 2024, with a closing date of September 30, 2030.

The Marshalls Energy Company (MEC), as Employer and implementing agency, intends to apply a portion of the proceeds of the Grant to eligible payments under a contract for consulting services to prepare and support an implementation plan for renewable energy, energy efficiency and e-mobility under the Energy Act, 2025 and the National Energy Authority Act, 2025, excluding petroleum-sector provisions, under Sub-Component 3.1 (Sector Development Assistance) of the REGAIN Project. The assignment shall be carried out in close coordination with the newly established National Energy Authority (NEA) and shall cover all MEC-served systems, including Majuro, Ebeye and the outer islands.

The consulting services (“the Services”) comprise proposing activities to be undertaken in the short, medium, and long term and undertaking them to strengthen the capacity of key energy sector stakeholders by focusing on regulation, target setting, monitoring tools, dissemination of progress, feedback, and course correction to promote security, safety, reliability, and sustainability of energy supply (excluding petroleum) in RMI as per the provisions of the EA 2025 and aligned with the National Energy Authority Act, 2025.  Services include, among others:

  • Diagnostic review of the Electricity Sector (in particular RE, EE and E-Mobility) of the Marshall Islands;
  • Strategic review of the applicable RMI’s electricity sector-related international and national commitments and targets;
  • Propose a strategy for addressing the identified gaps;
  • Assessing the Institutional structure and the manpower requirements of the Energy sector;
  • Monitoring, Database and Reporting Framework for RE;
  • Electricity tariff review and recommendations, building on MEC’s existing tariff methodology and extending it to Ebeye; and
  • Addressing the recommendations by preparing, revising, or aligning the policies, regulations, codes, guidelines, and other instruments required to give effect to the relevant provisions of the Energy Act, 2025 and the National Energy Authority Act, 2025, excluding petroleum-sector provisions.

The assignment is structured as a lump-sum contract with an estimated duration of 9 months, with an expected start date in January 2027. The selected firm will nominate a multidisciplinary team, including the Key Experts described in the attached TOR, and will report to MEC, coordinating closely with NEA, the World Bank, and other relevant stakeholders.

The Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment are attached to this Request for Expressions of Interest.

MEC now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

 

The shortlisting criteria, as set out in Section 10 of the attached TOR, are:

  1. Experience preparing energy-sector legal, policy and regulatory frameworks, or implementation plans for energy legislation, including regulations, codes and licensing (35 points)
  2. Experience in electricity tariff, cost-of-service and revenue-requirement studies for small island or multi-system utilities, preferably with high renewable energy penetration (25 points)
  3. Experience in the Pacific or other Small Island Developing States (25 points)
  4. Technical and managerial capability of the firm, including core business, years in business, organization and availability of relevant expertise (15 points)

The Consultant shall demonstrate availability of qualified experts in energy policy and regulation (renewable energy, energy efficiency and e-mobility), legal and regulatory drafting, electricity tariffs and utility finance, and stakeholder engagement. Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.  In addition, please refer to the following specific information on conflict of interest related to this assignment:

In the case of a joint venture, all partners shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

 

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Selection based on Consultant’s Qualifications (CQS) method set out in the World Bank Regulations for IPF-Borrowers, September 2025
