REPUBLIC OF MOZAMBIQUE

MINISTRY OF FINANCE

PROGRAM FOR STRENGTHENING GOVERNANCE AND CITIZEN SERVICE DELIVERY

MozPROSPERA — P514896

 

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(Individual Consultants)

Technical Advisory to the Minister of Finance, Public Debt Management Reform, Development Partners’ Portfolio Monitoring and South-South Knowledge Sharing

 

Reference nr:  MZ-MF-569750-CS-INDV

Loan/Grant Number: IDA-E7400

 

1. The Government of Mozambique, through the Ministry of Finance (MF), with the support of the International Development Association (IDA) of the World Bank Group, is preparing the Program for Strengthening Governance and Citizen Service Delivery (MozProspera), an operation under the Program-for-Results (PforR) modality. The Ministry of Finance is the implementing agency.

2. As part of this initiative, the Government intends to apply a portion of the proceeds to the recruitment of consulting services provided by an individual consultant. The consulting services (“the Services”) will include, but are not limited to, the following activities as detailed in the Terms of Reference:

  •  Strategic technical advisory to the Minister of Finance;
  • Diagnostic and support to the public debt management reform roadmap;
  • Technical support to strengthen debt management and cash management practices;
  • Strengthening South-South cooperation and knowledge sharing;
  • Capacity building and knowledge transfer.

3. The selected consultant will be engaged under a time-based contract and remunerated at an all-inclusive daily fee rate for actual days worked and certified, whether performed remotely or in-country, up to a maximum of one hundred (100) working days. Reasonable travel and in-country subsistence expenses incurred in connection with missions to Maputo shall be reimbursed in accordance with the contract provisions. The contract shall have an initial duration of six (6) months from the date of signature and may be extended subject to satisfactory performance, Program requirements, and the availability of funds.

4. The attention of interested consultants is drawn to section III, paragraphs 3.15 and 3.16 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (Procurement in Investment Project Financing), Sixth Edition, February 2025, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

5. The Ministry of Finance, now invites eligible individual consultants to indicate their interest in providing the services. Interested consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the services in the form of a curriculum vitae. A consultant will be selected in accordance with the individual consultant selection method set out in the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (Procurement in Investment Project Financing), Sixth Edition, February 2025 that can be accessed via the World Bank website at www.world bank.org/ procurement.

6. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to the minimum qualification criteria for the consultancy are:

  • Master’s degree (minimum) in Economics, Public Finance, Finance, Accounting, or an equivalent field;
  • Minimum of twelve (12) years of demonstrated professional experience in public finance, of which at least eight (8) years in sovereign public debt management;
  • Prior experience in ministries of finance, debt management offices, central banks, or international financial institutions, including at senior or advisory level;
  • Demonstrated international experience: at least five (5) years of work in public debt management in countries other than the candidate’s country of nationality, including advisory assignments with governments of developing countries.
  • Demonstrated experience in providing technical and policy advice to ministers, senior government officials or executive boards on public debt matters;
  • Hands-on experience with debt recording and management systems, including data validation, reconciliation and the production of debt service projections, and with their integration with the IFMIS;
  • Experience in Sub-Saharan Africa is valued; experience in Mozambique or in Portuguese-speaking (lusophone) countries constitutes a relevant comparative advantage.
  • Working proficiency, written and oral, in English and Portuguese.  

7. Further information and the detailed Terms of Reference may be obtained upon request via the email address provided below. Expressions of Interest, comprising a cover letter and curriculum vitae, must be submitted electronically and received no later than November 9, 2026.

 

Address:                   

Ministry of Finance

449/469, Julius Nyerere Avenue, Bloc A, 11st floor

Email: procurement.mozprospera@gmail.com 

 Maputo – Mozambique

Ministry of Rural Development,Social and Community Empowerment

Social Protection Project

 

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

 

Loan No: P178973

Assignment Title: Conducting Project Training Program

No: LK-MOWCASE-562873-CS-CQS

  1. The Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka has received financing from the World Bank to meet the cost of the Social Protection Project, which is being implemented by the Department of Samurdhi and intends to apply part of the proceeds for conducting project Training Program for SDOs and other relevant staff for Social protection Project.

 

  1. The Social Protection Project is a Government of Sri Lanka project funded by the World Bank. The project supports Sri Lanka in providing better-targeted income and livelihood opportunities to poor and vulnerable households and in improving the responsiveness of the social protection system. The relevant equipment is required to support training and other project-related activities under the project.

 

  1. The Chairman, of the Project Consultants Procurement Committee on behalf of the Social Protection Project, invites eligible consulting firms, Academic Institutions universities to indicate their interest in providing the consultancy service for the above requirements.

 

  1. Sri Lanka’s Empowerment Program pilot is being implemented with the support from the Asian Development Bank (ADB) and the World Bank (WB) in selected areas nation-wide. The ADB support covers 13 districts, namely Anuradhapura, Batticaloa, Jaffna, Kalutara, Kandy, Kegalla, Kilinochchi, Kurunegala, Matale, Mulaitivu, Nuwara Eliya, Polonnaruwa and Trincomalee – covering 400 Grama Niladharis (GNs) and with a target of 12,800  participants. The WB support covers 12 districts, namely Ampara, Badulla, Colombo, Mannar, Monaragala, Rathnapura, Vavuniya, Galle, Matara, Hambantota, Gampaha and Puttalam covering 439 GNs with a target of more than 10,975 participants, across two phases. Phase 1 includes 7 non-impact evaluation districts, covering 35 Divisional Secretariats (DS)s and 175 GNs. Phase 2 includes 5 Impact evaluation districts covering 44 DSs, along with 8 GNs per DS while 6 GNs are considered as treatment GNs   and randomly selected 02 GNs will be considred as Controll GNs . Further information can be found in Table 1 and the full geographical coverage of districts, DSs, and GNs

 

  1. The detailed “Terms of Reference (TOR)” is now available at Social Protection  project Procurement Unit and interested parties may download these documents from the Social Protection Project www.dsd.samurdhi.gov.lk

 

  1. Interested consultancy firms must provide documentary evidence and related information indicating that they have the required qualifications, capacity and relevant experience to perform the services as per the selection criteria listed below.

 

  1. The shortlisting criteria will be as follows:
    1. The firm shall be legally registered with the Registrar of Companies or other legally recognized authority, as applicable. Academic/research institutions, universities, development institutions or other recognized institutions with a proven track record in relevant training, capacity building, social research, institutional development or related assignments may also be considered, subject to applicable procurement requirements. The date of establishment/incorporation and institutional mandate shall be provided
    2. The firm shall  a minimum 0f 5 years of relavant professional experience in conducting training and capacity building programmes, Training of trainers (TOT) institutional development ,sociol-economic development ,project implementation support,human resource development ,monitoring and evaluation,or other assignments relevant to the objectives of the Social Protection Project. 

 

    1. The firm shall demonstrate successful experience in conducting at least three (3) similar assignments during the last five (5) years, preferably involving Training of Trainers (ToT), management training, capacity building, curriculum/training material development, institutional strengthening, or training of government/development-sector personnel.Experience in assignments covering five (5) or more districts, and/or assignments implemented under World Bank, IFAD or other foreign-funded/development partner-funded projects, will be considered relevant additional experience
    2. Availability of full-time key experts such as  TOT Training Specialist,  Senior Training /Capacity Building Specialist,Social Protection / Community Development Specialist,Monitoring and Evaluation Specialist,Financial Literacy / Livelihood Development Specialist,Training Facilitators / Resource Persons
    3.  Support staff and resource pool including financial strength to conduct an assignment without much depending on the client

 

  1. A consultant will be selected in accordance with the procedures set out in the world Bank, and the method of selection will be Consultants selection Method (CQS).

 

  1. Interested firms should provide necessary details/information as requested above with 01 original and 05 copies for shortlisting along with the EOI.

 

  1. Further information can be obtained at the address below during working office hours, i.e. 0900 to 1600 hours except for Saturday, Sunday, and public holidays.

 

  1. Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person or by post) by on or before 30th   October  2026 at 2.00 pm. Any Expression of Interest (EOI) received after the specified closing date and time shall be rejected and shall not be considered for further evaluation or shortlisting.

L’Office National du Conseil Agricole sollicite des offres fermées de la part de soumissionnaires éligibles et répondant aux qualifications requises pour fournir Travaux d’aménagement des CCAs Transférés des ORMVAs du GHARB et TADLA La procédure sera conduite par mise en concurrence nationale en recourant à un Appel d’Offres National (AON) telle que définie dans le « Règlement– de Passation des Marchés applicables aux Emprunteurs dans le cadre de Financement de Projets d’Investissement » de Février 2023 de la Banque Mondiale (« le Règlement de passation des marchés »), et ouverte à tous les soumissionnaires tels que définis dans le Règlement de passation des marchés. 04 Décembre 2026 à 10 heures Le Dossier d’Appel d’offres en français peut être téléchargé gratuitement par tout Soumissionnaire intéressé au niveau du portail des marchés publics sur l’adresse URL www.marchespublics.gov.ma. Les offres devront être remises au portail des marchés publics ci-dessous[1] au plus tard le 04 Décembre 2026 à 10 heures . La soumission des offres par voie électronique « sera » obligatoire. Toute offre déposée après l’expiration du délai limite de remise des offres sera rejetée. Les offres seront ouvertes en présence des représentants des soumissionnaires et des personnes présentes au siège de l’Office National du Conseil Agricole, sis à Avenue Mohammed Belarbi Alaoui Hay Riad – Rabat , le 04 Décembre 2026 à 10 heures. Another objective is to provide technical assistance on assessment of the EUROTRACE system challenges faced by National Statistics Agencies. SADC SECRETARIAT

 

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST (INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANTS SELECTION)

 

 

COUNTRY:                             Botswana

 

NAME OF PROJECT: SADC REGIONAL STATISTICS PROJECT (RSP)

 

PROJECT ID:                     P175731

 

ASSIGNMENT TITLE:            INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT TO CARRY OUT NATIONAL TRAINING AND TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE ON EUROTRACE TO FOUR (4) SADC MEMBER STATES. BW-SADC-563150-CS-INDV

 

REFERENCE NUMBER:      SADC/3/5/2/465

 

DATE OF ISSUE:                   20 October 2026

 

The SADC Secretariat, through the SADC Regional Statistics Project (RSP) (P175731), has received grant financing from the International Development Association (IDA) of the World Bank. The Project Development Objective is to strengthen the institutional capacity of SADC to produce, disseminate and use quality statistics while increasing regional harmonisation and collaboration. Under the Project, SADC is implementing Component 1: Harmonisation, Quality and Dissemination of Core Social and Economic Statistics.

 

In view of the above, the SADC Secretariat is undertaking several interventions aimed at strengthening the SADC Regional Statistical System (SRSS) and enhancing the production, quality, harmonisation, dissemination and use of regional statistics. These interventions include technical assistance and capacity building activities in priority statistical areas, including poverty statistics, statistical software and data processing, survey methodologies, national accounts, environment and climate change statistics, statistical communication, quality assurance and harmonised regional statistical guidelines.

 

The SADC Secretariat intends to apply part of the proceeds of the grant towards the consulting services for Conduct National Training and Technical Assistance on Eurotrace to Four (4) SADC Member States, in support of the objectives of the Regional Statistics Project.

 

The SADC Secretariate invites submissions from suitably qualified and interested individual consultants to conduct the training, recruited as individual consultants following World Bank Procurement Regulations dated September 2023.

 

Title                 :  Individual Consultant to Conduct National Training and Technical Assistance on Eurotrace to Four (4) SADC Member States (1 Position)

 

Accountable:  Senior Officer, Research and Statistics 

 

Duration of Assignment:  12 months

 

  1. The Objectives of the Assignment

 

The overall objective of this exercise is to train Member States on the use of statistical software for merchandise trade statistics.

 

  1. Specific objectives

The specific objective of the assignment is to undertake an advance national training on EUROTRACE, especially SQL server based EUROTRACE to Statistics Agencies of four (4) SADC Member States to process and analyse trade data. Another objective is to provide technical assistance on assessment of the EUROTRACE system challenges faced by National Statistics Agencies.

  1. Expected results

 

The consultant is expected to achieve the following results:

  1. Strengthened technical capacity of Statistics Agencies in four (4) SADC Member States in the effectively and efficiently management and processing of trade  data using SQL Server based EUROTRACE;
  2. Sources of challenges with EUROTRACE identified, documented and resolved; and
  3. Statistics Agencies in four (4) SADC Member States to process and disseminate trade statistics using Eurotrace (SQL).

 

 

  1. QUALIFICATION AND EXPERIENCE REQUIREMENTS

 

This assignment is expected to be carried out by an individual consultant as the Master Trainer and strong experience and there should be evidence of in-depth knowledge of EUROTRACE. The specific profile is provided below:

 

Qualifications and Skills

  • A minimum of a Degree in statistics, economics, IT, Data Science or related field, A Master’s degree and above shall be an advantage.
  • Certificate in training on EUROTRACE
  • Written and oral fluency in the English language is essential. 
  • Excellent oral and written communication, analytical, presentation and report writing skills in English Language. 
  • Excellent time management and organizational skills to prioritize workload and delivery needful during the training week.

 

General Professional Experience

  • The Expert Must have at least fifteen (15) years of experience in merchandise trade statistics compilation and dissemination.

 

Specific Professional Experience

  • Demonstrated experience of at least 10 years using EUROTRACE for processing and dissemination of merchandise trade statistics at national, regional or continental level;
  • Demonstrated experience as a resource person in delivering at least 5 training/technical assistance activities to developing countries at national, regional and continental level in Eurotrace software. Training in SADC Member States shall be an advantage.

 

  1. Duration of the assignment

 

The Individual Consultant will be engaged for 12 months. The assignment is for a continuous period of twelve (12) months from the date of contract signature. This is a calendar-based duration and does not represent an accumulation of individual billable days.

 

  1. Facilities to be provided by the Client

 

For the expert working on this consultancy, the Contracting Authority shall facilitate visa entry in the member states hosting the workshop, if required.

 

  1. Location of Employment

 

The assignment will involve traveling to four (4) SADC Member States.

 

  1. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” dated September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. 

 

  1. A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultant Selection Method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

 

  1. Mode of Application

 

Interested Individuals Consultants meeting the stated requirements should submit their Expressions of interest including updated detailed curriculum vitae (CVs) and copies of professional certificates must be delivered in a written form using a drag and drop electronic tender box by Thursday, 5th November 2026 on or before 00:00 hours, Botswana local time. No public opening will be heard.

 

 

SADC Collab Link: https://collab.sadc.int/s/M46sbqagZTxGTxY

 

 

Kindly note that only highly technically scored bidder will be contacted for negotiations meeting.

 

  1. VALIDITY OF THE TECHINICAL PROPOSAL

Your Technical proposal should be valid for a period of 120 days from the date of deadline for submission.

SADC SECRETARIAT

 

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST (INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANTS SELECTION)

 

 

COUNTRY:                             Botswana

 

NAME OF PROJECT:            SADC REGIONAL STATISTICS PROJECT (RSP)

 

PROJECT ID:                     P175731

 

ASSIGNMENT TITLE:            INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANCY TO UNDERTAKE CAPACITY BUILDING ON STATA IN FIVE (5) SADC MEMBER STATES AS A RESOURCE PERSON. BW-SADC-563171-CS-INDV

 

 

REFERENCE NUMBER: SADC/5/2/466

 

DATE OF ISSUE: 20 October 2026

 

The SADC Secretariat, through the SADC Regional Statistics Project (RSP) (P175731), has received grant financing from the International Development Association (IDA) of the World Bank. The Project Development Objective is to strengthen the institutional capacity of SADC to produce, disseminate and use quality statistics while increasing regional harmonisation and collaboration. Under the Project, SADC is implementing Component 1: Harmonisation, Quality and Dissemination of Core Social and Economic Statistics.

In view of the above, the SADC Secretariat is undertaking several interventions aimed at strengthening the SADC Regional Statistical System (SRSS) and enhancing the production, quality, harmonisation, dissemination and use of regional statistics. These interventions include technical assistance and capacity building activities in priority statistical areas, including poverty statistics, statistical software and data processing, survey methodologies, national accounts, environment and climate change statistics, statistical communication, quality assurance and harmonised regional statistical guidelines.

 

 

The SADC Secretariat intends to apply part of the proceeds of the grant towards the consulting services to undertake capacity building on Stata in five (5) SADC member states in support of the objectives of the Regional Statistics Project.

 

The SADC Secretariate invites submissions from suitably qualified and interested individual consultants to conduct the training, recruited as individual consultants following World Bank Procurement Regulations dated September 2023.

 

Title                 :  Individual Consultant to undertake capacity building on Stata in five (5) SADC member states (1 Position)

 

Accountable:  Senior Officer, Research and Statistics 

 

Duration of Assignment:  12 months

 

  1. The Objectives of the Assignment

 

The overall objective of this exercise is to enhance the capacity of Member States on collection, processing and analysis of census, surveys and administrative data.

 

  1. Specific objectives

 

The specific objective of the assignment is to undertake a national training on STATA to five (5) SADC Member States National Statistics Offices to process and analyse censuses, surveys  and administrative data, specific to each country.

 

Furthermore, the objectives are also to:

 

  • strengthen the technical capacity of National Statistics Offices staff in using STATA for advanced statistical analysis, focusing on Official Statistics.
  • promote the use of do-files and automation techniques to improve efficiency, traceability, and standardization of analysis processes.

 

  • assess the existing practices and use of STATA by the different departments of National Statistics Offices and encourage adoption of common methodologies across technical departments, ensuring coherence, quality, and statistical comparability

 

  1. Expected results

 

The consultant is expected to achieve the following result:

  • Strengthening technical capacity of National Statistics Offices in the management and processing of data from census and surveys using STATA; and 
  • Identification of gaps regarding use of STATA by the different departments of National Statistics Offices to roll out the gaps to close specific timelines and associated tasks. 

 

 

  1. QUALIFICATION AND EXPERIENCE REQUIREMENTS

 

This assignment is expected to be carried out by an individual consultant as the Master Trainer and there should be evidence of in-depth knowledge with statistical analysis software (STATA).  The specific profile is provided below:

 

Qualifications and Skills

    • A minimum of master’s degree in statistics, economics, IT or related field
    • Written and oral fluency in the English language is essential.  Knowledge of French and/or Portuguese is an added advantage.
    • Excellent oral and written communication, analytical, presentation and report writing skills in English Language. 
    • Excellent time management and organizational skills to prioritize workload and deliver needful during the training week.

 

General Professional Experience

    • The Expert Must have at least ten (10) years of experience using statistics analysis software STATA pertaining to Official Statistics.

 

Specific Professional Experience

    • Proven experience in statistical data processing and analysis, spatial analysis, modelling and data visualization using STATA for at least 3 major surveys for Official Statistics at national level;
    • Experience in the design and implementation of training materials for the conduct of statistical data analysis training in Official Statistics using STATA;
    • Extensive experience as a resource person in delivering at least 3 training on STATA at national level, particularly using household and census data.

 

  1. Duration of the assignment

 

The Individual Consultant will be recruited for 12 months. Note: the 12 months is the duration of the assignment and not the number of days required to undertake it. It caters for coordination of work to be done by recipients of the assignment and to a certain extent, flexibility for the consultant to deliver on the outputs.

 

  1. Facilities to be provided by the Client

 

For the expert working on this consultancy, the Contracting Authority shall facilitate visa entry in the member states hosting the workshop, if required.

 

  1. Location of Employment

 

The assignment will involve traveling to five (5) SADC Member States.

 

  1. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” dated September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. 

 

  1. A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultant Selection Method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

 

  1. Mode of Application

 

Interested Individuals Consultants meeting the stated requirements should submit their Expressions of interest including updated detailed curriculum vitae (CVs) and copies of professional certificates must be delivered in a written form using a drag and drop electronic tender box by Thursday, 5th November 2026 on or before 00:00 hours, Botswana local time. No public opening will be heard.

 

 

SADC Collab Link: https://collab.sadc.int/s/Gjobqm3gorKpAii

 

 

Kindly note that only highly technically scored bidder will be contacted for negotiations meeting.

 

  1. VALIDITY OF THE TECHINICAL PROPOSAL

Your Technical proposal should be valid for a period of 120 days from the date of deadline for submission.

notice_text: PROJET D’HARMONISATION ET D’AMELIORATION DES STATISTIQUES EN AFRIQUE DE L’OUEST ET DU CENTRE - SERIE DE PROJETS N°2 (HISWACA - SOP 2) ---------------------------- UNITE DE GESTION DU PROJET ------------------- AVIS A MANIFESTATION D’INTERÊTS N°080 /HISWACA /2026 RECRUTEMENT D'UN CONSULTANT POUR L'APPUI TECHNIQUE À LA MISE EN ŒUVRE DE L'ENQUÊTE TRIMESTRIELLE SUR L'EMPLOI ET LE SECTEUR INFORMEL AU CONGO (EESIC-T)AVIS A MANIFESTATION D’INTERÊTS N°080 /HISWACA /2026 RECRUTEMENT D'UN CONSULTANT POUR L'APPUI TECHNIQUE À LA MISE EN ŒUVRE DE L'ENQUÊTE TRIMESTRIELLE SUR L'EMPLOI ET LE SECTEUR INFORMEL AU CONGO (EESIC-T) 1. Le Gouvernement de la République du Congo a reçu un financement additionnel de l’Association Internationale pour le Développement (IDA) pour la mise en œuvre des activités du « Projet d’Harmonisation et d’Amélioration des Statistiques en Afrique de l’Ouest et du Centre (HISWACA) », et a l’intention d’utiliser une partie du montant de ce financement pour effectuer les paiements au titre du contrat suivant  : «recrutement d'un consultant national pour l'appui technique à la mise en œuvre de l'enquête trimestrielle sur l'emploi et le secteur informel au Congo (EESIC-T)». 2. L'objectif général de la mission est d'apporter un appui technique de haut niveau à l'Institut National de la Statistique pour la conception, la mise en œuvre, le suivi et l'exploitation de l'Enquête Trimestrielle sur l'Emploi et le Secteur Informel au Congo (EESIC-T), en garantissant la qualité de l'opération conformément à la méthodologie harmonisée de la CEMAC et en assurant une production périodique d'indicateurs fiables et comparables sur le marché du travail et le secteur informel. Plus spécifiquement, il s’agira de : Appuyer la finalisation des documents techniques et des outils de collecte (questionnaires ménage, emploi, secteur informel, fiche de dénombrement, manuels d'instructions, protocole d'enquête) en étroite collaboration avec l'expert international du BIT et l'équipe technique permanente ; Contribuer à la conception et au paramétrage de l'application CAPI utilisée pour la collecte des données, ainsi qu'à la définition des règles de cohérence, des filtres et des sauts ; Appuyer le tirage de l'échantillon trimestriel et la mise en œuvre opérationnelle du panel rotatif (renouvellement d'un tiers de l'échantillon chaque trimestre) sur la base du plan de sondage aréolaire à deux degrés ; Contribuer à l'organisation et à l'animation des sessions de formation des superviseurs, contrôleurs et enquêteurs, ainsi qu'à la conduite de l'enquête pilote ; Assurer le suivi technique des opérations de collecte trimestrielles, le contrôle qualité des données (suivi des entretiens, contre-interviews, contrôles automatiques) et l'accompagnement méthodologique des équipes terrain ; Participer au traitement, à la pondération et à l'analyse des données collectées, ainsi qu'à la production des tableaux de résultats et des indicateurs clés du marché du travail ; Veiller à l’archivage des bases de données trimestrielles apurées et pondérées ; Veiller à la mise à jour des tableaux de bord trimestriels des indicateurs clés du marché du travail et du secteur informel ; Contribuer à la rédaction des rapports trimestriels et annuels d'analyse des résultats de l'enquête ; Assurer l'interface technique permanente avec l'expert international du BIT et intégrer dans les travaux nationaux les orientations méthodologiques internationales. Etc… 3. L’Unité de gestion du projet HISWACA invite les consultants individuels à manifester leur intérêt en vue de fournir les services décrits ci-dessus. Les consultants individuels intéressés doivent fournir les informations sur leur qualifications et expérience démontrant qu’ils sont qualifiés pour les prestations (curriculum-vitae daté et signé, copies des diplômes et des justificatifs de références en prestations similaires réalisées, etc.) 4. La sélection du consultant se fera en accord avec les procédures définies dans le Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d’Investissements (FPI) de la Banque mondiale (version de juillet 2016, révisée en novembre 2017, août 2018, septembre 2023 et septembre 2025). 5.  Les consultants peuvent obtenir les termes de références de la mission par courriel à l’adresse : ugp@hiswaca-congo.org /  recrutementhiswaca@gmail.com , de 9 heures à 12 heures et de 14 heures à 16 heures (heures locales) du lundi au vendredi. 6. Les manifestations d’intérêts doivent être écrites en langue française et être déposées à l’adresse ci-dessous ou envoyées par courriel au plus tard le vendredi  13 novembre 2026  (à minuit, heure locale) et porter clairement la mention «recrutement d'un consultant national pour l'appui technique à la mise en œuvre de l'enquête trimestrielle sur l'emploi et le secteur informel au Congo (EESIC-T) ».   7. L’adresse à laquelle, il est fait référence ci-dessus est : projet HISWACA,  Centre d’Affaires des Tours Jumelles de Mpila, 12ième étage, Porte 1204, Tél : (+242) 06 157 01 01, E-mail : ugp@hiswaca-congo.org   / recrutementhiswaca@gmail.com      Fait à Brazzaville, le 21 octobre 2026                                                                                                                 Coordonnateur                                                                                                                                  Patrick Valery ALAKOUA

Les manifestations d’intérêts doivent être écrites en langue française et être déposées à l’adresse ci-dessous ou envoyées par courriel au plus tard le vendredi 13 novembre 2026 (à minuit, heure locale) et porter clairement la mention «recrutement d'un consultant national pour l'appui technique à la mise en œuvre de l'enquête trimestrielle sur l'emploi et le secteur informel au Congo (EESIC-T) ».  

7. L’adresse à laquelle, il est fait référence ci-dessus est : projet HISWACA, Centre d’Affaires des Tours Jumelles de Mpila, 12ième étage, Porte 1204, Tél : (+242) 06 157 01 01, E-mail : ugp@hiswaca-congo.org  / recrutementhiswaca@gmail.com

notice_text: Specific Procurement Notice Request for Bids Works (Two-envelope Bidding Process, Without Prequalification) Employer: Azerenerji” JSC Project: Azerbaijan Scaling-Up Renewable Energy Project (AZURE) Contract title: Construction of 330 kV single and double-circuit OHL’s a) Construction of 330 kV double-circuit Navahi SS OHL- Alat FEZ SS – 22.58 km b) Construction of 330 kV single-circuit Navahi SS- Gobustan WPP OHL-63 km c) Construction of 330 kV single-circuit Gobustan WPP - Gobu ES OHL-20.3 km Country: Azerbaijan Loan No. 9799-AZ RFB No: AZ-AZERENERJI-512325-CW-RFB- TL-2 Issued on: 21 October 2026 The Government of the Republic of Azerbaijan has received for financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Azerbaijan Scaling-Up Renewable Energy Project (AZURE) and intends to apply part of the proceeds toward payments under the contract for Construction of 330 kV single-circuit OHL Construction of 330 kV double-circuit Navahi SS OHL- Alat FEZ SS – 22.58 km Construction of 330 kV single-circuit Navahi SS- Gobustan WPP OHL-63 km Construction of 330 kV single-circuit Gobustan WPP - Gobu ES OHL-20.3 km   2. The Azerenerji JSC now invites sealed Bids from eligible Bidders for Construction of HV OHL 330 kV double-circuit OHL connecting Navahi SS with Alat FEZ SS – 22.58 km; Navahi SS with Gobustan WPP OHL-63 km and Gobustan WPP with Gobu ES OHL-20.3 km total construction period being 730 days. Margin of Domestic preference shall not apply. The qualification requirements are: a)The Bidder shall demonstrate that it has access to, or has available, liquid assets, unencumbered real assets, lines of credit, and other financial means (independent of any contractual advance payment) sufficient to meet the construction cash flow requirements estimated as USD 5 million for the subject contract(s) net of the Bidder’s other commitments b)Minimum average annual construction turnover of USD 36 million, calculated as total certified payments received for contracts in progress and/or completed within the last 3 years c)A minimum number of one (1)  similar contract of value USD 60 million or a minimum number of Two (2)  similar contracts of value USD 30 million each that have been satisfactorily and substantially completed as a prime contractor, joint venture member[1], management contractor or Subcontractor between 1st January 2021 and bid submission deadline 3. Bidding will be conducted through international competitive procurement using Request for Bids (RFB) as specified in the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers- Procurement in Investment Projects Financing” Seventh Edition September 2025  (“Procurement Regulations”), and is open to all eligible Bidders as defined in the Procurement Regulations. 4. Bids will be evaluated in accordance with the evaluation process set out in the bidding documents. The following weightings shall apply for Rated Criteria (including technical and non-price factors): 50 %. and for the Bid cost: 50 %. 5. Interested eligible Bidders may obtain further information from Mr. Vugar Guliyev, PIU Director “Azerenerji” JSC Address:  10 Abdulkarim Alizade str., Azerenerji Head office, Third  Floor Country: Baku, Azerbaijan Postal Code: AZ1005 E-mail: vuqar.quliyev@azerenerji.gov.az  and inspect the Bidding document during office hours . 09.00 to 17.00 hours at the address given above. 6. The Bidding document in English will be provided free of charge to interested eligible Bidders upon the submission of a written application to the address below. 7. Bids must be delivered to the address below on or before 15:00 (Baku time) on 21 December 2026. Electronic bidding will not be permitted. Late Bids will be rejected. The outer Bid envelopes marked “ORIGINAL BID,” and the inner envelopes marked “TECHNICAL PART” will be publicly opened in the presence of the Bidders’ designated representatives and anyone who chooses to attend, at the address below on 15:00 (Baku time) on 21 December 2026. All envelopes marked “FINANCIAL PART” shall remain unopened and will be held in safe custody of the Employer until the second public Bid opening.  8. All Bids must be accompanied by a (i) Bid Security of USD 200,000 . and (ii) Local Labour Method Statement. 9. Attention is drawn to the Procurement Regulations requiring the Borrower to disclose information on the successful bidder’s beneficial ownership, as part of the Contract Award Notice, using the Beneficial Ownership Disclosure Form as included in the bidding document. 10. AVIS DE DEMANDE DE COTATION OUVERTE

Financement : Crédit IDA 71210

Réf      : Consultation de Fournisseur N° 07-26/PAAEP/UGP-MEAH/DC/FRN BUR

Objet     : Acquisition de fournitures des bureaux

  1. La République de Madagascar a reçu un financement de la Banque Mondiale pour financer la mise œuvre du Projet d’Amélioration de l’Accès à l’Eau Potable de Madagascar (PAAEP-UGP MEAH), et a l’intention d’utiliser une partie de ce crédit pour effectuer des paiements au titre du marché, objet du présent Avis.
  2. L'UGP PAAEP-MEAH sollicite des offres sous plis fermées de la part des soumissionnaires éligibles et répondant aux qualifications requises pour la fourniture et la livraison de fourniture des bureaux pour le projet.
  3. Les dossiers de demande de cotations (DC) en version française, sont disponibles dans le site WEB du projet mentionné ci-dessous, et sont accessibles à tous les soumissionnaires éligibles et intéressés.
  4. La procédure sera conduite par une demande de cotation telle que décrite dans le « Règlement de Passation de Marchés par les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projet d’Investissement (FPI), de la Banque mondiale, en date du juillet 2016, mise à jour en septembre 2023 (5ème édition) et ouverte à tous les soumissionnaires de pays éligibles.
  5. La cotation présentée par le fournisseur devra comprendre obligatoirement :

a)   la lettre de cotation, datée et signée ;

b)   le Bordereau Descriptif, Quantitatif et Estimatif dûment rempli, daté et signé ;

c)   la lettre de marché paraphé ;

e)   la liste des fournitures et délai de livraison ;

f)   la liste des marchés similaires avec leur montant respectif appuyés par des attestations de bonne fin ou tout autre document équivalent ;

g)   les spécifications techniques ;

h)   la garantie de soumission ;

i)   les copies certifiées de :

-     la carte statistique

-     la Numéro d’Immatriculation Fiscale (CIF) à jour.

  1. Les offres devront être remises sous pli fermé à l'adresse ci-dessous au plus tard le Jeudi 05 NOVEMBRE 2026 à dix (10) heures. La soumission des offres par voie électronique ne sera pas autorisée. Les offres reçues au-delà de cette date et heures limites seront rejetées.
  2. Les cotations seront valables jusqu’au 04 Février 2027.
  3. Le montant de la garantie de soumission est Deux millions Ariary (2 000 000 Ar).
  4. Les offres seront ouvertes en présence des représentants des soumissionnaires et des personnes présentes à l’adresse mentionnée ci-dessous le Jeudi 05 Novembre 2026 et à l’heure indiquée ci-dessus.
  5. L’adresse à laquelle il est fait référence ci-dessus est : 

Bâtiment A1 – Rez-de-chaussée.

Explorer Business Park (Ex-village des jeux) Ankorondrano, Antananarivo 101.

Site WEB : www.paaep.mg

notice_text:   SOKOTO STATE PROJECT IMPLEMENTATION UNIT REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (REOI) Selection of Consulting Firms — Consultant Qualification Selection (CQS) Country: Federal Republic of Nigeria Project: Sustainable Power and Irrigation for Nigeria (SPIN) Project Credit No.: IDA-76370 Assignment Title: Consultancy Services for the Preparation of a Resettlement Action Plan (RAP) for the Rehabilitation of the Kware Irrigation Scheme, Kware, Sokoto State Reference No.: NG-SOKOTO STATE SPIN-572043-CS-CQS Procurement Process: Selection of Consultants — CQS (Firm) 1. Background The Federal Government of Nigeria, supported by the World Bank through the Federal Ministry of Water Resources and Sanitation, is implementing the Sustainable Power and Irrigation for Nigeria (SPIN) Project. The Project Development Objective is to improve water security in Nigeria by enhancing the management and resilience of water resource infrastructure, increasing water availability for irrigation and hydropower, improving dam safety, and promoting institutional collaboration for climate-resilient food and energy production. This assignment relates to Components 2 (Irrigation Modernization) and 3 (Improvements in Dam Operations and Enhancing Dam Safety) of the Project. The Kware Irrigation Scheme, in Kware Local Government Area of Sokoto State, spans approximately 500 hectares within a broader 10,000-hectare irrigation zone supplied by the Kware–Shalla Dam. An Environmental and Social Screening exercise conducted in 2025 classified the Scheme as Category A (High Environmental and Social Risk), with High social sensitivity driven by the proximity of the Giro community to the dam, flood risk to surrounding communities, and the potential for physical or economic displacement during rehabilitation. The SPIN Project target is full rehabilitation and operationalisation of 600 hectares, with planned works including raising of the dam embankment by one metre, construction of a spillway control well, a second (emergency release) pipeline, and rehabilitation of the main and distributary canal network. Given the scale and nature of these works, a site-specific Resettlement Action Plan (RAP) is required, consistent with the disclosed SPIN Resettlement Policy Framework (RPF), World Bank Environmental and Social Standard 5 (ESS5) on Land Acquisition, Restrictions on Land Use and Involuntary Resettlement, and the Nigerian Land Use Act. The Sokoto State Ministry of Agriculture and Natural Resources, through the SPIN Project Implementation Unit (the "Client"), now wishes to engage a qualified firm to prepare the RAP. 2. Objective and Scope of Services The objective of the assignment is to identify potential physical and economic displacement risks and impacts associated with the rehabilitation of the Kware Irrigation Scheme, and to prepare a comprehensive, site-specific RAP that avoids, minimises, mitigates, and manages displacement and livelihood impacts, in compliance with the Nigerian Land Use Act and World Bank ESS5. The Scope of Services includes, but is not limited to: Review of project documents, engineering designs, and applicable national legal frameworks, with a gap analysis between Nigerian law and ESS5 and proposed bridging measures; A 100% census and detailed socio-economic survey of Project Affected Persons (PAPs), disaggregated by sex, age, and vulnerability status, and a 100% inventory of affected assets (land, structures, crops, trees, and common property); Establishment of a formal cut-off date, supported by public notification, and use of GPS, GIS, and satellite imagery in asset surveys and mapping; Preparation of an Entitlement Matrix and full-replacement-cost compensation rates, with particular attention to eligibility criteria that are advantageous to women and other vulnerable groups; Design of a detailed livelihood restoration framework, including vocational training, income-generating activities, and special provisions for vulnerable groups; A stakeholder consultation and disclosure strategy, a site-specific Grievance Redress Mechanism, and measures to address impacts on host communities; A detailed, costed, and time-bound RAP implementation schedule linked to civil works milestones, institutional implementation arrangements, and a monitoring and evaluation framework, including provision for an independent RAP Completion Audit. The full Terms of Reference (TOR) describing the detailed scope, methodology, deliverables, and reporting requirements will be provided to shortlisted firms. 3. Duration of the Assignment The assignment shall not exceed eight (8) weeks from the date of contract signing. 4. Qualification Requirements The Client now invites eligible consulting firms ("Consultants") to indicate their interest in providing the above-described services. Interested Consultants must provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the services. The shortlisting criteria are as follows: The firm must be an Environmental and Social Management consulting firm with a minimum of five (5) years' work experience in projects requiring resettlement planning and implementation; Demonstrated working knowledge of the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework, particularly ESS5, gained through hands-on experience preparing and implementing Resettlement Action Plans in rural/agricultural settings, having prepared at least three (3) RAPs for World Bank-funded projects; Demonstrated capacity to field a multi-disciplinary team covering, at a minimum: social development/RAP specialism, land economics/valuation, socio-economic survey and census, livelihood and economic restoration, gender and GBV, engineering (for impact-footprint mapping), and GIS/mapping; Qualified and experienced staff in social safeguards, socio-economics, land valuation, livelihood restoration, and GBV/SEA/SH risk management, with excellent communication and report-writing skills; Sound financial standing and availability of key professional, technical, and administrative staff and resources to carry out the assignment within the stipulated timeframe. Consultants may associate with other firms in the form of a joint venture or a sub-consultancy to enhance their qualifications. In the case of a joint venture, all members shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire assignment, and the Expression of Interest shall clearly identify the lead firm and the roles of each member. 5. Submission Requirements Interested Consultants should submit the following information: A letter of expression of interest; Company/firm profile, including registration/incorporation documents and evidence of legal status; Description of similar assignments undertaken in the last ten (10) years, indicating client name, contract value, duration, funding source, and a brief description of services provided, with particular reference to RAP preparation and implementation; Organisational chart and an indicative list of key professional staff available for the assignment, with a summary of their qualifications (detailed CVs are not required at this stage); Evidence of financial capacity (e.g., audited financial statements for the last three years or a statement from a recognised financial institution); and A statement confirming the firm's (and any joint venture partners') eligibility and absence of conflict of interest, in accordance with the World Bank's Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers. Attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraph 3.14, 3.16, 3.17 and Annex VI of the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (Fifth Edition, September 2023, or the edition applicable to the Financing Agreement), setting out the World Bank's policy on conflict of interest. 6. Selection Method A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Consultant Qualification Selection (CQS) method set out in the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers. A shortlist of approximately four (4) firms will be prepared from the Expressions of Interest received, and shortlisted firms will subsequently be invited to submit technical and financial proposals through a Request for Proposals (RFP). 7. Submission of Expressions of Interest Expressions of interest, in English, marked "Expression of Interest Preparation of a Resettlement Action Plan (RAP) for the Kware Irrigation Scheme" and quoting the Reference Number above, must be delivered in a sealed envelope (or, where permitted, by e-mail) to the address below not later than  15th oct 2026 at 12;00pm (local time). 8. Contact Address SOKOTO STATE SPIN PROJECT IMPLEMENTATION UNIT No 17A GAWON NAMA, KWARE ROAD SOKOTO STATE, NIGERIA TEL: +2347068237012 E-mail: sokotospin@gmail.com   This request for expressions of interest is issued without obligation on the part of the Client, and the Client reserves the right to accept or reject any or all Expressions of Interest received.

SOKOTO STATE PROJECT IMPLEMENTATION UNIT

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (REOI)

Selection of Consulting Firms — Consultant Qualification Selection (CQS)

Country: Federal Republic of Nigeria

Project: Sustainable Power and Irrigation for Nigeria (SPIN) Project

Credit No.: IDA-76370

Assignment Title: Consultancy Services for the Preparation of a Resettlement Action Plan (RAP) for the Rehabilitation of the Kware Irrigation Scheme, Kware, Sokoto State

Reference No.: NG-SOKOTO STATE SPIN-572043-CS-CQS

Procurement Process: Selection of Consultants — CQS (Firm)

1. Background

The Federal Government of Nigeria, supported by the World Bank through the Federal Ministry of Water Resources and Sanitation, is implementing the Sustainable Power and Irrigation for Nigeria (SPIN) Project. The Project Development Objective is to improve water security in Nigeria by enhancing the management and resilience of water resource infrastructure, increasing water availability for irrigation and hydropower, improving dam safety, and promoting institutional collaboration for climate-resilient food and energy production. This assignment relates to Components 2 (Irrigation Modernization) and 3 (Improvements in Dam Operations and Enhancing Dam Safety) of the Project.

The Kware Irrigation Scheme, in Kware Local Government Area of Sokoto State, spans approximately 500 hectares within a broader 10,000-hectare irrigation zone supplied by the Kware–Shalla Dam. An Environmental and Social Screening exercise conducted in 2025 classified the Scheme as Category A (High Environmental and Social Risk), with High social sensitivity driven by the proximity of the Giro community to the dam, flood risk to surrounding communities, and the potential for physical or economic displacement during rehabilitation. The SPIN Project target is full rehabilitation and operationalisation of 600 hectares, with planned works including raising of the dam embankment by one metre, construction of a spillway control well, a second (emergency release) pipeline, and rehabilitation of the main and distributary canal network.

Given the scale and nature of these works, a site-specific Resettlement Action Plan (RAP) is required, consistent with the disclosed SPIN Resettlement Policy Framework (RPF), World Bank Environmental and Social Standard 5 (ESS5) on Land Acquisition, Restrictions on Land Use and Involuntary Resettlement, and the Nigerian Land Use Act. The Sokoto State Ministry of Agriculture and Natural Resources, through the SPIN Project Implementation Unit (the "Client"), now wishes to engage a qualified firm to prepare the RAP.

2. Objective and Scope of Services

The objective of the assignment is to identify potential physical and economic displacement risks and impacts associated with the rehabilitation of the Kware Irrigation Scheme, and to prepare a comprehensive, site-specific RAP that avoids, minimises, mitigates, and manages displacement and livelihood impacts, in compliance with the Nigerian Land Use Act and World Bank ESS5. The Scope of Services includes, but is not limited to:

  1. Review of project documents, engineering designs, and applicable national legal frameworks, with a gap analysis between Nigerian law and ESS5 and proposed bridging measures;
  2. A 100% census and detailed socio-economic survey of Project Affected Persons (PAPs), disaggregated by sex, age, and vulnerability status, and a 100% inventory of affected assets (land, structures, crops, trees, and common property);
  3. Establishment of a formal cut-off date, supported by public notification, and use of GPS, GIS, and satellite imagery in asset surveys and mapping;
  4. Preparation of an Entitlement Matrix and full-replacement-cost compensation rates, with particular attention to eligibility criteria that are advantageous to women and other vulnerable groups;
  5. Design of a detailed livelihood restoration framework, including vocational training, income-generating activities, and special provisions for vulnerable groups;
  6. A stakeholder consultation and disclosure strategy, a site-specific Grievance Redress Mechanism, and measures to address impacts on host communities;
  7. A detailed, costed, and time-bound RAP implementation schedule linked to civil works milestones, institutional implementation arrangements, and a monitoring and evaluation framework, including provision for an independent RAP Completion Audit.

The full Terms of Reference (TOR) describing the detailed scope, methodology, deliverables, and reporting requirements will be provided to shortlisted firms.

3. Duration of the Assignment

The assignment shall not exceed eight (8) weeks from the date of contract signing.

4. Qualification Requirements

The Client now invites eligible consulting firms ("Consultants") to indicate their interest in providing the above-described services. Interested Consultants must provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the services. The shortlisting criteria are as follows:

  1. The firm must be an Environmental and Social Management consulting firm with a minimum of five (5) years' work experience in projects requiring resettlement planning and implementation;
  2. Demonstrated working knowledge of the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework, particularly ESS5, gained through hands-on experience preparing and implementing Resettlement Action Plans in rural/agricultural settings, having prepared at least three (3) RAPs for World Bank-funded projects;
  3. Demonstrated capacity to field a multi-disciplinary team covering, at a minimum: social development/RAP specialism, land economics/valuation, socio-economic survey and census, livelihood and economic restoration, gender and GBV, engineering (for impact-footprint mapping), and GIS/mapping;
  4. Qualified and experienced staff in social safeguards, socio-economics, land valuation, livelihood restoration, and GBV/SEA/SH risk management, with excellent communication and report-writing skills;
  5. Sound financial standing and availability of key professional, technical, and administrative staff and resources to carry out the assignment within the stipulated timeframe.

Consultants may associate with other firms in the form of a joint venture or a sub-consultancy to enhance their qualifications. In the case of a joint venture, all members shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire assignment, and the Expression of Interest shall clearly identify the lead firm and the roles of each member.

5. Submission Requirements

Interested Consultants should submit the following information:

  • A letter of expression of interest;
  • Company/firm profile, including registration/incorporation documents and evidence of legal status;
  • Description of similar assignments undertaken in the last ten (10) years, indicating client name, contract value, duration, funding source, and a brief description of services provided, with particular reference to RAP preparation and implementation;
  • Organisational chart and an indicative list of key professional staff available for the assignment, with a summary of their qualifications (detailed CVs are not required at this stage);
  • Evidence of financial capacity (e.g., audited financial statements for the last three years or a statement from a recognised financial institution); and
  • A statement confirming the firm's (and any joint venture partners') eligibility and absence of conflict of interest, in accordance with the World Bank's Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers.

Attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraph 3.14, 3.16, 3.17 and Annex VI of the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (Fifth Edition, September 2023, or the edition applicable to the Financing Agreement), setting out the World Bank's policy on conflict of interest.

6. Selection Method

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Consultant Qualification Selection (CQS) method set out in the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers. A shortlist of approximately four (4) firms will be prepared from the Expressions of Interest received, and shortlisted firms will subsequently be invited to submit technical and financial proposals through a Request for Proposals (RFP).

7. Submission of Expressions of Interest

Expressions of interest, in English, marked "Expression of Interest Preparation of a Resettlement Action Plan (RAP) for the Kware Irrigation Scheme" and quoting the Reference Number above, must be delivered in a sealed envelope (or, where permitted, by e-mail) to the address below not later than  15th oct 2026 at 12;00pm (local time).

notice_text: SOKOTO STATE PROJECT IMPLEMENTATION UNIT REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (REOI) Selection of Consulting Firms — Consultant Qualification Selection (CQS) Country: Federal Republic of Nigeria Project: Sustainable Power and Irrigation for Nigeria (SPIN) Project Credit No.: IDA-76370 Assignment Title: Consultancy Services for the Detailed Design Review for the Rehabilitation of the Kware Irrigation Scheme, Kware, Sokoto State Reference No.: NG-SOKOTO STATE SPIN-572874-CS-CQS Procurement Process: Selection of Consultants — CQS (Firm) 1. Background The Federal Government of Nigeria, with financing from the World Bank, is implementing the Sustainable Power and Irrigation for Nigeria (SPIN) Project to strengthen dam safety, improve water resource management, and expand irrigation infrastructure across participating states. The Project builds on the Transforming Irrigation Management in Nigeria (TRIMING) Project and aims to rehabilitate approximately 40,000 hectares of irrigated command areas nationwide while improving dam safety and water storage management across Nigeria's dams. The Kware Irrigation Scheme, located in Kware Local Government Area, Sokoto State, was originally constructed in 1954 and derives its water supply from Kware Lake, formed by the Kware Water Conservation Structure. An Update Design Report (May 2026) proposes extending the Scheme by 500 hectares net cultural command area (550 hectares gross) through rehabilitation of the reservoir, intake works, canal network, and associated hydraulic structures. An independent technical review of the Engineering Design Report and Bill of Engineering Measurement and Evaluation (BEME) classified the submission as requiring significant revision, citing unresolved technical, cost, and economic viability concerns, including incomplete construction drawings, an unsubstantiated increase in the height of the Water Conservation Structure, a unit cost significantly above the World Bank benchmark, and a negative economic return. The Kware Irrigation Scheme, located in Kware Local Government Area, Sokoto State, was originally constructed in 1954 and derives its water supply from Kware Lake, formed by the Kware Water Conservation Structure. An Update Design Report (May 2026) proposes extending the Scheme by 500 hectares net cultural command area (550 hectares gross) through rehabilitation of the reservoir, intake works, canal network, and associated hydraulic structures.

An independent technical review of the Engineering Design Report and Bill of Engineering Measurement and Evaluation (BEME) classified the submission as requiring significant revision, citing unresolved technical, cost, and economic viability concerns, including incomplete construction drawings, an unsubstantiated increase in the height of the Water Conservation Structure, a unit cost significantly above the World Bank benchmark, and a negative economic return. The Sokoto State Ministry of Agriculture and Natural Resources, through the SPIN Project Implementation Unit (the "Client"), now wishes to engage an independent Consulting Firm to undertake a comprehensive Detailed Design Review to bring the Scheme to a bankable, cost-effective, and economically viable standard suitable for World Bank financing.

2. Objective and Scope of Services

  1. The objective of the assignment is to undertake a comprehensive, independent Detailed Design Review of the Kware Irrigation Scheme Update Design, in order to verify, validate, complete, and, where necessary, revise the engineering design, cost estimates, and economic analysis, delivering a technically sound, cost-optimized, and economically viable rehabilitation design ready for implementation. The Scope of Services includes, but is not limited to:
  2. Review and verification of topographic, hydrological, geotechnical, and soil investigation data, including supplementary field surveys where gaps exist;
  3. Independent hydraulic and structural review of the Water Conservation Structure, intake structure, protective dyke, and reinforced concrete irrigation delivery sump, and preparation of a Dam Safety Review and Dam Safety Management Plan;
  4. Review of the canal network, hydraulic structures, and drainage design, and preparation/reconciliation of complete construction drawings (AutoCAD and PDF);
  5. Review, verification, and reconciliation of the Bill of Engineering Measurement and Evaluation (BEME), inclusive of VAT and appropriate contingencies, and value engineering to approach the World Bank benchmark unit cost of USD 8,000/ha;
  6. Update of the economic and financial analysis (NPV, IRR, benefit-cost ratio, sensitivity analysis) with measures to achieve a positive economic return;
  7. Review and strengthening of institutional arrangements for Water Users Associations and Participatory Irrigation Management, incorporation of domestic/livestock water access and canal protection measures, and confirmation of compliance with World Bank Environmental and Social Standards;
  8. Climate resilience assessment, asset management planning, construction methodology and procurement-readiness review, and preparation of an Operation and Maintenance Framework.

The full Terms of Reference (TOR) describing the detailed scope, methodology, deliverables, and reporting requirements will be provided to shortlisted firms.

3. Duration of the Assignment

The assignment is expected to be completed within a total period of fourteen (14) weeks from the date of commencement.

4. Qualification Requirements

The Client now invites eligible consulting firms ("Consultants") to indicate their interest in providing the above-described services. Interested Consultants must provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the services. The shortlisting criteria are as follows:

  1. General experience of the firm in irrigation, dam/water conservation structure design, and design review assignments, with a minimum of ten (10) years' relevant corporate experience;
  2. Specific experience of the firm in at least three (3) similar assignments (detailed design, design review, or rehabilitation design of irrigation and/or dam/water conservation infrastructure) completed within the last ten (10) years, of comparable scope and complexity, preferably in Nigeria or West Africa, including at least one assignment financed by the World Bank or another multilateral development bank;
  3. Demonstrated capacity to field a multi-disciplinary team covering, at a minimum: irrigation/dam engineering, hydraulic and structural engineering, hydrology and water resources, geotechnical engineering, quantity surveying/cost engineering, agricultural economics, institutional/Participatory Irrigation Management, environmental and social safeguards, and digital engineering/GIS;
  4. Sound financial standing and availability of key professional, technical, and administrative staff and resources to carry out the assignment within the stipulated timeframe;
  5. Evidence of compliance with World Bank Environmental and Social Framework requirements on prior similar assignments, where applicable.

Consultants may associate with other firms in the form of a joint venture or a sub-consultancy to enhance their qualifications. In the case of a joint venture, all members shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire assignment, and the Expression of Interest shall clearly identify the lead firm and the roles of each member.

5. Submission Requirements

Interested Consultants should submit the following information:

  • A letter of expression of interest;
  • Company/firm profile, including registration/incorporation documents and evidence of legal status;

  • Organisational chart and an indicative list of key professional staff available for the assignment, with a summary of their qualifications (detailed CVs are not required at this stage);
  • Evidence of financial capacity (e.g., audited financial statements for the last three years or a statement from a recognised financial institution); and
  • A statement confirming the firm's (and any joint venture partners') eligibility and absence of conflict of interest, in accordance with the World Bank's Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers.

Attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraph 3.14, 3.16, 3.17 and Annex VI of the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (Fifth Edition, September 2023, or the edition applicable to the Financing Agreement), setting out the World Bank's policy on conflict of interest.

6. Selection Method

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Consultant Qualification Selection (CQS) method set out in the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers. A shortlist of approximately four (4) firms will be prepared from the Expressions of Interest received, and shortlisted firms will subsequently be invited to submit technical and financial proposals through a Request for Proposals (RFP).

7. Submission of Expressions of Interest

Expressions of interest, in English, marked "Expression of Interest Detailed Design Review of the Kware Irrigation Scheme" and quoting the Reference Number above, must be delivered in a sealed envelope (or, where permitted, by e-mail) to the address below not later than 22th oct 2026 at 12;00pm

notice_text: République du Tchad.                                          Unité-Travail -Progrès                                                                            Préssidence de la république Primature Ministere de l'Eau et de l'Energie Commission de Passation des Marchés   Projet d'Accroissement de l'Accès à l'Énergie au Tchad   Appel d’Offres N° : TD-CEAS-520614-GO-RFB Accord(s)-Cadre(s) pour Fournitures (Procédure Primaire d’Acquisition à deux (2) Enveloppes) Agence d’Acquisition :  Cellule d'Exécution du Projet d'Accroissement de l'Accès à l'Énergie au Tchad (CEP-MEE), agissant pour le compte du Ministère de l'Eau et de l'Énergie Pays :                              République du Tchad Nom du Projet :             Projet d’Accroissement de l’Accès à l’ Énergie. (PAAET) au Tchad N° Don :                         IDA D985-TD – P174495 Titre: Accords-Cadres pour Fournitures installation et maintenance des systèmes solaires autonomes (SSS) pour l’électrification des centres de santé et des écoles en quatre (04) lots AO N° : TD-CEAS-520614-GO-RFB Émis le : 21 octobre 2026   La République du Tchad a reçu un financement de la Banque mondiale pour financer le Projet d’Accroissement de l’Accès à l’Énergie au Tchad (PAAET) et a l’intention d’utiliser une partie de ce Don pour effectuer des paiements au titre des Commandes susceptibles d’être attribuées dans le cadre des Accords-Cadres (AC) relatifs à la fourniture, à l’installation et à la maintenance des systèmes solaires autonomes (SSS) pour l’électrification des centres de santé et des écoles, conclus à l’issue d’une Procédure Primaire de Passation de Marché. Pour ces marchés, l’Emprunteur effectuera les paiements en recourant à la méthode de décaissement par paiement direct, telle que définie dans les Directives de la Banque mondiale applicables aux décaissements dans le cadre de financements de projets d’investissement, sauf pour les paiements pour lesquels le marché prévoit l’utilisation d’une lettre de crédit. L’Agence d’Acquisition conduit la Procédure Primaire de Passation de Marché en vue de conclure des Accords-Cadres. L’Agence d’Acquisition est la seule Agence d’Acquisition en vertu de ces Accords-Cadres. Elle sollicite des Offres sous plis scellés de la part de Soumissionnaires éligibles pour la fourniture et l’installation des systèmes solaires autonomes (SSS) destinés à l’électrification des centres de santé et des écoles en quatre (04) lots. Les quantités prévues au titre de la Procédure primaire concernent 436 écoles et 256 centres de santé. Des quantités additionnelles estimatives, portant sur 153 écoles et 434 centres de santé, pourront être commandées ultérieurement, selon les besoins, au moyen de Commandes subséquentes passées dans le cadre des Accords-Cadres. Les Accords-Cadres à conclure seront à utilisateur unique. L’unique Acheteur autorisé à passer des Commandes en vertu des Accords-Cadres est la Cellule d’Exécution du Projet d’Accroissement de l’Accès à l’Énergie au Tchad (CEP-PAAET), agissant pour le compte du Ministère de l’Eau et de l’Énergie. Les Accords-Cadres à conclure seront à Fournisseurs Multiples . La sélection d’un Fournisseur dans le cadre d’un Accord-Cadre pour l’attribution de Commandes sera effectuée par une Procédure Secondaire de Passation de Marché, telle que définie dans l’Accord-Cadre. Les modalités détaillées de la procédure secondaire sont décrites dans les accord-cadres . Toutefois, la conclusion de l’Accord-Cadre n’imposera aucune obligation à l’Agence d’Acquisition d’acquérir les Fournitures par Commandes subséquentes. La conclusion de l’Accord-Cadre ne garantit pas qu’un Fournisseur ayant signé un Accord-Cadre sera attributaire d’une ou de plusieurs Commandes L’appel d’offres sera conduit par mise en concurrence internationale en recourant à un Appel d’Offres (AO) telle que définie dans le «  Règlement de la Banque mondiale applicables aux Emprunteurs – Passation des Marchés dans le cadre du financement de projets d’investissement, 6ème Edition de février 2025 (« le Règlement de passation des Marchés ») et est ouvert à tous les Soumissionnaires éligibles tels que définis dans le Règlement de passation des marchés. Les Offres seront évaluées conformément au processus d'évaluation défini dans le dossier d'appel d'offres. Les pondérations suivantes s'appliqueront aux Critères notés (y compris les facteurs techniques et autres que le prix) : 70% pour la partie technique et 30 % pour le coût de l'Offre. Les Soumissionnaires peuvent remettre une Offre pour un ou plus des lots ci-après : N° lots Qté Kits SSS Quantités de la Procédure  Primaire Quantités additionnelles estimatives au titre de l’Accord-Cadre Province Services Qté Ec. Qté CS Qté Ec. Qté CS Lot 1 289 46 84 17 142 Wadi Fira, Salamat, Sila, Ennedi Est, Ennedi Ouest et Tibesti. Fourniture Installation Maintenance Lot 2 328 137 53 48 90 N’Djamena, Hadjer-Lamis, Barh-El-Ghazel, Kanem, Lac et Borkou Lot 3 242 96 42 33 71 Chari Baguirmi, Mayo Kebbi Est, Mayo Kebbi Ouest et Tandjilé. Lot 4 420 157 77 55 131 Logone Oriental, Mandoul, Moyen Chari et Logone Occidental. TOTAL 1 279 436 256 153 434     Les quantités indiquées au titre de la Procédure primaire correspondent aux besoins initiaux prévus. Les quantités additionnelles estimatives au titre de l’Accord-Cadre pourront faire l’objet de Commandes subséquentes, selon les besoins de l’Agence d’Acquisition, pendant la durée de validité des Accords-Cadres. Elles ne constituent pas un engagement ferme de commande Les Accords-Cadres seront conclus pour une durée initiale de douze (12) mois à compter de leur date d’entrée en vigueur. Les Commandes subséquentes préciseront les délais de fourniture, d’installation, de réception, ainsi que les obligations de garantie, de maintenance et d’entretien applicables. La durée initiale des Accords-Cadres pourra être prorogée conformément aux dispositions du Dossier d’Appel d’Offres et des Accords-Cadres. La Procédure Primaire de Passation de Marché établira un ou plusieurs Accords-Cadres fermés. Aucun nouveau fournisseur ne pourra être admis dans les Accords-Cadres pendant leur durée de validité. Les Soumissionnaires intéressés et éligibles peuvent obtenir des informations et prendre connaissance des documents d’Appel d’Offres auprès de la de la Cellule d’Exécution de Projet du Ministère de l’Eau et de l’Energie, sise au quartier Diguel Est, derrière l’Hôtel de l’Amitié, immeuble contigu à la Pharmacie Humanité BAH CHIGUERI, tél. : +235 85 42 73 79 / +235 98 80 15 06, courriel : daossscep1@yahoo.com, de 7 heures 00 à 15 heures 30 minutes les jours ouvrables, et les vendredis de 7 heures 00 à 12 heures 00, heure locale. Le Dossier d’Appel d’Offres en français peut être acheté par tout Soumissionnaire intéressé, sur demande écrite adressée à l’adresse indiquée ci-dessous, contre paiement d’un montant non remboursable de cent cinquante mille francs CFA (150 000 XAF), ou de l’équivalent dans une monnaie librement convertible. Le paiement s’effectuera en espèces auprès de la comptabilité de la CEP-MEE contre récépissé. Pour tout autre mode de paiement, les Soumissionnaires peuvent se renseigner auprès de la comptabilité aux numéros de téléphone suivants : +235 85 42 73 79 / +235 98 80 15 06. Pour les Soumissionnaires étrangers souhaitant recevoir le dossier physique par DHL ou tout autre service d’expédition, les frais d’expédition seront à leur charge. Les Offres devront être déposées à l’adresse indiquée ci-dessous au plus tard le [date à compléter] 2026 à 10 heures 00, heure de N’Djamena. La soumission des Offres par voie électronique ne sera pas autorisée. Les Offres remises en retard ne seront pas acceptées. Toute Offre reçue après l’expiration du délai limite de dépôt des Offres sera rejetée.    L’Offre devra comprendre deux Parties, à savoir la Partie Technique et la Partie Financière. Les enveloppes extérieures des Offres marquées « OFFRE ORIGINALE » ainsi que les enveloppes intérieures marquées « PARTIE TECHNIQUE » seront ouvertes publiquement, en présence des représentants des Soumissionnaires et des personnes présentes, à l’adresse indiquée ci-dessous, le 22 décembre 2026 à 10 heures 00, heure de N’Djamena. Toutes les enveloppes marquées « SECONDE ENVELOPPE - PARTIE FINANCIÈRE » devront rester fermées et seront conservées en lieu sûr par l’Agence d’Acquisition jusqu’à la seconde ouverture publique. Une attention particulière doit être portée au Règlement de Passation de Marchés qui exige que l’Emprunteur divulgue les informations sur la propriété effective du bénéficiaire , en même temps que la publication de la notification de l’attribution de l’accord cadre, en utilisant le Formulaire de Divulgation des Bénéficiaires Effectifs inclut dans le Dossier d’Appel d’Offres. L’adresse à laquelle, il est fait référence ci-dessus est:   MINISTERE DE L’EAU ET DE L’ENERGIE PROJET D’ACCROISSEMENT DE L’ACCES A L’ENERGIE AU TCHAD (PAAET ) Cellule d’Exécution de Projets du Ministère de l’Eau et de l’Energie, (CEP-MEE)         Adresse : Quartier DIGUEL EST derrière l’hôtel de l’amitié, Immeuble collé à la Pharmacie Humanité BAH CHIGUERI Tél :             +235 85 42 73 79 / +235 98 80 15 06 Ville :             N’Djaména Pays :             Tchad E-mail :           daossscep1@yahoo.com   Le Secrétaire Général du Ministère de l’Eau et de l’Energie   NOUR SALEH HAGGAR

notice_text:     Appel à cotations pour Fournitures (Processus à Une Enveloppe)   No : CI-PDC2V-558138-GO-RFQ Pays :   République de Côte d’Ivoire Acheteur : Unité de Coordination du Projet de Développement des Chaines de Valeur Vivrières (UC-PDC2V) Projet : Projet de Développement des Chaines de Valeur Vivrières (PDC2V) No Crédit: Crédit IDA N°69080               Intitulé du Marché : Acquisition d'équipements supplémentaires nécessaires pour l'accréditation du LANADA Emis le :  21 Octobre 2025   La République de Côte d’Ivoire a reçu un crédit de l’Association Internationale pour le Développement pour financer le Projet de Développement des Chaines de Valeur Vivrières (PDC2V) , et à l’intention d’utiliser une partie de ce crédit pour effectuer des paiements au titre du Marché relatif à l’acquisition d'équipements supplémentaires nécessaires pour l'accréditation du LANADA. L’Unité de Coordination du PDC2V sollicite des offres fermées de la part de soumissionnaires éligibles et répondant aux qualifications requises pour fournir les équipements techniques nécessaires à l’accréditation du LANADA . La passation du Marché sera conduite par Mise en Concurrence nationale telle que définie dans le «  Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d’Investissement  » de la Banque mondiale de septembre 2025 , et ouvert à tous les soumissionnaires de pays éligibles tels que définis dans ledit Règlement. Les soumissionnaires éligibles et intéressés peuvent obtenir des informations auprès de l’Unité de Coordination du PDC2V aux adresses suivantes : (Voir Mme KOUABENAN SOLOU Edwige, Spécialiste en Passation des marchés) ; edwige. solou@pdc2v.ci avec copie à patrick.kramo@pdc2v.ci  et examiner le Dossier d’Appel à cotations ou prendre connaissance du dossier à l’adresse mentionnée ci-dessous de 8 heures à 12 heures et de 14 heures à 17 heures, Temps Universel . Les Soumissionnaires intéressés et éligibles peuvent obtenir gratuitement un dossier de demande de cotations en formulant une demande écrite à l’adresse mentionnée ci-dessous. Les cotations devront être soumises à l’adresse ci-dessous au plus tard le jeudi 5 novembre 2025 à 10 heures précises temps universel. La soumission des offres par voie électronique ne sera pas autorisée. Les cotations remises en retard ne seront pas acceptées . Les offres seront ouvertes en présence des représentants des soumissionnaires présents en personne à la salle de réunions du siège du PDC2V sis à l’adresse indiquée ci-dessous, le jeudi 5 novembre 2025 à 10 heures 30 minutes temps universel. L’adresse à laquelle il est fait référence ci-dessus est :  Unité de Coordination du Projet des Chaînes de Valeurs Vivrières (UC-PDC2V), Abidjan Cocody , Rue de la Canebière, Non loin de L’ambassade d’Italie, Voir Mme KOUABENAN SOLOU Edwige, Spécialiste en Passation des Marchés Tél : (+225) 27 24 34 40 75 Email : edwige. solou@pdc2v.ci
