notice_text: Renewable Energy Generation and Access INcrease Project (REGAIN) Grant No.: E331-MH REGAIN Project Reference No. MH-MEC-563965-CS-CQS October 26, 2026 The Government of the Republic of the Marshall Islands (GRMI) has received financing from the International Development Association (IDA) (the “Bank”) in the form of a grant (hereinafter called “the Grant”), in the amount of US$60 million, toward the cost of the Renewable Energy Generation and Access Increase (REGAIN) Project (P181250), approved and effective as of December 13, 2024, with a closing date of September 30, 2030. The Marshalls Energy Company (MEC), as Employer and implementing agency, intends to apply a portion of the proceeds of the Grant to eligible payments under a contract for consulting services to prepare and support an implementation plan for renewable energy, energy efficiency and e-mobility under the Energy Act, 2025 and the National Energy Authority Act, 2025, excluding petroleum-sector provisions, under Sub-Component 3.1 (Sector Development Assistance) of the REGAIN Project. The assignment shall be carried out in close coordination with the newly established National Energy Authority (NEA) and shall cover all MEC-served systems, including Majuro, Ebeye and the outer islands. The consulting services (“the Services”) comprise proposing activities to be undertaken in the short, medium, and long term and undertaking them to strengthen the capacity of key energy sector stakeholders by focusing on regulation, target setting, monitoring tools, dissemination of progress, feedback, and course correction to promote security, safety, reliability, and sustainability of energy supply (excluding petroleum) in RMI as per the provisions of the EA 2025 and aligned with the National Energy Authority Act, 2025. Services include, among others: • Diagnostic review of the Electricity Sector (in particular RE, EE and E-Mobility) of the Marshall Islands; • Strategic review of the applicable RMI’s electricity sector-related international and national commitments and targets; • Propose a strategy for addressing the identified gaps; • Assessing the Institutional structure and the manpower requirements of the Energy sector; • Monitoring, Database and Reporting Framework for RE; • Electricity tariff review and recommendations, building on MEC’s existing tariff methodology and extending it to Ebeye; and • Addressing the recommendations by preparing, revising, or aligning the policies, regulations, codes, guidelines, and other instruments required to give effect to the relevant provisions of the Energy Act, 2025 and the National Energy Authority Act, 2025, excluding petroleum-sector provisions. The assignment is structured as a lump-sum contract with an estimated duration of 9 months, with an expected start date in January 2027. The selected firm will nominate a multidisciplinary team, including the Key Experts described in the attached TOR, and will report to MEC, coordinating closely with NEA, the World Bank, and other relevant stakeholders. The Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment are attached to this Request for Expressions of Interest. MEC now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria, as set out in Section 10 of the attached TOR, are: 1. Experience preparing energy-sector legal, policy and regulatory frameworks, or implementation plans for energy legislation, including regulations, codes and licensing (35 points) 2. Experience in electricity tariff, cost-of-service and revenue-requirement studies for small island or multi- system utilities, preferably with high renewable energy penetration (25 points) 3 3. Experience in the Pacific or other Small Island Developing States (25 points) 4. Technical and managerial capability of the firm, including core business, years in business, organization and availability of relevant expertise (15 points) The Consultant shall demonstrate availability of qualified experts in energy policy and regulation (renewable energy, energy efficiency and e-mobility), legal and regulatory drafting, electricity tariffs and utility finance, and stakeholder engagement. Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. In addition, please refer to the following specific information on conflict of interest related to this assignment: Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all partners shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected. A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Selection based on Consultant’s Qualifications (CQS) method set out in the World Bank Regulations for IPF-Borrowers, September 2025 Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours, 0900 to 1700 hours, Monday to Friday. Expressions of Interest EOI must be delivered in electronic form to the address below by November 23, 2026, 5:00 pm Majuro time. MEC: Attn: Steve Wakefield PO Box 1439, Majuro MH 96960 Republic of the Marshall Islands Tel: 692-625-3827/3829 E-mail: swakefield@mecrmi.com Copy: Jack Chong-Gum, jack.chonggum@mecrmi.net EOI Submission Requirements: Expressions of Interest should include the following information: 1. Firm profile 2. Organizational Capacity 3. Relevant assignments (maximum 10 projects), preferably including energy-sector regulatory, energy legislation implementation or tariff assignments in small island states. 4. Information addressing each of the shortlisting criteria 5. Company registration documents Page Limit: Maximum 15 pages excluding registration documents. Submissions beyond the maximum page limit of 15 pages will not be considered. Yours sincerely, 4 Jack Chong-Gum CEO , Marshalls Energy Company jack.chonggum@mecrmi.net 5 Republic of the Marshall Islands Marshalls Energy Company (MEC) Terms of Reference (TOR) Implementation Plan for Renewable Energy, Energy Efficiency and E-Mobility under the Energy Act, 2025 and National Energy Authority Act, 2025, excluding Petroleum Provisions – REGAIN Project Project ID: P181250 Assignment Type: International Firm (Lump sum Contract) Duration: 9 Months Location: Remote with Periodic Missions to Majuro 1. Background The Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI) is one of the world's smallest and most isolated nations. The country consists of 29 atolls and 5 low coral islands situated on about 181 square kilometers (km 2 ) of land mass in the Pacific Ocean. Majuro (the nation's capital) and Ebeye, the country's two largest urban centers, account for about 96 percent of the total population, while the remaining inhabitants live on the outer atolls. The Government of the Republic of the Marshall Islands (GRMI) depends mostly on diesel generation to meet the country's growing electricity needs. The country aims to enhance its energy security through renewable energy generation, improve the reliability of electricity supply, enhance energy efficiency, expand e-mobility, and improve access to electricity. Increased energy resilience will reduce dependence on hydrocarbon fuels, insulate the country from the risks of price rises and supply uncertainties, and equip it with natural disaster-resilient electricity infrastructure. MEC, the state-owned energy utility, generates and provides electricity to Majuro Atoll, serving 55 percent of RMI's population. MEC also manages three mini-grids in Jaluit, Wotje, Rongrong (Majuro Atoll), and Kili Island, the latter having been recently transferred to MEC from the Kili Bikini Ejit (KBE) Local Government. Following the integration of the Kwajalein Atoll Joint Utilities Resources (KAJUR) into MEC, MEC is also responsible for power generation and distribution in Ebeye, together with the water and sewerage services previously provided by KAJUR. MEC is responsible for executing plans to enhance energy security but lacks the capability to conceive and implement them. It lacks the funds required to implement these plans. The Government of the Republic of the Marshall Islands (GRMI) has partnered with the World Bank through the Renewable Energy Generation and Access Increase Project (REGAIN) – an IDA grant of US$60 million approved and effective as of December 13, 2024, with a closing date of September 30, 2030. The REGAIN project aims to increase renewable energy generation and improve access to electricity while reducing reliance on diesel-based generation through funding and technical support. RMI’s Electricity Roadmap targets net-zero greenhouse gas emissions and 100% renewable electricity by 2050. As a small and geographically dispersed island nation, RMI remains highly dependent on imported diesel for electricity generation, exposing the country to high energy costs and vulnerability to global fuel price shocks and supply disruptions. To manage this risk, RMI needs to diversify its electricity supply portfolio by 6 integrating more RE, manage demand growth by promoting efficient electricity use, pursue new business opportunities such as EVs, and monitor and report implementation status to the GRMI for appropriate course correction. Ensuring a reliable, clean, and cost-effective electricity supply is therefore critical to achieving national climate commitments, strengthening energy security, and supporting sustainable socio-economic development. The country lacks the legal, policy, and regulatory framework, institutional capability, and the trained manpower required to achieve these objectives. The GRMI has taken some steps in this direction, such as the notification of the Energy Act 2025, which provides a legal, policy, regulatory, and organizational framework to promote security, safety, reliability, and sustainability of energy supply for the benefit of RMI’s economy and citizens and to promote the efficient use of energy and of energy from indigenous sources. Under Sub-Component 3.1 of the REGAIN project (Sector Development Assistance), MEC plans to seek consultancy support from a firm to propose a roadmap and undertake proposed activities for the Implementation of the Energy Act (IEA) 2025. In the roadmap, IEA shall propose activities to be undertaken in the short, medium, and long term and undertake them to strengthen the capacity of key energy sector stakeholders by focusing on regulation, target setting, monitoring tools, dissemination of progress, feedback, and course correction to promote security, safety, reliability, and sustainability of energy supply in RMI. IEA shall be prepared in close coordination with the newly established National Energy Authority (NEA) and MEC. IEA shall take into account all Acts, policies, regulations, studies and current practices relevant to electricity (all RE included), Energy Efficiency, E-mobility and their funding, including but not limited to: Energy Act 2025 National Energy Authority Act, 2025 Recommendations contained in Integrated Resource and Resilience Plan 2024-2034 Electricity Roadmap of 2018, which provides a relevant and guiding framework for the sector’s development MEC’s current tariff methodology and tariff model, prepared by MEC’s Supplemental Management and Operations (SMO) consultant under ADB-funded technical assistance, which covers MEC’s operations prior to the integration of KAJUR and on which the tariff review under Task 6 shall build National Targets and the progress achieved against them to date Relevant energy sector programs and studies of other development partners active in the RMI, in particular the Asian Development Bank (ADB), such as the Energy Transition Project, should be taken into account to ensure coordination and avoid duplication. The assignment will support GRMI, MEC, and NEA in translating the Energy Act, 2025, and the National Energy Authority Act, 2025, into an actionable implementation plan for renewable energy, energy efficiency, and e-mobility. The assignment will identify required policy, regulatory, institutional, monitoring, and capacity- building actions, while excluding provisions related to the petroleum sector. This support aligns with REGAIN’s institutional strengthening objectives and RMI’s need to reduce reliance on diesel, improve energy security, and support the integration of renewable energy. 7 2. Objectives The objective of the assignment is to prepare a practical, time-bound implementation plan for renewable energy, energy efficiency, and e-mobility under the Energy Act, 2025, and the National Energy Authority Act, 2025, excluding petroleum-sector provisions, and to support the preparation of priority policy, regulatory, institutional, monitoring, and capacity-building instruments required for implementation. Institutional strengthening for the implementation of RE, EE, and e-mobility provisions. Policy and regulatory framework, guidelines for the development of higher RE integration, EE promotion, and e-mobility uptake. Monitoring and reporting framework for RE, EE, and e-mobility targets, progress, and implementation gaps. Database/reporting arrangements for RE, EE, and e-mobility information. Capacity development strategy for institutions, utilities, and local manpower. 3. Project Description This assignment is financed by the World Bank under the institutional strengthening and implementation support activities of REGAIN. It will support the policy, regulatory, institutional, monitoring, and capacity- building measures required to implement the RE, EE, and E-mobility provisions of the Energy Act, 2025, and the National Energy Authority Act, 2025. 4. Implementation Arrangements MEC will be the Employer and the contracting authority for this assignment, responsible for approving deliverables and payments. The Consultant may proceed to the next deliverable under MEC's general guidance. NEA, as the statutory authority responsible for regulating the energy sector, shall be responsible for the technical and regulatory approval of policy- and regulation-driven deliverables. MEC, as Employer, retains ultimate authority for administrative and financial approval and for the release of REGAIN project funds, which shall follow NEA's technical sign-off on the relevant deliverable. The responsible ministry and Cabinet shall be consulted where recommendations require policy approval, regulatory adoption, statutory action, budget allocation, or cross-government implementation. MEC shall be responsible for formal approval of all deliverables and payments. The Consultant shall work under the direction of MEC and coordinate closely with: MEC management and technical staff REGAIN Project Management Services Consultant, as applicable Project Implementation Unit (PMU) within MEC NEA, the national regulatory body, serving as the regulatory interface between MEC and the Consultant Responsible Ministry and Cabinet on policy formulation World Bank on matters requiring no-objection, reporting, or implementation support ADB and other development partners active in RMI's energy sector, as relevant Petroleum-sector implementation matters are excluded from this assignment. 8 5. Scope of Services The scope of services is limited to the electricity sector, in particular renewable energy, energy efficiency, and e- mobility, including relevant non-petroleum legal, policy, regulatory, institutional, monitoring, enforcement, data, and capacity-building provisions necessary for their implementation. Petroleum sector related provisions of the Energy Act, 2025, are excluded from the assignment. While MEC is the Contracting Employer for the entire assignment, NEA serves as the primary technical Client for Tasks 1, 2, 3, and 7, given their statutory and regulatory content. MEC's approval of these deliverables is administrative and financial and follows NEA's technical acceptance. Task 1: Diagnostic review of the Electricity Sector (in particular RE, EE and E-Mobility) of the Marshall Islands The Consultant shall review and map the existing institutional arrangement, policy, and regulatory framework against the provisions and the directions contained in the Energy Act (EA) 2025 and the National Energy Authority (NEA) Act 2025 (harmonious reading) for the development of Renewable Energy (RE), Energy Efficiency (EE), and E-Mobility (E-MB). The Consultant will propose a strategy to address misaligned or missing institutional arrangements, policies, and regulatory framework. (i) Review of existing applicable policies, strategies, plans, and studies in the context of the requirements of EA 2025 and NEA Act 2025, (ii) Identify whether the gap is institutional, policy, or regulatory, whether it will be addressed within the existing framework (alignment/modification), or whether a new framework is to be created, and (iii) Recommend a broad policy, regulatory, and Institutional framework to address these gaps. Task 2: Strategic review of the applicable RMI’s electricity sector related international and national commitments and targets The Consultant will undertake a focused review of the GRMI's international commitments, national targets, initiatives for the development of RE, EE, and E-MB, and the progress achieved. The diagnostic and strategic review will include the following: (i) Discussion with the stakeholders and ascertaining reasons for the shortfall in the envisaged progress, (ii) The Consultant shall review relevant national targets, international commitments, ongoing initiatives, and selected comparable Pacific/SIDS practices for RE, EE, and e-mobility implementation. The purpose of the review shall be to identify practical options for policy, regulatory, institutional, monitoring, and capacity-building measures suitable for RMI, (iii) Identification of implementation gaps, in particular critical legal, policy, regulatory, and institutional gaps, which impacted the achievements of these initiatives and targets, (iv) Assess whether these legal, policy, and regulatory gaps stem from implementation shortfall or a missing framework, and (v) Recommend a broad policy, regulatory, and institutional framework to address these gaps. Task 3: Propose a strategy for addressing the identified gaps The Consultant will propose a strategy with a time-bound implementation roadmap for addressing the gaps identified in Tasks 1 and 2. The proposed strategy will include the following: (i) Identification of Implementation gaps, i.e., the framework/provision exists but has not been implemented, or there is a shortfall in its implementation, (ii) Identification of gaps in the existing framework, i.e., the legal, policy, regulatory, or Institutional framework provides for the enabling provision, but it has not been enacted or notified; indicate whether it is a policy, regulatory, or institutional issue, 9 (iii) Identify misalignment (even a section or provision of it) of the policy, regulatory framework, or the institutional framework with the EA 2025 and NEA 2025, (iv) Identification of gaps that cannot be dealt with by the existing framework, (v) Recommendation of a strategy to deal with these identified gaps. The proposed strategy will indicate the required interventions (legal, policy, regulatory and institutional), their implementation order, the stakeholders responsible for addressing them and the timelines within which these will be addressed (short term- within 3 months, medium term- within 6 months and long term-within 12 months) duly aligned with the statutory timelines provided in the Acts and related policies, (vi) Indicate how the recommended interventions will address the identified gaps. (vii) Indicate the way forward for the gaps which cannot be addressed under the existing legal framework, and (viii) Develop a comprehensive implementation roadmap considering the recommendations made in Task 2 and in this Task, and compile the recommendations. The roadmap should indicate: Short-term actions, Medium-term actions, Long-term actions, Responsible institution, Required decision or instrument, Dependency, Level of priority, and Whether the consultant will draft the instrument under this assignment. Task 4: Assessing the Institutional structure and the manpower requirements of the sector The Consultant will examine whether the current institutional structure, including its roles and responsibilities, aligns with those prescribed in the Energy Act and is conducive to the development of RE, EE, and E-MB in RMI. The Consultant will examine the following: (i) Clarity in their role and responsibilities (without any overlap) for the development of RE, EE, and E- MB, (ii) The institutional capacity to lead the development of RE, EE, and E-MB in RMI, such as project planning, design, implementation, operation, and maintenance, and (iii) Recommendations for addressing institutional alignment of roles and responsibilities, capacity gaps, and the coordination mechanism between them for the development of RE, EE, and E-MB, taking into account the integration of KAJUR’s operations into MEC. The Consultant will also assess the skills and the manpower required for the development of RE, EE, and E-MB in RMI. The Consultant shall assess: (i) Manpower and the skills available with all important stakeholders, (ii) Assess the manpower and the skill requirements considering the national targets and the evolving (proposed Roadmap) legal, policy, regulatory and institutional framework for the development of RE, EE and E-MB for the next 5 years, (iii) Indicate the gaps between availability and requirements, and (iv) Prepare a strategy to meet this gap, indicating the number, the skill requirements, and how the required skills will be met (contents of the training, how and where the training will be provided, suggestions for international collaboration, certification). 10 Task 5: Monitoring, Database and Reporting Framework for RE The Consultant will assess the status of the RE database to determine its suitability for publishing a report that records, documents, and shares critical information on RE, EE, and E-MB. The Consultant will: (i) Evaluate the existing database and identify the missing indicators/information gap/data field necessary for various stakeholders to discharge their roles and responsibilities for the development of RE, EE, and E-MB in the country (covering Majuro, Ebeye and the outer island systems), (ii) Recommend formats, information to be gathered, sources of this information, reporting institutions, reporting frequency, and validation process, (iii) Recommend the structure of the report to be published, and (iv) Prepare the first RE encompassing the above recommendations, which NEA can subsequently update and improve upon. Task 6: Electricity tariff review and recommendations The tariff review shall build on, and not duplicate, MEC’s current tariff methodology and tariff model prepared by the SMO consultant. It shall focus on how that methodology has performed in practice, on areas it did not examine in depth, and on extending it to all systems now operated by MEC, including Ebeye following the integration of KAJUR’s operations into MEC, which was not covered by the earlier work. The review shall also provide MEC and NEA with a clear, evidence-based rationale and supporting calculations for the recommended tariff options, so that they are well prepared to respond to tariff proposals from policymakers, investors and other stakeholders. The Consultant shall review the existing electricity tariff arrangements and prepare recommendations and an implementation pathway that are consistent with the Energy Act, 2025, and the National Energy Authority Act, 2025. The Consultant shall, in particular: (i) Assess the adequacy of the current tariff level, structure, adjustment mechanisms, billing arrangements and related subsidy or compensation mechanisms; (ii) Assess the revenue requirement and efficient cost of electricity service, based on verified utility financial, operational and investment data; (iii) Determine the extent to which prevailing tariffs and practices align with the principles contemplated under the relevant sections of the Energy Act; (iv) Assess tariff implications of planned renewable energy, EE, E-mobility, battery storage, network, resilience and access investments; (v) Recommend refinements to the existing tariff methodology, tariff structure, adjustment mechanism and regulatory review process that NEA can use in tariff determinations; (vi) Review the application of MEC’s current tariff methodology and identify any issues, anomalies or unintended outcomes that have emerged in practice and that may require adjustment; (vii) Extend the revenue-requirement and cost-of-supply analysis to Ebeye following the integration of KAJUR’s operations into MEC, including harmonization of KAJUR’s financial, operational and customer data with MEC’s, clear separation of electricity costs from water and sewerage costs, and options and a transition pathway for bringing Ebeye’s electricity tariff into MEC’s tariff framework; (viii) Assess the merits and implications of the planned introduction of a single tariff for all customer classes; (ix) Assess whether a uniform national tariff should be maintained across all MEC-served systems (Majuro, Ebeye and the outer islands), or whether location-specific tariffs or tariff adjustment factors are warranted, including the resulting cross-subsidies between locations; 11 (x) Using the known sizes and costs of the hybrid and mini-grid systems to be installed in the outer islands, estimate the indicative cost of supply and potential tariff for each location, and assess the implications of any proposal to reduce tariffs in locations with high renewable energy penetration; (xi) Assess the practicality, timing and customer impact of reducing or removing existing government subsidies, and the alternatives available; (xii) Assess the feasibility of time-of-use tariffs that reflect the different costs of daytime (predominantly solar) and nighttime (predominantly diesel) supply; (xiii) Recommend tariffs and charging arrangements for electric vehicle charging; (xiv) Assess feed-in tariff, net-metering and power purchase arrangements for privately owned renewable energy systems seeking to export to MEC’s grid, including pricing based on avoided cost, the grid integration, storage and backup costs borne by MEC, and the volume of such generation the grid can accommodate; (xv) Assess the implications of electricity supplied by third parties outside MEC’s networks, such as renewable energy systems at government or private facilities that supply neighboring communities, including the pricing basis and regulatory requirements for such supply, and how differences between their prices and cost-reflective MEC tariffs can be explained and managed; (xvi) Assess distributional and affordability implications for customer classes, including vulnerable customers, and identify transparent options for any subsidy or compensation that may be required; and (xvii) Provide practical inputs for preparation and future implementation of the National Electricity Tariff and Billing Code. Task 7: Addressing the recommendations Based on the approved recommendations and implementation roadmap under Task 3, and working under the technical supervision of NEA, the Consultant shall identify, prepare, revise or align the policies, regulations, codes, guidelines and other instruments required to give effect to the relevant provisions of the Energy Act, 2025 and the National Energy Authority Act, 2025, excluding petroleum-sector provisions. The Consultant shall, in particular: (i) Prepare or align the electricity-sector regulatory instruments identified as necessary under the Acts, including, as applicable, electricity licensing, electricity-sector regulation, Grid Code, service standards, universal service and subsidy-related mechanisms, (ii) Prepare or align the instruments required for renewable energy, including, as applicable, grid integration, renewable IPPs, community renewable-energy projects, rooftop installations and renewable microgrids, (iii) Prepare or align the instruments required for energy efficiency, including applicable standards, labeling requirements, air-conditioning and cooling energy-efficiency requirements, and other EE measures required to implement the applicable provisions of the Acts, (iv) Prepare or align the instruments required for e-mobility, including applicable requirements relating to charging infrastructure, technical standards, charging services, electricity supply and tariff arrangements, and other matters required to implement the applicable provisions of the Acts, and (v) Propose the institutional framework and clearly define the roles and responsibilities of the relevant institutions for implementation. 6. Qualifications, Tasks, and Level of Effort of Specified Key Experts The Consultant shall propose a team adequate for the assignment. In its proposal, the Consultant shall specify: 12 Each proposed key personnel position, The name of the proposed expert, where available, Role and responsibilities, Minimum and actual qualifications and detailed relevant experience, Whether the input is international or national/local, Whether the input is home office or field-based, Estimated level of effort in person-days or person-months, and Anticipated timing of deployment and deployment location(s). At a minimum, the Consultant is expected to consider the inclusion of expertise and an indicative level of effort and split of on-site and remote deployment, as follows: Expert Position Key Tasks / Responsibilities Minimum Qualifications / Experience Int’l / Nat’l Team Leader / Senior Energy Sector Specialist Overall project management and project coordination; lead stakeholder engagement and consultations. Fees and Reimbursable Expenses As this engagement will be structured as a lump-sum contract, the selected Consultant shall submit a financial proposal (in addition to a technical proposal) that includes: A total lump-sum price for the performance of the services, payable against the deliverables set out in Section VIII, supported by a breakdown of professional fees by each proposed expert and personnel category, indicating the applicable unit rates and estimated level of effort (person-months or person-days), provided for information purposes; and 14 Reimbursable expenses, included within the lump-sum price, covering any anticipated travel, accommodation, per diem, logistics, communications, and other project-related costs necessary for the performance of the services. Deliverables The project has six (6) main deliverables. The Consultant shall prepare and submit the following deliverables in accordance with the Scope of Services. The Deliverable shall be submitted within twenty-four weeks of the NTP. 5. Deliverable 5: Electricity Tariff Review and Recommendations (Linked to: Task 6) The Consultant shall prepare a stand-alone Electricity Tariff Review and Recommendations Report, presenting the assessment, findings, and recommended tariff and regulatory pathway in accordance with Task 6. The Deliverable shall be submitted within twenty-six weeks of the NTP. 6. Deliverable 6: Policies, Regulations, Codes and Guidelines for Implementation of the Energy Act (Linked to: Task 7, informed by Tasks 1, 2 and 3) Based on the approved recommendations and implementation roadmap, the Consultant shall prepare and/or align the policies, regulations, codes, and guidelines identified as necessary to implement the relevant provisions of the Energy Act, 2025, and the National Energy Authority Act, 2025, within the scope of the assignment. The deliverable shall comprise the agreed package of new and/or revised policies, regulations, codes and guidelines covering, as applicable: Electricity-sector regulation; Renewable energy; Energy efficiency, including air-conditioning and cooling; and E-mobility. The policies, regulations, codes and guidelines shall be consistent with the gaps, priorities and sequencing established through the preceding Tasks and agreed with NEA and MEC. 16 The Deliverable shall be submitted within thirty-two weeks of the NTP. 9. MEC shall: Provide or facilitate access to relevant technical, operational, customer, commercial, financial and investment information and data, including information required for the tariff review, covering all MEC- served systems including Ebeye (former KAJUR operations), and MEC’s current tariff methodology and tariff model, 17 Provide available plans, studies, reports, databases and information relating to existing and planned RE, EE, e-mobility, storage, and network, Facilitate access to relevant MEC and PMU personnel and stakeholder consultations, and Undertake the contractual, administrative and financial review and approval of deliverables in accordance with the implementation arrangements. The Consultant shall, as part of the Inception Report, submit a consolidated data and information request specifying the information required, its proposed source, format and required date. The Consultant shall promptly identify material data gaps and propose appropriate alternative sources, assumptions or methodologies where required. The provision of information by MEC, NEA or any other stakeholder shall not relieve the Consultant of its responsibility for the verification, analysis, adequacy and quality of the Services and deliverables required under the Contract.

Renewable Energy Generation and Access INcrease Project (REGAIN)

Grant No.: E331-MH
REGAIN Project
Reference No. MH-MEC-563965-CS-CQS

October 26, 2026


The Government of the Republic of the Marshall Islands (GRMI) has received financing from the International
Development Association (IDA) (the “Bank”) in the form of a grant (hereinafter called “the Grant”), in the
amount of US$60 million, toward the cost of the Renewable Energy Generation and Access Increase (REGAIN)
Project (P181250), approved and effective as of December 13, 2024, with a closing date of September 30, 2030.
The Marshalls Energy Company (MEC), as Employer and implementing agency, intends to apply a portion of
the proceeds of the Grant to eligible payments under a contract for consulting services to prepare and support an
implementation plan for renewable energy, energy efficiency and e-mobility under the Energy Act, 2025 and the
National Energy Authority Act, 2025, excluding petroleum-sector provisions, under Sub-Component 3.1
(Sector Development Assistance) of the REGAIN Project. The assignment shall be carried out in close
coordination with the newly established National Energy Authority (NEA) and shall cover all MEC-served
systems, including Majuro, Ebeye and the outer islands.
The consulting services (“the Services”) comprise proposing activities to be undertaken in the short, medium,
and long term and undertaking them to strengthen the capacity of key energy sector stakeholders by focusing on
regulation, target setting, monitoring tools, dissemination of progress, feedback, and course correction to
promote security, safety, reliability, and sustainability of energy supply (excluding petroleum) in RMI as per the
provisions of the EA 2025 and aligned with the National Energy Authority Act, 2025. Services include, among
others:
• Diagnostic review of the Electricity Sector (in particular RE, EE and E-Mobility) of the Marshall Islands;
• Strategic review of the applicable RMI’s electricity sector-related international and national commitments
and targets;
• Propose a strategy for addressing the identified gaps;
• Assessing the Institutional structure and the manpower requirements of the Energy sector;
• Monitoring, Database and Reporting Framework for RE;
• Electricity tariff review and recommendations, building on MEC’s existing tariff methodology and
extending it to Ebeye; and
• Addressing the recommendations by preparing, revising, or aligning the policies, regulations, codes,
guidelines, and other instruments required to give effect to the relevant provisions of the Energy Act, 2025
and the National Energy Authority Act, 2025, excluding petroleum-sector provisions.
The assignment is structured as a lump-sum contract with an estimated duration of 9 months, with an expected
start date in January 2027. The selected firm will nominate a multidisciplinary team, including the Key Experts
described in the attached TOR, and will report to MEC, coordinating closely with NEA, the World Bank, and
other relevant stakeholders.
The Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment are attached to this Request for Expressions of Interest.
MEC now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services.
Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and
relevant experience to perform the Services.
The shortlisting criteria, as set out in Section 10 of the attached TOR, are:
1. Experience preparing energy-sector legal, policy and regulatory frameworks, or implementation plans
for energy legislation, including regulations, codes and licensing (35 points)

system utilities, preferably with high renewable energy penetration (25 points)

Terms of Reference (TOR)

Implementation Plan for Renewable Energy, Energy Efficiency and E-Mobility under the
Energy Act, 2025 and National Energy Authority Act, 2025, excluding Petroleum Provisions –

REGAIN Project

Project ID: P181250
Assignment Type: International Firm (Lump sum Contract)
Duration: 9 Months
Location: Remote with Periodic Missions to Majuro
1. Background
The Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI) is one of the world's smallest and most isolated nations. The
country consists of 29 atolls and 5 low coral islands situated on about 181 square kilometers (km 2 ) of land mass
in the Pacific Ocean. Majuro (the nation's capital) and Ebeye, the country's two largest urban centers, account
for about 96 percent of the total population, while the remaining inhabitants live on the outer atolls. The
Government of the Republic of the Marshall Islands (GRMI) depends mostly on diesel generation to meet the
country's growing electricity needs. The country aims to enhance its energy security through renewable energy
generation, improve the reliability of electricity supply, enhance energy efficiency, expand e-mobility, and
improve access to electricity. Increased energy resilience will reduce dependence on hydrocarbon fuels, insulate
the country from the risks of price rises and supply uncertainties, and equip it with natural disaster-resilient
electricity infrastructure.
MEC, the state-owned energy utility, generates and provides electricity to Majuro Atoll, serving 55 percent of
RMI's population. MEC also manages three mini-grids in Jaluit, Wotje, Rongrong (Majuro Atoll), and Kili
Island, the latter having been recently transferred to MEC from the Kili Bikini Ejit (KBE) Local Government.
Following the integration of the Kwajalein Atoll Joint Utilities Resources (KAJUR) into MEC, MEC is also
responsible for power generation and distribution in Ebeye, together with the water and sewerage services
previously provided by KAJUR. MEC is responsible for executing plans to enhance energy security but lacks
the capability to conceive and implement them. It lacks the funds required to implement these plans. The
Government of the Republic of the Marshall Islands (GRMI) has partnered with the World Bank through the
Renewable Energy Generation and Access Increase Project (REGAIN) – an IDA grant of US$60 million
approved and effective as of December 13, 2024, with a closing date of September 30, 2030. The REGAIN
project aims to increase renewable energy generation and improve access to electricity while reducing reliance
on diesel-based generation through funding and technical support.
RMI’s Electricity Roadmap targets net-zero greenhouse gas emissions and 100% renewable electricity by 2050.
As a small and geographically dispersed island nation, RMI remains highly dependent on imported diesel for
electricity generation, exposing the country to high energy costs and vulnerability to global fuel price shocks
and supply disruptions. To manage this risk, RMI needs to diversify its electricity supply portfolio by

6
integrating more RE, manage demand growth by promoting efficient electricity use, pursue new business
opportunities such as EVs, and monitor and report implementation status to the GRMI for appropriate course
correction. Ensuring a reliable, clean, and cost-effective electricity supply is therefore critical to achieving
national climate commitments, strengthening energy security, and supporting sustainable socio-economic
development. The country lacks the legal, policy, and regulatory framework, institutional capability, and the
trained manpower required to achieve these objectives. The GRMI has taken some steps in this direction, such
as the notification of the Energy Act 2025, which provides a legal, policy, regulatory, and organizational
framework to promote security, safety, reliability, and sustainability of energy supply for the benefit of RMI’s
economy and citizens and to promote the efficient use of energy and of energy from indigenous sources.
Under Sub-Component 3.1 of the REGAIN project (Sector Development Assistance), MEC plans to seek
consultancy support from a firm to propose a roadmap and undertake proposed activities for the Implementation
of the Energy Act (IEA) 2025. In the roadmap, IEA shall propose activities to be undertaken in the short,
medium, and long term and undertake them to strengthen the capacity of key energy sector stakeholders by
focusing on regulation, target setting, monitoring tools, dissemination of progress, feedback, and course
correction to promote security, safety, reliability, and sustainability of energy supply in RMI.
IEA shall be prepared in close coordination with the newly established National Energy Authority (NEA) and
MEC.
IEA shall take into account all Acts, policies, regulations, studies and current practices relevant to electricity (all
RE included), Energy Efficiency, E-mobility and their funding, including but not limited to:
Energy Act 2025
National Energy Authority Act, 2025
Recommendations contained in Integrated Resource and Resilience Plan 2024-2034
Electricity Roadmap of 2018, which provides a relevant and guiding framework for the sector’s
development
MEC’s current tariff methodology and tariff model, prepared by MEC’s Supplemental Management and
Operations (SMO) consultant under ADB-funded technical assistance, which covers MEC’s operations
prior to the integration of KAJUR and on which the tariff review under Task 6 shall build
National Targets and the progress achieved against them to date
Relevant energy sector programs and studies of other development partners active in the RMI, in
particular the Asian Development Bank (ADB), such as the Energy Transition Project, should be taken
into account to ensure coordination and avoid duplication.
The assignment will support GRMI, MEC, and NEA in translating the Energy Act, 2025, and the National
Energy Authority Act, 2025, into an actionable implementation plan for renewable energy, energy efficiency,
and e-mobility. The assignment will identify required policy, regulatory, institutional, monitoring, and capacity-
building actions, while excluding provisions related to the petroleum sector. This support aligns with REGAIN’s
institutional strengthening objectives and RMI’s need to reduce reliance on diesel, improve energy security, and
support the integration of renewable energy.

7
2. Objectives
The objective of the assignment is to prepare a practical, time-bound implementation plan for renewable energy,
energy efficiency, and e-mobility under the Energy Act, 2025, and the National Energy Authority Act, 2025,
excluding petroleum-sector provisions, and to support the preparation of priority policy, regulatory, institutional,
monitoring, and capacity-building instruments required for implementation.

Institutional strengthening for the implementation of RE, EE, and e-mobility provisions.
Policy and regulatory framework, guidelines for the development of higher RE integration, EE
promotion, and e-mobility uptake.
Monitoring and reporting framework for RE, EE, and e-mobility targets, progress, and
implementation gaps.
Database/reporting arrangements for RE, EE, and e-mobility information.
Capacity development strategy for institutions, utilities, and local manpower.

3. Project Description
This assignment is financed by the World Bank under the institutional strengthening and implementation
support activities of REGAIN. It will support the policy, regulatory, institutional, monitoring, and capacity-
building measures required to implement the RE, EE, and E-mobility provisions of the Energy Act, 2025, and
the National Energy Authority Act, 2025.
4. Implementation Arrangements
MEC will be the Employer and the contracting authority for this assignment, responsible for approving
deliverables and payments. The Consultant may proceed to the next deliverable under MEC's general guidance.
NEA, as the statutory authority responsible for regulating the energy sector, shall be responsible for the
technical and regulatory approval of policy- and regulation-driven deliverables. MEC, as Employer, retains
ultimate authority for administrative and financial approval and for the release of REGAIN project funds, which
shall follow NEA's technical sign-off on the relevant deliverable. The responsible ministry and Cabinet shall be
consulted where recommendations require policy approval, regulatory adoption, statutory action, budget
allocation, or cross-government implementation. MEC shall be responsible for formal approval of all
deliverables and payments. The Consultant shall work under the direction of MEC and coordinate closely with:

MEC management and technical staff
REGAIN Project Management Services Consultant, as applicable
Project Implementation Unit (PMU) within MEC
NEA, the national regulatory body, serving as the regulatory interface between MEC and the
Consultant
Responsible Ministry and Cabinet on policy formulation
World Bank on matters requiring no-objection, reporting, or implementation support
ADB and other development partners active in RMI's energy sector, as relevant

Petroleum-sector implementation matters are excluded from this assignment.

8
5. Scope of Services
The scope of services is limited to the electricity sector, in particular renewable energy, energy efficiency, and e-
mobility, including relevant non-petroleum legal, policy, regulatory, institutional, monitoring, enforcement,
data, and capacity-building provisions necessary for their implementation. Petroleum sector related provisions
of the Energy Act, 2025, are excluded from the assignment. While MEC is the Contracting Employer for the
entire assignment, NEA serves as the primary technical Client for Tasks 1, 2, 3, and 7, given their statutory and
regulatory content. MEC's approval of these deliverables is administrative and financial and follows NEA's
technical acceptance.
Task 1: Diagnostic review of the Electricity Sector (in particular RE, EE and E-Mobility) of the Marshall
Islands
The Consultant shall review and map the existing institutional arrangement, policy, and regulatory framework
against the provisions and the directions contained in the Energy Act (EA) 2025 and the National Energy
Authority (NEA) Act 2025 (harmonious reading) for the development of Renewable Energy (RE), Energy
Efficiency (EE), and E-Mobility (E-MB). The Consultant will propose a strategy to address misaligned or
missing institutional arrangements, policies, and regulatory framework.
(i) Review of existing applicable policies, strategies, plans, and studies in the context of the requirements
of EA 2025 and NEA Act 2025,
(ii) Identify whether the gap is institutional, policy, or regulatory, whether it will be addressed within the
existing framework (alignment/modification), or whether a new framework is to be created, and
(iii) Recommend a broad policy, regulatory, and Institutional framework to address these gaps.
Task 2: Strategic review of the applicable RMI’s electricity sector related international and national
commitments and targets
The Consultant will undertake a focused review of the GRMI's international commitments, national targets,
initiatives for the development of RE, EE, and E-MB, and the progress achieved. The diagnostic and strategic
review will include the following:
(i) Discussion with the stakeholders and ascertaining reasons for the shortfall in the envisaged progress,
(ii) The Consultant shall review relevant national targets, international commitments, ongoing initiatives,
and selected comparable Pacific/SIDS practices for RE, EE, and e-mobility implementation. The
purpose of the review shall be to identify practical options for policy, regulatory, institutional,
monitoring, and capacity-building measures suitable for RMI,
(iii) Identification of implementation gaps, in particular critical legal, policy, regulatory, and institutional
gaps, which impacted the achievements of these initiatives and targets,
(iv) Assess whether these legal, policy, and regulatory gaps stem from implementation shortfall or a missing
framework, and
(v) Recommend a broad policy, regulatory, and institutional framework to address these gaps.
Task 3: Propose a strategy for addressing the identified gaps
The Consultant will propose a strategy with a time-bound implementation roadmap for addressing the gaps
identified in Tasks 1 and 2. The proposed strategy will include the following:
(i) Identification of Implementation gaps, i.e., the framework/provision exists but has not been
implemented, or there is a shortfall in its implementation,
(ii) Identification of gaps in the existing framework, i.e., the legal, policy, regulatory, or Institutional
framework provides for the enabling provision, but it has not been enacted or notified; indicate whether
it is a policy, regulatory, or institutional issue,

9
(iii) Identify misalignment (even a section or provision of it) of the policy, regulatory framework, or the
institutional framework with the EA 2025 and NEA 2025,
(iv) Identification of gaps that cannot be dealt with by the existing framework,
(v) Recommendation of a strategy to deal with these identified gaps. The proposed strategy will indicate the
required interventions (legal, policy, regulatory and institutional), their implementation order, the
stakeholders responsible for addressing them and the timelines within which these will be addressed
(short term- within 3 months, medium term- within 6 months and long term-within 12 months) duly
aligned with the statutory timelines provided in the Acts and related policies,
(vi) Indicate how the recommended interventions will address the identified gaps.
(vii) Indicate the way forward for the gaps which cannot be addressed under the existing legal framework,
and
(viii) Develop a comprehensive implementation roadmap considering the recommendations made in Task 2
and in this Task, and compile the recommendations.
The roadmap should indicate:
Short-term actions,
Medium-term actions,
Long-term actions,
Responsible institution,
Required decision or instrument,
Dependency,
Level of priority, and
Whether the consultant will draft the instrument under this assignment.
Task 4: Assessing the Institutional structure and the manpower requirements of the sector
The Consultant will examine whether the current institutional structure, including its roles and responsibilities,
aligns with those prescribed in the Energy Act and is conducive to the development of RE, EE, and E-MB in
RMI. The Consultant will examine the following:
(i) Clarity in their role and responsibilities (without any overlap) for the development of RE, EE, and E-
MB,
(ii) The institutional capacity to lead the development of RE, EE, and E-MB in RMI, such as project
planning, design, implementation, operation, and maintenance, and
(iii) Recommendations for addressing institutional alignment of roles and responsibilities, capacity gaps, and
the coordination mechanism between them for the development of RE, EE, and E-MB, taking into
account the integration of KAJUR’s operations into MEC.
The Consultant will also assess the skills and the manpower required for the development of RE, EE, and E-MB
in RMI. The Consultant shall assess:
(i) Manpower and the skills available with all important stakeholders,
(ii) Assess the manpower and the skill requirements considering the national targets and the evolving
(proposed Roadmap) legal, policy, regulatory and institutional framework for the development of RE,
EE and E-MB for the next 5 years,
(iii) Indicate the gaps between availability and requirements, and
(iv) Prepare a strategy to meet this gap, indicating the number, the skill requirements, and how the required
skills will be met (contents of the training, how and where the training will be provided, suggestions for
international collaboration, certification).

10
Task 5: Monitoring, Database and Reporting Framework for RE
The Consultant will assess the status of the RE database to determine its suitability for publishing a report that
records, documents, and shares critical information on RE, EE, and E-MB. The Consultant will:
(i) Evaluate the existing database and identify the missing indicators/information gap/data field necessary
for various stakeholders to discharge their roles and responsibilities for the development of RE, EE, and
E-MB in the country (covering Majuro, Ebeye and the outer island systems),
(ii) Recommend formats, information to be gathered, sources of this information, reporting institutions,
reporting frequency, and validation process,
(iii) Recommend the structure of the report to be published, and
(iv) Prepare the first RE encompassing the above recommendations, which NEA can subsequently update
and improve upon.
Task 6: Electricity tariff review and recommendations
The tariff review shall build on, and not duplicate, MEC’s current tariff methodology and tariff model prepared
by the SMO consultant. It shall focus on how that methodology has performed in practice, on areas it did not
examine in depth, and on extending it to all systems now operated by MEC, including Ebeye following the
integration of KAJUR’s operations into MEC, which was not covered by the earlier work. The review shall also
provide MEC and NEA with a clear, evidence-based rationale and supporting calculations for the recommended
tariff options, so that they are well prepared to respond to tariff proposals from policymakers, investors and
other stakeholders.
The Consultant shall review the existing electricity tariff arrangements and prepare recommendations and an
implementation pathway that are consistent with the Energy Act, 2025, and the National Energy Authority Act,
2025. The Consultant shall, in particular:
(i) Assess the adequacy of the current tariff level, structure, adjustment mechanisms, billing arrangements
and related subsidy or compensation mechanisms;
(ii) Assess the revenue requirement and efficient cost of electricity service, based on verified utility
financial, operational and investment data;
(iii) Determine the extent to which prevailing tariffs and practices align with the principles contemplated
under the relevant sections of the Energy Act;
(iv) Assess tariff implications of planned renewable energy, EE, E-mobility, battery storage, network,
resilience and access investments;
(v) Recommend refinements to the existing tariff methodology, tariff structure, adjustment mechanism and
regulatory review process that NEA can use in tariff determinations;
(vi) Review the application of MEC’s current tariff methodology and identify any issues, anomalies or
unintended outcomes that have emerged in practice and that may require adjustment;
(vii) Extend the revenue-requirement and cost-of-supply analysis to Ebeye following the integration of
KAJUR’s operations into MEC, including harmonization of KAJUR’s financial, operational and
customer data with MEC’s, clear separation of electricity costs from water and sewerage costs, and
options and a transition pathway for bringing Ebeye’s electricity tariff into MEC’s tariff framework;
(viii) Assess the merits and implications of the planned introduction of a single tariff for all customer classes;
(ix) Assess whether a uniform national tariff should be maintained across all MEC-served systems (Majuro,
Ebeye and the outer islands), or whether location-specific tariffs or tariff adjustment factors are
warranted, including the resulting cross-subsidies between locations;

11
(x) Using the known sizes and costs of the hybrid and mini-grid systems to be installed in the outer islands,
estimate the indicative cost of supply and potential tariff for each location, and assess the implications of
any proposal to reduce tariffs in locations with high renewable energy penetration;
(xi) Assess the practicality, timing and customer impact of reducing or removing existing government
subsidies, and the alternatives available;
(xii) Assess the feasibility of time-of-use tariffs that reflect the different costs of daytime (predominantly
solar) and nighttime (predominantly diesel) supply;
(xiii) Recommend tariffs and charging arrangements for electric vehicle charging;
(xiv) Assess feed-in tariff, net-metering and power purchase arrangements for privately owned renewable
energy systems seeking to export to MEC’s grid, including pricing based on avoided cost, the grid
integration, storage and backup costs borne by MEC, and the volume of such generation the grid can
accommodate;
(xv) Assess the implications of electricity supplied by third parties outside MEC’s networks, such as
renewable energy systems at government or private facilities that supply neighboring communities,
including the pricing basis and regulatory requirements for such supply, and how differences between
their prices and cost-reflective MEC tariffs can be explained and managed;
(xvi) Assess distributional and affordability implications for customer classes, including vulnerable
customers, and identify transparent options for any subsidy or compensation that may be required; and
(xvii) Provide practical inputs for preparation and future implementation of the National Electricity Tariff and
Billing Code.
Task 7: Addressing the recommendations
Based on the approved recommendations and implementation roadmap under Task 3, and working under the
technical supervision of NEA, the Consultant shall identify, prepare, revise or align the policies, regulations,
codes, guidelines and other instruments required to give effect to the relevant provisions of the Energy Act,
2025 and the National Energy Authority Act, 2025, excluding petroleum-sector provisions.
The Consultant shall, in particular:
(i) Prepare or align the electricity-sector regulatory instruments identified as necessary under the Acts,
including, as applicable, electricity licensing, electricity-sector regulation, Grid Code, service standards,
universal service and subsidy-related mechanisms,
(ii) Prepare or align the instruments required for renewable energy, including, as applicable, grid integration,
renewable IPPs, community renewable-energy projects, rooftop installations and renewable microgrids,
(iii) Prepare or align the instruments required for energy efficiency, including applicable standards, labeling
requirements, air-conditioning and cooling energy-efficiency requirements, and other EE measures
required to implement the applicable provisions of the Acts,
(iv) Prepare or align the instruments required for e-mobility, including applicable requirements relating to
charging infrastructure, technical standards, charging services, electricity supply and tariff arrangements,
and other matters required to implement the applicable provisions of the Acts, and
(v) Propose the institutional framework and clearly define the roles and responsibilities of the relevant
institutions for implementation.
6. Qualifications, Tasks, and Level of Effort of Specified Key Experts
The Consultant shall propose a team adequate for the assignment. In its proposal, the Consultant shall specify:

12
Each proposed key personnel position,
The name of the proposed expert, where available,
Role and responsibilities,
Minimum and actual qualifications and detailed relevant experience,
Whether the input is international or national/local,
Whether the input is home office or field-based,
Estimated level of effort in person-days or person-months, and
Anticipated timing of deployment and deployment location(s).
At a minimum, the Consultant is expected to consider the inclusion of expertise and an indicative level of effort
and split of on-site and remote deployment, as follows:

7. Fees and Reimbursable Expenses
As this engagement will be structured as a lump-sum contract, the selected Consultant shall submit a financial
proposal (in addition to a technical proposal) that includes:
A total lump-sum price for the performance of the services, payable against the deliverables set
out in Section VIII, supported by a breakdown of professional fees by each proposed expert and
personnel category, indicating the applicable unit rates and estimated level of effort (person-months
or person-days), provided for information purposes; and

14
Reimbursable expenses, included within the lump-sum price, covering any anticipated travel,
accommodation, per diem, logistics, communications, and other project-related costs necessary for
the performance of the services.

The lump-sum price shall be inclusive of all costs necessary for the performance of the services. The Consultant
shall clearly state the assumptions underlying the proposed costs and provide sufficient detail to allow MEC to
assess the reasonableness of the proposed budget.
8. Deliverables
The project has six (6) main deliverables.
The Consultant shall prepare and submit the following deliverables in accordance with the Scope of Services.
The Task references identify the principal Tasks contributing to each deliverable and shall not limit the
Consultant's obligation to take into account relevant findings and recommendations arising from other Tasks.
1. Deliverable 1: Inception Report (Linked to: Tasks 1 to 7)
The Consultant shall submit an Inception Report confirming its understanding of the assignment, methodology,
work plan, stakeholder engagement arrangements, data and information requirements, and detailed schedule for
carrying out the seven Tasks and submitting the required deliverables.
An Inception Workshop shall be conducted with MEC, NEA, and other relevant stakeholders, and agreed
outcomes shall be reflected in the final Inception Report.
The Deliverable shall be submitted within two weeks of Notice to Proceed (NTP).
2. Deliverable 2: Diagnostic Assessment and Implementation Roadmap (Linked to: Tasks 1, 2 and 3)
The Consultant shall prepare a consolidated Diagnostic Assessment and Implementation Roadmap for the
relevant provisions of the Energy Act, 2025, and the National Energy Authority Act, 2025, relating to
renewable energy, energy efficiency, and e-mobility.
The deliverable shall consolidate the diagnostic and strategic reviews, identify and categorize the principal
implementation, policy, regulatory, and institutional gaps and misalignments, and establish a prioritized, time-
bound roadmap to address them.
The roadmap shall identify responsible institutions, required actions, sequencing, dependencies, priorities, and
the policies, regulations, codes, and guidelines to be prepared or aligned under this assignment.
The Deliverable shall be submitted within ten weeks of the NTP.
3. Deliverable 3: Institutional and Capacity Development Framework (Linked to: Task 4 and relevant
institutional findings from Tasks 1 to 3)
The Consultant shall prepare an Institutional and Capacity Development Framework setting out the
recommended institutional arrangements, roles and responsibilities, coordination arrangements, manpower and
skills requirements, identified capacity gaps, and capacity-development strategy for RE, EE and e-mobility.

15
The proposed framework shall be consistent with the findings and priorities established under Deliverable 2
The Deliverable shall be submitted within eighteen weeks of the NTP.
4. Deliverable 4: Monitoring, Database and Reporting Framework and RE Report (Linked to: Task 5)
The Consultant shall prepare the Monitoring, Database and Reporting Framework for monitoring progress in
RE, EE and e-mobility, including the recommended database, data collection, validation and reporting
arrangements and institutional responsibilities.
The deliverable shall include the recommended database and reporting arrangements and the first RE Report,
prepared in a form suitable for subsequent updating by NEA.
The Deliverable shall be submitted within twenty-four weeks of the NTP.
5. Deliverable 5: Electricity Tariff Review and Recommendations (Linked to: Task 6)
The Consultant shall prepare a stand-alone Electricity Tariff Review and Recommendations Report, presenting
the assessment, findings, and recommended tariff and regulatory pathway in accordance with Task 6.
The deliverable shall provide the analytical and regulatory basis necessary to support tariff-related decisions and the
preparation or implementation of the applicable tariff and billing regulatory framework.
The deliverable shall also include the updated tariff model in editable form, covering all MEC-served systems
including Ebeye, and concise briefing notes setting out the rationale and supporting calculations for the
recommended tariff positions, for use by MEC and NEA in policy and stakeholder discussions.
The Deliverable shall be submitted within twenty-six weeks of the NTP.
6. Deliverable 6: Policies, Regulations, Codes and Guidelines for Implementation of the Energy Act
(Linked to: Task 7, informed by Tasks 1, 2 and 3)
Based on the approved recommendations and implementation roadmap, the Consultant shall prepare and/or
align the policies, regulations, codes, and guidelines identified as necessary to implement the relevant
provisions of the Energy Act, 2025, and the National Energy Authority Act, 2025, within the scope of the
assignment.
The deliverable shall comprise the agreed package of new and/or revised policies, regulations, codes and
guidelines covering, as applicable:
Electricity-sector regulation;
Renewable energy;
Energy efficiency, including air-conditioning and cooling; and
E-mobility.
The policies, regulations, codes and guidelines shall be consistent with the gaps, priorities and sequencing
established through the preceding Tasks and agreed with NEA and MEC.

16
The Deliverable shall be submitted within thirty-two weeks of the NTP.
9. Contract Duration
The contract duration is 9 months. The expected start date is January 2027.
10. Evaluation Criteria
The Consultant will be selected using the Consultant’s Qualifications-Based Selection (CQS) method in
accordance with the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers and the REGAIN Procurement
Plan. Interested firms shall submit an Expression of Interest (EOI) demonstrating their qualifications and
relevant experience. EOIs will be evaluated against the criteria below. The most qualified and experienced firm
will be invited to submit a combined technical and financial proposal and, if responsive, to negotiate a contract.
Experience preparing energy-sector legal, policy and regulatory frameworks, or implementation plans
for energy legislation, including regulations, codes and licensing (35 points)
Experience in electricity tariff, cost-of-service and revenue-requirement studies for small island or multi-
system utilities, preferably with high renewable energy penetration (25 points)
Experience in the Pacific or other Small Island Developing States (25 points)
Technical and managerial capability of the firm, including core business, years in business, organization
and availability of relevant expertise (15 points)
Total: 100 points
Key experts will not be evaluated at the EOI stage. The qualifications of the proposed key experts set out in
Section 6 will be reviewed when the selected firm submits its technical proposal.
11. Inputs to be provided by MEC and NEA
MEC, as the Employer, and NEA, as the technical and regulatory counterpart, shall provide or facilitate timely
access to the information, documents, data, personnel, and stakeholders reasonably required for the performance
of the Services, to the extent available.
NEA shall:
Provide or facilitate access to applicable policies, regulations, codes, guidelines, regulatory instruments,
sector targets, reports, databases and other relevant regulatory information,
Provide available information on institutional arrangements, regulatory processes, staffing and capacity
relevant to the assignment,
Facilitate access to relevant officials and stakeholders for consultations and workshops, and
Review and provide timely technical comments and acceptance of deliverables submitted to it for review
or acceptance.
MEC shall:
Provide or facilitate access to relevant technical, operational, customer, commercial, financial and
investment information and data, including information required for the tariff review, covering all MEC-
served systems including Ebeye (former KAJUR operations), and MEC’s current tariff methodology and
tariff model,

17
Provide available plans, studies, reports, databases and information relating to existing and planned RE,
EE, e-mobility, storage, and network,
Facilitate access to relevant MEC and PMU personnel and stakeholder consultations, and
Undertake the contractual, administrative and financial review and approval of deliverables in
accordance with the implementation arrangements.
The Consultant shall, as part of the Inception Report, submit a consolidated data and information request
specifying the information required, its proposed source, format and required date. The Consultant shall
promptly identify material data gaps and propose appropriate alternative sources, assumptions or methodologies
where required.
The provision of information by MEC, NEA or any other stakeholder shall not relieve the Consultant of its
responsibility for the verification, analysis, adequacy and quality of the Services and deliverables required under
the Contract.

País: República Argentina Préstamo no: BIRF N° 9232-AR   SDO n.o: LPN 40/2026 (AR-DGPPSE - ADIF-486312-CW-RFB) La República Argentina ha recibido financiamiento del Banco Mundial para sufragar el costo de Proyecto de Modernización del Transporte Ferroviario de Pasajeros en Buenos Aires - Línea Mitre y se propone destinar parte de los fondos a la cancelación de pagos previstos en el contrato de “Intervención en Subestaciones Rectificadoras de San Fernando, Victoria, San Isidro, Olivos, Núñez y Palermo - Línea Mitre”. La Administración de Infraestructura Ferroviarias Sociedad Anónima invita ahora a los Licitantes elegibles a presentar ofertas cerradas para la Obra de Intervención en Subestaciones Rectificadoras de San Fernando, Victoria, San Isidro, Olivos, Núñez y Palermo - Línea Mitre. El plazo total de ejecución es de quinientos cuarenta (540) días corridos para cada lote . La contratación se realizará mediante competencia nacional utilizando la Solicitud de Ofertas (SDO) que se especifique en las Regulaciones de Adquisiciones para Prestatarios de Financiamiento para Proyectos de Inversión, correspondiente a la versión de noviembre de 2020 (“Regulaciones de Adquisiciones”), y está abierta a todos los Licitantes, como se define en las Regulaciones de Adquisiciones. Los Licitantes elegibles interesados pueden pedir más información a la Administración de Infraestructura Ferroviarias Sociedad Anónima, a través de consultas que deberán ser enviadas en formato PDF (con membrete y firma digital del Licitante), manteniendo siempre los requisitos para las consultas de formato papel, a la casilla de correo electrónico licitaciones@adifsa.com.ar. Como medio de respuesta a las consultas, ADIF utilizará las Circulares Aclaratorias y Enmiendas que se publicarán en la página web https://plataforma.adifsa.com.ar/portal_licitaciones. Asimismo, podrán revisar y obtener el documento de licitación en el sitio web indicado al final del presente anuncio . Las ofertas se deben enviar al domicilio consignado más abajo a más tardar el 17 de Noviembre de 2026 hasta las 14 horas . No se permitirá presentar ofertas en forma electrónica. No se aceptarán ofertas tardías. Las ofertas se abrirán públicamente, en presencia de los representantes designados por los Licitantes y de cualquier persona que decida asistir, en el domicilio consignado más abajo, el 17 de Noviembre de 2026 a las 15 horas . Todas las Ofertas deben ir acompañadas de una Declaración de Mantenimiento de la Oferta. Se llama la atención sobre las Regulaciones de Adquisiciones que requieren que el Prestatario divulgue información sobre la propiedad efectiva del adjudicatario, como parte de la Notificación de Adjudicación de Contrato, utilizando el Formulario de Divulgación de la Propiedad Efectiva incluido en el documento de licitación. Los domicilios mencionados más arriba son: a) Sitio web para obtener el pliego : https://plataforma.adifsa.com.ar/portal_licitaciones   b) Dirección referida a los efectos de la presentación de las ofertas es: Administración de Infraestructuras Ferroviarias Sociedad Anónima Área de Contrataciones Avenida Dr. Ramos Mejía 1302, Piso 5°, Oficina 509/505 Ciudad Autónoma de Buenos Aires. CP C1104ABC. República Argentina. c) Dirección referida a los efectos de la apertura de las ofertas es: Administración de Infraestructuras Ferroviarias Sociedad Anónima Avenida Dr. Ramos Mejía 1302, Piso 5°, Oficina 500 Ciudad Autónoma de Buenos Aires. CP C1104ABC. República Argentina. Se informa que el Contratante emitió la Enmienda Nro. 1 (mediante la cual se comunica una nueva visita de obra para el 26 de octubre de 2026 a las 10 hs.). El documento mencionado se podrá consultar en el siguiente link: https://plataforma.adifsa.com.ar/portal_licitaciones

notice_text: REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (CONSULTING FIRM)  PREPARATION OF A NATIONAL LAND USE PLAN FOR BELIZE Institution:    Ministry of Finance Country:        Belize, Central America Project:          Belize Blue Cities and Beyond Project ( P181064 ) Process ID:     BZ-CEU-460793-CS-QCBS Duration:       18 months Deadline:       October 30, 2026; 9:00 AM. (Local Belize Time) (EXTENSION) Assignment Title: Consultancy Services to Prepare a National Land Use Plan for Belize. The Government of Belize has received financing from the World Bank for the implementation of the Belize Blue Cities and Beyond Project and intends to apply part of the Project’s proceeds to contract a firm to prepare a National Land Use Plan for Belize. GENERAL PROCUREMENT NOTICE

COUNTRY: KENYA

PROJECT: ROADS FOR RURAL ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT PROJECT (RREDP)

SECTOR: TRANSPORT SECTOR

GENERAL PROCUREMENT NOTICE

PROJECT ID No.: P517267

The Government of the Republic of Kenya intends to apply for financing in the amount of US$ 600 million equivalent from the World Bank towards the cost of the Roads for Rural Economic Development Project (RREDP) and it intends to apply part of the proceeds to payments for goods, works, non-consulting services and consulting services to be procured under this project.

 

The project will include the following Components:

Component 1: Foundational infrastructure to improve rural connectivity, agricultural productivity, access to markets, services, and economic opportunities. The Authority intends to upgrade approximately 536 km of selected roads in Elgeyo Marakwet, Uasin Gishu, Kericho, Bomet, Nandi, Narok and Nakuru counties to bituminous standard using climate-resilient designs, and to construct bridges at selected locations in Lower Eastern region. The works will also include road safety improvements and associated civil works for fibre-optic cables. The works will be procured through a design-and-build approach, together with the corresponding construction supervision services.

 

Component 2: Improvement of access to basic community socio-economic infrastructure.  The Authority intends to design and construct key community socio-economic infrastructure facilities in selected counties of Elgeyo Marakwet, Uasin Gishu, Kericho, Bomet, Nandi, Narok and Nakuru following a comprehensive needs assessment study.       

Component 3: Strengthening rural cross-border connectivity and trade facilitation. Activities will include construction of buildings and installation of digital systems at Olposimoru, Nyamtiro, and Kopanga border stations.

 

Component 4: Institutional strengthening of selected transport sector and related institutions. Activities will include strengthening institutional capacity for project implementation, road sector planning, and road maintenance management through procurement of goods and services.

 

Procurement of contracts financed by the World Bank will be conducted through the procedures as specified in the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, Seventh Edition (September 2025) (Procurement Regulations) and is open to all eligible firms and individuals as defined in the Procurement Regulations. After project negotiations, the World Bank shall arrange the publication on its external website of the agreed initial procurement plan and all subsequent updates once it has provided a no objection.

Specific procurement notices for contracts subject to open international competitive procurement will be announced, as they become available, on the World Bank’s external website, on the Kenya National Highways Authority website, www.kenha.co.ke, and in at least one newspaper of national circulation in Kenya.

Initial Selection of contractors will be required for the 536 km road sections.

Interested eligible firms and individuals who would wish to be considered for the provision of goods, works, non-consulting services and consulting services under the above-mentioned project, or those requiring additional information, should contact the Borrower at the address below:

P.O. Box 49712 - 00100, Nairobi, Kenya
