MINISTERE DE L’ENERGIE ET DES HYDROCARBURES

 

MINISTERE DU DEVELOPPEMENT NUMERIQUE, DES POSTES ET DES TELECOMMUNICATIONS

 

--------------------------------

PROJET DIGITAL AND ENERGY CONNECTIVITY FOR INCLUSION IN MADAGASCAR (DECIM)

--------------------------------

UNITE DE COORDINATION DU PROJET

------------------------

 

APPEL A MANIFESTATION D’INTERET

POUR LES SERVICES DE CONSULTANT

N° 15/26/DECIM/AMI

Pays : Madagascar

Nom du Projet : Projet de Connectivité Numérique et Energétique pour l’Inclusion à Madagascar (DECIM)

Numéro de Crédit : 7286 MG

Intitulé de la Mission : Élaboration de normes de construction pour des infrastructures énergétiques/numériques & TIC, avec un MGE :

  • Lot 1 : Normes pour les infrastructures énergétiques.
  • Lot 2 : Normes pour les infrastructures numériques, télécommunication et TIC.

N° de référence : MG-DECIM-P178701-560978-CS-QCBS

1. Le Gouvernement de Madagascar a reçu un financement de la Banque mondiale pour couvrir le coût du Projet de Connectivité Numérique et Energétique pour l’Inclusion à Madagascar (Projet DECIM) et a l'intention d’utiliser une partie du montant de ce crédit pour effectuer les paiements au titre du contrat suivant le recrutement d’un cabinet/firme sur « Élaboration de normes de construction pour des infrastructures énergétiques/numériques & TIC, avec un MGE :

  • Lot 1 : Normes pour les infrastructures énergétiques ;
  • Lot 2 : Normes pour les infrastructures numériques, télécommunication et TIC. »

2. Les services de consultant (« les Services ») vise à renforcer les capacités des acteurs du secteur à travers du consultation, de formation et la vulgarisation des normes auprès des institutions publique, des opérateurs et des parties prenantes. L’activité permettra de mettre en place un cadre réglementaire technique de référence pour sécuriser les investissements et améliorer la résilience des infrastructure numérique et énergétique dans le Pays.

3. Les Termes de Référence (TDR) pour la mission sont disponible sur le site internet suivant : https://decim.mg/firme/normes-construction-infrastructures-energetiques-numeriques/tdr/

4. L’Unité de Coordination du Projet DECIM invite dès à présent les firmes de consultants admissibles (« Consultants ») à faire part de leur intérêt à fournir les Services. Les Consultants intéressés doivent fournir des informations démontrant qu’ils possèdent les qualifications requises et l’expérience pertinente pour exécuter les Services.

 

Qualification du cabinet (en tant que société) en rapport avec la mission :

Le Cabinet devrait être un bureau d’études ayant au moins cinq (05) années d’expériences dans le domaine :

  • D’élaboration de normes techniques et spécifiques nationales/internationales (ISO, IEC, ITU, etc.) et règlements sectoriels, de textes réglementaires et normatifs dans la construction/réhabilitation d’infrastructures et/ou ouvrages infrastructures résistantes aux catastrophes et aléas climatiques, sinistres géologiques intégrant une résilience climatique (dans le cadre de Sendai, GCF, etc.) ;
  • De réalisation de diagnostics de vulnérabilité climatique ou études de risques naturels (inondations, séismes, glissements, cyclones, etc.) ;
  • De bonne maîtrise des lois, codes de construction, cadres réglementaires et institutionnels nationaux ;
  • De l’élaboration de Manuel de Gestion et d’Entretien (MGE) en vue de la pérennisation des infrastructures ;
  • De l’élaboration de politiques sectorielles, schémas directeurs, plans de résilience ou de développement durable ;
  • De capacité à animer des ateliers multi-acteurs (gouvernement, secteur privé, société civile, opérateurs techniques) ;
  • D’expérience dans la conduite de consultations nationales pour l’adoption consensuelle de normes ;
  • Des compétences et expertise confirmée dans le domaine de l’Energie et/ou du numérique et TIC (maitrise d’œuvre, élaboration de spécifications techniques, etc.) ;
  • De réalisations dans des pays étrangers des missions de contextes similaires avec intégration de vulnérabilité climatique et défis infrastructure ;
  • Une approche méthodologique convaincante :
  • Qualité de la stratégie de diagnostic et d’analyse réaliste ;
  • Pertinence des outils ou similitude à des missions similaires proposés pour la réalisation de la mission claire ;
  • Capacité à proposer des solutions innovantes adaptées aux contextes nationaux.

Expériences similaires pertinentes :

Le cabinet dispose d’une expérience avérée dans des missions comparables. Il prend en compte :

  • La réalisation antérieure d’expériences prouvées dans le secteur de l’Energie et/ou du numérique, télécoms ou des TIC ;
  • D’au moins cinq (05) ans d’expérience dans l’élaboration de normes techniques et règlementations sectorielles (du secteur de l’Energie et/ou du numérique, télécoms ou des TIC) ;
  • Des expériences concrètes intégrant des aspects de résilience et de gestion des risques et des catastrophes ;
  • Des travaux menés en consultation suivant un contexte multi-acteurs (gouvernement, ministères, secteur privé, partenaires techniques, société civile, PTF, etc.) ;
  • La maitrise du cadre institutionnel et normatif national ;
  • Des missions similaires menées dans à Madagascar ou à l’étranger.

5. L’attention des Consultants intéressés est attirée sur la Section III, paragraphes, 3.14, 3.16 et 3.17 du « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs de FPI » de la Banque mondiale, cinquième édition - septembre 2023, qui énonce la politique de la Banque mondiale en matière de conflits d’intérêts.

6. Les Consultants peuvent s’associer à d’autres firmes locales pour améliorer leurs qualifications, mais ils doivent indiquer clairement si l’association prend la forme d’un groupement et/ou d’une sous-traitance. Dans le cas d’un groupement, tous les membres du groupement d’entreprises seront solidairement responsables de l’ensemble du contrat, s’ils sont sélectionnés.

7. Un consultant sera sélectionné conformément à la méthode de Sélection fondée sur la Qualité et le Coût énoncée dans le Règlement de Passation des Marchés.

8. De plus amples informations peuvent être obtenues à l'adresse ci-dessous pendant les heures de bureau de 09h00 à 16h00.

Purchaser: National Information Technology Authority-Uganda

Name of Project: Uganda Digital Acceleration Project (UDAP)

Project ID: P171305             Credit No.: 6898-UG            Country: Uganda

Contract Title:  Design, Development and Deployment of the Digital Solution for Equitable Health Care Among Refugee Communities

Reference No.: NITA-U/UDAP/SUPLS/2026-2027/00026

Issued on: 16th October, 2026                                       

1.The Government of Uganda represented by the National Information Technology Authority Uganda (NITA-U) has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the: Uganda Digital Acceleration Project-Government Network (UDAP-GOVNET), and intends to apply part of the proceeds toward payments under the contract for Design, Development and Deployment of the Digital Solution for Equitable Health Care among Refugee Communities.  .
 

2.National Information Technology Authority-Uganda (NITA-U) now invites sealed Bids from eligible Proposers for Design, Development and Deployment of the Digital Solution for Equitable Health Care among Refugee Communities.

3. The procurement process will be conducted through International competitive procurement using Request for Proposals (RFP) as specified in the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers - Procurement in Investment Projects Financing” (July 2016, revised February 2025) and is open to all eligible proposers as defined in the Procurement Regulations.

4. Interested eligible Proposers may obtain further information from National Information Technology Authority-Uganda and inspect the request for proposal document during office hours 0800 to 1700 hours from Monday to Friday at the address given below.

5.A pre-proposal meeting will be held 3rd November, 2026 at NITA-U Head Office, Palm Courts, Plot 7A, Rotary Avenue at 1100 Hours East Africa Time with an Online Virtual Meeting .A link will be shared with all registered proposers prior to the date of the meeting. The proposers who wish to attend the meeting shall register and submit their official email addresses not later than one (1) day to the date of the meeting to jacqueline.musimenta@nita.go.ug.

6.The request for proposal document in English may be purchased by interested eligible Proposers upon the submission of a written application to the address below and upon payment of a nonrefundable fee of Ugx.200,000 (Two Hundred Thousand Uganda Shillings Only) or equivalent in a freely convertible currency. The method of payment will be the Electronic Funds Transfer (EFT) Bank account number: 006550058000001, Customer name: National Information Technology Authority, Uganda (NITA-U), Account title: NITA-U Local Revenue Expenditure Account, Bank Name: Bank of Uganda Swift Code: UGBAUGKA. A PDF bidding document shall be sent to the potential bidder electronically upon receipt of confirmation of payment.

7.Proposals must be delivered to the address below on or before 30th November, 2026 at 1100 Hours East Africa Time Electronic procurement will not be permitted. Late Proposals will be rejected. Proposals will be publicly opened in the presence of the Proposers’ designated representatives and anyone who chooses to attend, at the address below on 1st Floor Boardroom, 1105 Hours East Africa Time 30th November, 2026.  All envelopes marked “FINANCIAL PART” shall remain unopened and will be held in safe custody of the Purchaser until the second public Proposals opening.

 8.Proposals must be accompanied by a Proposal Security of ;

 UGX 120,000,000/= (Uganda Shillings, One Hundred and Twenty Million) or an equivalent amount in a freely convertible currency.

 

The Proposal Security shall be valid in accordance with Section II-Proposal Data Sheet (PDS); ITP 20.1

10.The address referred to above is:

    Kampala-Uganda

MINISTRY OF EDUCATION

 

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (REOI)

 

GHANA ACCOUNTABILITY FOR LEARNING OUTCOMES PROJECT ADDITIONAL FINANCING 2 (GALOP AF 2)

PROJECT ID: 165557

 

PROCUREMENT OF CONSULTANCY SERVICES (FIRMS)

 

BACKGROUND

The Government of Ghana, under World Bank and Global Partnership for Education (GPE) funding, is supporting the government’s education strategic plan to improve equitable access to quality basic education in Ghana. The Ghana Accountability for Learning Outcomes Project (GALOP), approved for an amount of USD 218.7 million, has the Project Development Objective (PDO) to improve the quality of education in low-performing basic education schools and to strengthen education sector equity and accountability in Ghana. The GALOP was originally implemented over a five-year period from Jan 2020 to Dec 2024. However, the parent project has been extended to close by 31st December 2026 and the Ministry has received a second additional financing (AF 2) totaling $118.8m to scale up successful interventions from the parent project to be implemented by 31st December 2028.

The Government of Ghana has recently secured funds from the World Bank (USD 300 million) for the Ministry of Education to implement the Second Education Transformation for Access, Relevance and Results for Jobs Project (STARR-J), with the PDO to expand access to, and improve the quality and relevance of, secondary education in Ghana. The Project focuses on expanding infrastructure and opportunities for underserved students, strengthening teaching and learning (especially in STEM and competency-based training), modernizing technical and vocational systems, and aligning education outcomes with skills demanded by employers, ultimately helping students transition more successfully into further education or decent work.

The purpose of the REOI is to invite prospective firms to submit Expressions of Interest to provide any of the underlisted services.

No

Description of Assignment

Reference No.

Selection Method

1

 

Consultancy Services of an IT Consultant for the Development of an Online Sectoral  Grievance Redress Mechanism (GRM)

MOE/GALOP/CS/8/2026

https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1SuqCU1ZkbdlduucTPILtsmjjcG0MAx-0?usp=sharing

 

NB: Consultant should state clearly the Reference No. and the Assignment they are applying for.

Interested firms should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to undertake the above services required as per the Terms of Reference (ToR) for any of the assignments provided in the link above.

The short-listing criteria are:

  • Experience of firm in similar/related assignments
  • Experience working in country and/or region in similar conditions
  • Adequacy of the firm’s technical and Managerial capacity
  • Qualifications and Experience of key experts proposed and their Competences
  • Availability of appropriate skills among staff
  • Any other relevant information as required in the ToR
  1. Selection of Consultants

The selection method for the assignments will be as indicated in the table above in line with procedures specified by World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers; Procurement in Investment Project Financing - Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services, July 2016; Revised September 2025 (7th Edition).

EOIs must be deposited at the address below on or before 4th November 2026 at 4:00 pm.

Soft copy submissions shall be via the email address provided below;

 

EOI Address;

 

The Chief Director

Ministry of Education

P. O. Box M45

Accra

Attn: Director, Procurement

Submissions shall be made in both hard copy and soft copy to the address below;

Ministry of Education, Procurement Directorate, Room K35

E-mail :  moeprocurementunit@gmail.com  / cc: procurement@moe.gov.gh  

 Interested eligible consultants may obtain further information from the Procurement Directorate, Ministry of Education, at the address given above during working hours from 8:30 am – 4:30 pm.

SOLICITAÇÃO DE COTAÇÕES (REQUEST FOR QUOTATIONS - RFQ)

Aquisição de Licenças Office - Ref.ª MATINF-BEM 07-2025

 

O Governo da República de Angola, por intermédio do Ministério da Acção Social, Família e Promoção da Mulher (MASFAMU), recebeu financiamento do Banco Internacional de Reconstrução e Desenvolvimento (BIRD), através do Empréstimo IBRD-97180, para apoiar a implementação do Projecto de Reforço do Sistema de Protecção Social para o Capital Humano e a Resiliência (P181495), e pretende aplicar parte dos recursos desse financiamento à actividade «Aquisição de Licenças do Office».

A Unidade de Implementação do Projecto (UIP) convida empresas elegíveis a apresentarem cotações para «Aquisição de Licenças do Office», observando as quantidades e especificações técnicas da Solicitação de Cotações (RFQ) correspondente.

O processo será conduzido através do método Solicitação de Cotações (Request for Quotations - RFQ), categoria «Bens», com abordagem Aberta ao Mercado Nacional, em regime de pós-qualificação e etapa única - um envelope, em conformidade com o Regulamento de Aquisições aplicável aos Mutuários de Financiamento de Projectos de Investimento do Banco Mundial e com o Plano de Aquisições aprovado no STEP.

notice_text:          Government of Somaliland     Hargeisa Local Government   Somali Urban Resilience Project (SURP II) REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (REOI) (INDIVIDUAL CONSULTING SERVICES) PIU Community Engagement Officer   Country: Government of Somaliland Project ID No: P170922 Project: Somali Urban Resilience Project (SURP-II) Consultant Service: PIU Community Engagement Officer   Individual/Firm: Individual Duty Station: Hargeisa Deadline: November 05, 2026 Ref: SO-HM-574040-CS-INDV   Background of the Project   The Hargeisa Local Government is implementing the SURP II Project (Nagaad Project) financed by the World Bank. The Project Development Objective (PDO) of the Nagaad Project is to strengthen the public service delivery capacity of local governments, expand access to climate-resilient urban infrastructure and services, and enable an immediate and effective response to eligible crises or emergencies in targeted areas.   Hargeisa Municipality is responsible for managing and supervising all project activities within the municipality, including timely implementation of civil work, procurement of goods and services, application of environmental and social safeguards, and continuous community engagement. It oversees contractors and supervision consultants to ensure quality, manages financial accounts in coordination with the EAFD, ensures timely payments, and prepares periodic plans, budgets, and reports. The PIU Community Engagement Officer also implements the project’s grievance mechanism, monitors and evaluates progress, and regularly reports results and issues to the PCU and World Bank. Hargeisa Municipality is seeking to use of the SURP II project to finance the recruitment of PIU Community Engagement Officer.   Responsibilities   The Community Engagement Officer will be responsible for overseeing and facilitating the engagement aspects of the Nagaad Project within Hargeisa Local government, with a primary focus on promoting inclusive, equitable, and participatory processes throughout the project lifecycle. The Officer will ensure that the project is implemented in a socially sensitive manner and that community voices are meaningfully integrated into planning, implementation, and monitoring activities. Provide substantive support in collecting and transcribing relevant information from community members and municipal authorities during field visits and consultations. Keep the Project Coordinator continuously informed about any local issues or social dynamics that may impact project implementation or community relations.   All specific duties and responsibilities are detailed in the Terms of Reference (TOR), available on the Hargeisa Municipality website at https://hargeisamunicipality.com or upon request via in-person submission or email.   Selection Criteria   The selection shall be based on qualifications, experience and skills of the candidate and followed by an interview. The qualifications, experience and competencies include: A university degree in Social Sciences, Gender Studies, Community Development, Public Administration, or another relevant discipline. Minimum of 3 years of experience in planning and implementing community engagement activities within development or infrastructure projects. At least 2 years of proven experience in implementing GBV prevention and response initiatives. Demonstrated ability to effectively engage and build trust with diverse community groups, including vulnerable populations. Practical experience in facilitating community consultations, mobilization, and training sessions. Strong communication and facilitation skills, with the ability to manage sensitive discussions with empathy and professionalism. Solid understanding of gender equality, social inclusion, and participatory approaches. Ability to analyze social dynamics, identify risks, and adapt strategies to local contexts REPORTING   The Community Engagement Officer will report directly to the PIU Project Coordinator and work under the overall guidance of the World Bank Task Team Leader(s) for the SURP II Project. TIMING Duration of Assignment : The Community Engagement Officer shall be contracted for an initial period of one-year, renewable subject to satisfactory performance evaluation by the Municipality and approval by the World Bank, as well as the availability of project funds.   Hargeisa Local Government now invites eligible Individual Consultants to indicate their interest in providing the above-mentioned services. Interested consultants must provide the following (i) Curriculum Vitae (CV) with 3 reference people; (ii) copies of certificates of academic qualifications; (iii) cover letter indicating that they are qualified to perform the services and (iv) Passports or ID.   SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to section III, para 3.14,3.16 & 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers: Procurement in Investment Projects Financing Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services, July 2016, revised November 2017, August 2018, November 2020, and September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultant method set out in the World Bank Procurement Regulations.    Interested applicants may obtain further information including a detailed Terms of Reference from the Hargeisa Local Government in person or by e-mail to the address given below during office hours from 9.00 a.m.– 4.00 p.m. Saturday to Thursday.   Deadline : Expressions of interest and CV must be delivered to the address below by hand, mail, courier or email on or before November 05, 2026, at 16:00 EAT                 Attention: PIU Coordinator of SURP II Project Hargeisa Local Government Government of Somaliland 402 Jidka Abubakar Al Siddiq, Maxamuud Xarbi, Gacan Libaax, Hargeysa 90701 Hargeisa, Somaliland   Email Address: hlgnagaadprocurement@gmail.com ,   CC:  sirabdirahman.yusuf@gmail.com

Government of Somaliland

    Hargeisa Local Government

  Somali Urban Resilience Project (SURP II)

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST(REOI)

(INDIVIDUAL CONSULTING SERVICES)

PIU Community Engagement Officer

 

Country: Government of Somaliland

Project ID No: P170922

Project: Somali Urban Resilience Project (SURP-II)

Consultant Service: PIU Community Engagement Officer  

Individual/Firm: Individual

Duty Station: Hargeisa

Deadline: November 05, 2026

Ref: SO-HM-574040-CS-INDV

 

  1. Background of the Project

 

The Hargeisa Local Government is implementing the SURP II Project (Nagaad Project) financed by the World Bank. The Project Development Objective (PDO) of the Nagaad Project is to strengthen the public service delivery capacity of local governments, expand access to climate-resilient urban infrastructure and services, and enable an immediate and effective response to eligible crises or emergencies in targeted areas.

 

Hargeisa Municipality is responsible for managing and supervising all project activities within the municipality, including timely implementation of civil work, procurement of goods and services, application of environmental and social safeguards, and continuous community engagement. It oversees contractors and supervision consultants to ensure quality, manages financial accounts in coordination with the EAFD, ensures timely payments, and prepares periodic plans, budgets, and reports. The PIU Community Engagement Officer also implements the project’s grievance mechanism, monitors and evaluates progress, and regularly reports results and issues to the PCU and World Bank.

Hargeisa Municipality is seeking to use of the SURP II project to finance the recruitment of PIU Community Engagement Officer.

 

  1. Responsibilities

 

The Community Engagement Officer will be responsible for overseeing and facilitating the engagement aspects of the Nagaad Project within Hargeisa Local government, with a primary focus on promoting inclusive, equitable, and participatory processes throughout the project lifecycle. The Officer will ensure that the project is implemented in a socially sensitive manner and that community voices are meaningfully integrated into planning, implementation, and monitoring activities.

  • Provide substantive support in collecting and transcribing relevant information from community members and municipal authorities during field visits and consultations.
  • Keep the Project Coordinator continuously informed about any local issues or social dynamics that may impact project implementation or community relations.

 

All specific duties and responsibilities are detailed in the Terms of Reference (TOR), available on the Hargeisa Municipality website at https://hargeisamunicipality.com or upon request via in-person submission or email.

 

  1. Selection Criteria

 

The selection shall be based on qualifications, experience and skills of the candidate and followed by an interview. The qualifications, experience and competencies include:

  • A university degree in Social Sciences, Gender Studies, Community Development, Public Administration, or another relevant discipline.
  • Minimum of 3 years of experience in planning and implementing community engagement activities within development or infrastructure projects.
  • At least 2 years of proven experience in implementing GBV prevention and response initiatives.
  • Demonstrated ability to effectively engage and build trust with diverse community groups, including vulnerable populations.
  • Practical experience in facilitating community consultations, mobilization, and training sessions.
  • Strong communication and facilitation skills, with the ability to manage sensitive discussions with empathy and professionalism.
  • Solid understanding of gender equality, social inclusion, and participatory approaches.
  • Ability to analyze social dynamics, identify risks, and adapt strategies to local contexts
  1. REPORTING

 

The Community Engagement Officer will report directly to the PIU Project Coordinator and work under the overall guidance of the World Bank Task Team Leader(s) for the SURP II Project.

  1. TIMING Duration of Assignment:

The Community Engagement Officer shall be contracted for an initial period of one-year, renewable subject to satisfactory performance evaluation by the Municipality and approval by the World Bank, as well as the availability of project funds.

 

Hargeisa Local Government now invites eligible Individual Consultants to indicate their interest in providing the above-mentioned services. Interested consultants must provide the following (i) Curriculum Vitae (CV) with 3 reference people; (ii) copies of certificates of academic qualifications; (iii) cover letter indicating that they are qualified to perform the services and (iv) Passports or ID.

 

  1. SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to section III, para 3.14,3.16 & 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers: Procurement in Investment Projects Financing Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services, July 2016, revised November 2017, August 2018, November 2020, and September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultant method set out in the World Bank Procurement Regulations. 

 

Interested applicants may obtain further information including a detailed Terms of Reference from the Hargeisa Local Government in person or by e-mail to the address given below during office hours from 9.00 a.m.– 4.00 p.m. Saturday to Thursday.

 

Deadline: Expressions of interest and CV must be delivered to the address below by hand, mail, courier or email on or before November 05, 2026, at 16:00 EAT

 



              Attention: PIU Coordinator of SURP II Project

Hargeisa Local Government

Government of Somaliland

402 Jidka Abubakar Al Siddiq, Maxamuud Xarbi, Gacan Libaax, Hargeysa 90701

Hargeisa, Somaliland

notice_text: AVIS A MANIFESTATIONS D’INTÉRÊT     Pays : SÉNÉGAL Nom du projet : PROJET D’AMÉLIORATION DE LA CONNECTIVITÉ DES ZONES DE PRODUCTION AGRICOLE (PCZA) DU NORD ET DU CENTRE DU SÉNÉGAL   Numéro de Prêt/Crédit/Don : Crédit IDA n° 80680-SN   Intitulé de la Mission : Supervision des travaux d’aménagements connexes (écoles, établissements de santé, marchés, magasins de stockage, plateformes multifonctionnelles pour les femmes, etc.) dans le cadre du Projet d’amélioration de la Connectivité des Zones de production Agricole (PCZA) du nord et du centre du Sénégal -Phase II   N° de référence : SN-AGEROUTE-567712-CW-RFB   Le Gouvernement de la République du Sénégal a obtenu un crédit additionnel de l’Association Internationale de Développement (IDA) d’un montant équivalent à US$ 140 millions en vue de financer le coût de la seconde phase du Projet d’amélioration de la Connectivité des Zones agricoles (PCZA) du nord et du centre et se propose d’utiliser une partie les fonds de ce crédit pour financer les services de consultance comprenant le contrôle et la supervision des travaux de construction d’aménagements connexes (salles de classes, magasins, marchés, plateformes multifonctionnelles, etc.) des lots suivants en une (01) seule mission :   Lot 5 - tronçon Koussanar-Maka Coulibantang-Koumpentoum Lot 6 - tronçon Tambacounda-Goumbayel-Dianké Makha   Les services comprennent:   la supervision des travaux; la vérification et la réception des travaux; l’établissement des quantités de travaux exécutés; l’analyse et la validation des dossiers d’exécution; la rédaction des rapports périodiques ; la supervision de la mise en œuvre des mesures prévues au titre du Plan de Gestion Environnementale et Sociale; et  l’assistance à l’Agence dans l’exécution du projet.   Les Termes de Référence (TDR) de la mission peuvent être obtenus aux adresses ci-après: mlaye@ageroute.sn  ; rndour@ageroute.sn ; mmbaye@ageroute.sn L’Agence des Travaux et de Gestion des Routes (AGEROUTE) Sénégal invite dès à présent les firmes de consultants admissibles (« Consultants ») à faire part de leur intérêt à fournir les Services. Les Consultants intéressés doivent fournir des informations démontrant qu’ils possèdent les qualifications requises et l’expérience pertinente pour exécuter les Services. Les critères de sélection d’une liste restreinte sont les suivants :   qualification générale dans le domaine (activités principales, nombre d’années d'existence et nombre de personnel permanent depuis  5 ans du bureau) ;  expérience pour des missions similaires (fournir les attestations justifiant la réalisation des missions); capacité technique et managériale du bureau ; moyens logistiques disponibles ; références de clients et de toute autre information jugée nécessaire ; qualification du personnel dans le domaine; toute autre information jugée pertinente.   Les experts clés ne seront pas évalués à l’étape de la préparation de la liste restreinte. NB : En cas d'égalité du nombre total de points obtenus, le cabinet / groupement de cabinets ayant réalisé plus de missions spécifiques sera privilégié. L’attention des Consultants intéressés est attirée sur la Section III, paragraphes, 3.14, 3.16 et 3.17 du « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs de FPI (juillet 2016, révisée en Novembre 2017, Aout 2018, Novembre 2020, Septembre 2023 et Février 2025 )  « Règlements de Passation des marchés »), relatives aux règles de la Banque mondiale en matière de conflits d’intérêts sont applicables. Les Consultants peuvent s’associer à d’autres firmes pour améliorer leurs qualifications, mais ils doivent indiquer clairement si l’association prend la forme d’un groupement et/ou d’une sous-traitance. Dans le cas d’un groupement, tous les membres du groupement seront solidairement responsables de l’ensemble du contrat, s’ils sont sélectionnés. Un Consultant sera sélectionné selon la méthode de sélection fondée sur la qualité et le coût (QCBS), conformément à la réglementation applicable en matière de passation de marchés de la Banque mondiale. Sur la base des manifestations d’intérêt soumises et des critères susmentionnés, cinq à huit cabinets ou associations les plus qualifiés seront présélectionnés et invités à participer à la phase suivante. Des informations supplémentaires peuvent être obtenues à l’adresse ci-dessous pendant les heures de bureau de 8h00 à 17h00 GMT. Les manifestations d’intérêt, écrites en langue française, doivent être fournies à l’adresse ci-dessous (en personne, ou par courriel) au plus tard le 03 novembre 2026 à 11 heures 30 minutes (GMT): Agence des Travaux et de Gestion des Routes (AGEROUTE) SENEGAL, A l’attention de : Gallo BA, Directeur Général Rue F X Rue David Diop, Fann Résidence Téléphone : (+221) 33 869 07 51 Fax : (+221) 33 864 63 53 Email : rndour@ageroute.sn ; mlaye@ageroute.sn ; mmbaye@ageroute.sn L’enveloppe présentant la Candidature devra porter expressément la mention: « Manifestation d'intérêt pour Contrôle et supervision des travaux d’aménagements connexes (écoles, établissements de santé, marchés, magasins de stockage, plateformes multifonctionnelles pour les femmes, etc.) dans le cadre du Projet d’amélioration de la Connectivité des Zones de production Agricole (PCZA) du nord et du centre du Sénégal – Phase 2 ».

notice_text: Ministry of Education and Human Resources Development Modernizing Education, Skills, and Administrative Reforms (MASAR) Program Terms of Reference for:  Digital Transformation Senior Coordinator Reference No.:  JO-MOE-566807-CS-INDV Program Background: The Modernizing Education, Skills, and Administrative Reforms (MASAR) Program for Results (PforR) is a transformative, system-wide reform initiative anchored in Jordan’s Economic Modernization Vision (EMV). The MASAR Operation is designed to support the Ministry of Education and Human Resources Development in addressing foundational bottlenecks in access, quality, and relevance of education, with a dual emphasis on equity and efficiency. The operation aims to strengthen institutional capacity while enabling measurable improvements in learning outcomes and employability, particularly through early childhood education and labor market-aligned technical and vocational education and training (TVET), and digital transformation in education. The program became effective in 2024, with a total financing envelope of USD 400 million, supported by the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD). It comprises two core components: Program-for-Results (PforR) : the principal financing instrument that disburses against verified achievement of results tied to government reform priorities. Investment Project Financing (IPF) : a complementary technical assistance (TA) component aimed at supporting the implementation of system-strengthening activities and accelerating the achievement of Disbursement Linked Indicators (DLIs). MASAR is structured around four interlinked Results Areas (RAs) that are strategically aligned with key education-sector transition points and cross-cutting governance reforms: RA1: Home to School – Expanding Access to Foundational Learning. This includes (i) increasing equitable access to KG2, particularly in under-served districts and refugee-hosting communities; (ii) enhancing the quality of early childhood education through a revised KG1-KG2 curriculum and quality assurance mechanisms; and (iii) improving foundational literacy skills for Grades 1–3 through targeted pedagogical interventions and a comprehensive implementation plan. RA2: School to Work – Increasing Access to Labor Market-Relevant TVET. MASAR seeks to improve the alignment of TVET with private sector needs by institutionalizing public-private partnerships, scaling apprenticeships, and expanding career guidance and employment pathways. This is complemented by the operationalization of an equivalency system that supports the portability and recognition of TVET qualifications, and enhanced use of learner trajectory data to inform student support services. RA3: Strengthening Sector Governance and Efficiency. The program supports the operationalization of a restructured governance model for the education sector and introduces reforms to human resource management, with a particular focus on teacher recruitment, deployment, and professional development policies. RA4: Digital Transformation in Education, to be introduced through the MASAR Additional Financing (AF), supporting digital and AI-enabled learning for students in Grades 4-12 and strengthening the institutional infrastructure needed for national-scale technology integration in education. In addition to its core education objectives, MASAR embeds environmental and social sustainability principles across its implementation. Ultimately, MASAR is designed to deliver measurable, inclusive, and sustainable improvements in Jordan’s education system. It expands access to early learning, strengthens foundational skills, improves graduate employability, strengthens digital skills, technology-enabled learning, and future-ready competencies, and reinforces institutional coherence through evidence-based policymaking. By supporting inclusive education and strengthening school-to-work transitions, the program directly contributes to Jordan’s long-term economic resilience and human capital development agenda. Objectives of the Assignment: The objective of this assignment is to provide strategic and operational support for the implementation of MASAR Result Area 4 (Digital Transformation in Education) and the coordination of MoE's digital education transformation portfolio, ensuring achievement of RA4 DLRs, alignment with national reform priorities, effective inter-institutional and donor coordination, and timely delivery of evidence required for programme verification and disbursement. The Senior Coordinator will support operational follow-up, troubleshoot bottlenecks, monitor implementation against annual work plans, coordinate GFPP-financed preparatory activities, and contribute to institutionalizing sustainable digital education governance, EdTech implementation capacity, child-safe and inclusive digital learning standards, and cross-government coordination mechanisms within MoE systems. Specifically, the Senior Coordinator will: Lead MASAR RA4 preparation and implementation, driving progress against DLR 8.1-8.5 milestones and ensuring that technical assistance, procurement, capacity building, and institutional arrangements are sequenced to deliver required results on time. Serve as the coordination focal point responsible for tracking, consolidating, and supporting delivery of RA4-related DLRs and associated verification evidence. Coordinate GFPP-financed preparation activities so that technical assessments, pilots, PIU establishment, EdTech and AI Hub readiness, knowledge exchange, and capacity building directly inform the MASAR AF design and first-year implementation readiness. Coordinate the digital education donor and partner portfolio, to ensure strategic alignment with the Education Strategic Plan, the National Education Sector Strategy, the EMV, and MASAR AF priorities while preventing duplication across programmes. Produce regular, analytically rigorous RA4 and digital education portfolio progress reporting for DCU leadership, MASAR operational program manager, and relevant government counterparts. Identify unresourced digital transformation priority areas and support resource mobilization and partner alignment. Scope of Work MASAR RA4 Planning and Implementation Develop, update, and closely monitor annual action plans for RA4, ensuring alignment with MASAR’s overall results framework, DLR timelines, and MoE priorities. Break activities into operational tasks with clear milestones, dependencies, and responsible units. Support the preparation and review of annual work plans, budgets, and implementation schedules to ensure timely delivery of programme results. Conduct periodic implementation reviews and recommend adjustments to activities, sequencing, resource allocation, and technical assistance arrangements to maintain progress toward DLR achievement. Provide regular progress reports against implementation for result area 4 workplan under MASAR, including the preparation of MASAR's bi-annual progress reports. Support the preparation and quality review of ToRs for RA4 consultancies and contracts, including connectivity assessments, device pilots, EdTech technical assistance, AI governance, digital content development, cybersecurity, data privacy, and M&E assignments. Digital Education Portfolio Coordination and Partner Alignment Maintain and analyse a Digital Education Projects Matrix as a strategic portfolio management tool, identifying gaps, duplication risks, sequencing challenges, and opportunities for synergies across interventions. Advise DCU and MASAR leadership on the prioritisation, alignment, endorsement, modification, and coordination of Digital Transformation initiatives to support implementation of the Education Strategic Plan (ESP) and national reform priorities. Screen new digital education, EdTech, AI, connectivity, content, teacher training, and device-related proposals for alignment with RA4 DLRs, existing interventions, MoE standards, and donor investments. Facilitate division-of-labour arrangements among development partners and stakeholders, ensuring clarity of roles, responsibilities, expected results, and implementation timelines. Identify un-resourced Digital Education priority areas and support resource mobilisation efforts through engagement with development partners and relevant stakeholders. Maintain cluster meeting records and action trackers; ensure follow-through on agreed actions between meetings. Serve as the focal point for the Google Chromebook project. Stakeholder Coordination and Representation Serve as the primary coordination focal point for digital transformation reforms, ensuring effective collaboration among Ministry directorates, development partners, implementing agencies, and other stakeholders. Coordinate regularly with relevant MoE directorates and external stakeholders to ensure clarity of roles, timelines, and expected contributions. Participate in technical committees, working groups, task teams, and workshops, providing inputs and ensuring follow-up on agreed actions. Attend all MASAR supervision missions as the RA4 technical focal point. Represent DCU’s coordination mandate at all Digital Transformation technical working groups and maintain proactive, technically substantive relationships with implementing agencies including UN agencies, development partners, private sector technology firms, telecom providers, universities, and others, as needed. Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification Track all RA4-relevant MASAR DLRs and maintain a real-time DLR risk register; flag at-risk DLRs to the Program Manager and DCU Leadership with sufficient lead time for corrective action. Monitor implementation progress across the broader digital transformation portfolio, maintaining oversight of milestones, deliverables, risks, dependencies, and corrective actions Coordinate the preparation, consolidation, and quality assurance of DLR verification evidence, ensuring compliance with agreed verification protocols and readiness for independent verification reviews. Review Verification reports submitted by the verification agency for the DLRs under result area 4. Support monitoring, evaluation, reporting, verification, and learning requirements across digital transformation-related donor-funded programmes, ensuring timely provision of data, performance information, and evidence in accordance with donor requirements. Support supervision missions, evaluations, audits, verification exercises, and technical assessments by ensuring data readiness and facilitating access to relevant information and stakeholders. Risk Management and Troubleshooting Identify implementation risks, bottlenecks, and systemic constraints affecting RA4 and the broader digital transformation portfolio. Provide timely solutions or mitigation measures and engage relevant directorates to resolve issues. Escalate critical challenges to the Program Manager and DCU Deputy Director with clear problem statements and recommended actions. Knowledge Management and Institutional Strengthening Facilitate knowledge exchange across MoE directorates and donor partners, ensuring that lessons learned, technical guidance, and best practices are captured and shared. Support capacity-building efforts related to EdTech program management, digital pedagogy, AI-supported teaching, digital content development, school connectivity, device management, cybersecurity, data privacy, and DLR verification. Promote institutionalization of MASAR RA4 processes and DCU digital transformation coordination mechanisms within MoE systems to strengthen long-term sustainability. Document lessons from pilots and knowledge exchanges and ensure that they inform implementation manuals, technical standards, procurement documents, and training packages. Duration and Location Contract duration is 1 year with possible extension based on performance and availability of funding. Full-time presence is required. The Senior Coordinator will be based at the Ministry of Education and Human Resources Development, Amman, Jordan. Required Qualifications and Experience Education: A bachelor's degree in Education, Digital Education, ICT, Computer Science, Public Policy, Economics, Development Studies, Engineering, or a related field. A master's degree is preferred, particularly in education policy, digital transformation, educational technology, public Experience: At least 10 years of progressively responsible experience in education sector reform, digital transformation, EdTech implementation, programme management, or donor coordination, including at least 5 years in a leadership or coordination role involving multiple stakeholders. Technical Skills: Deep understanding of digital education systems, school connectivity, device deployment, digital content, teacher digital pedagogy, AI-enabled education tools, data privacy, cybersecurity, child online protection, accessibility, and inclusive technology design. Strong background in results-based management, including work planning, monitoring progress, tracking indicators, maintaining risk registers, and preparing progress reports. Experience with PforR, DLI/DLR-based programmes, World Bank operations, or large-scale public-sector technology programs is a strong advantage. Familiarity with Jordan's education sector, digital government architecture, and the Economic Modernization Vision is desirable. Stakeholder Engagement and Communication: Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, with a proven ability to engage and coordinate government officials, development partners, UN agencies, and private-sector stakeholders. Experience in facilitating workshops, leading working groups, and achieving consensus among diverse actors. Fluency in English and Arabic is required. Political Economy and Organisational Skills: Strong political economy awareness with the ability to navigate complex multi-donor environments diplomatically. Self-driven, results-oriented, and capable of managing multiple simultaneous work streams. Demonstrated ability to produce high-quality, decision-ready briefings for senior leadership and meet tight deadlines. Reporting and Institutional Arrangements The Senior Coordinator shall report administratively to the MASAR Operational Program Manager and maintain a technical reporting line to the DCU Deputy Director for portfolio coordination functions. For day-to-day operations, the Senior Coordinator will work closely with designated focal points in the Ministry of Education and Human Resources Development, the World Bank task team, Digital Transformation donor programme teams, and DLR task team leaders as primary counterparts. Submission  Interested candidates are invited to submit their resume and any relevant certifications by the deadline specified in the announcement on the Ministry’s website, to the following email address: A.Orabi@moej.edu.jo  Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted for an interview.

  • Support the preparation and quality review of ToRs for RA4 consultancies and contracts, including connectivity assessments, device pilots, EdTech technical assistance, AI governance, digital content development, cybersecurity, data privacy, and M&E assignments.

Digital Education Portfolio Coordination and Partner Alignment

  • Maintain and analyse a Digital Education Projects Matrix as a strategic portfolio management tool, identifying gaps, duplication risks, sequencing challenges, and opportunities for synergies across interventions.
  • Advise DCU and MASAR leadership on the prioritisation, alignment, endorsement, modification, and coordination of Digital Transformation initiatives to support implementation of the Education Strategic Plan (ESP) and national reform priorities.
  • Screen new digital education, EdTech, AI, connectivity, content, teacher training, and device-related proposals for alignment with RA4 DLRs, existing interventions, MoE standards, and donor investments.
  • Facilitate division-of-labour arrangements among development partners and stakeholders, ensuring clarity of roles, responsibilities, expected results, and implementation timelines.
  • Identify un-resourced Digital Education priority areas and support resource mobilisation efforts through engagement with development partners and relevant stakeholders.
  • Maintain cluster meeting records and action trackers; ensure follow-through on agreed actions between meetings.
  • Serve as the focal point for the Google Chromebook project.
  1. Stakeholder Coordination and Representation
  • Serve as the primary coordination focal point for digital transformation reforms, ensuring effective collaboration among Ministry directorates, development partners, implementing agencies, and other stakeholders.
  • Coordinate regularly with relevant MoE directorates and external stakeholders to ensure clarity of roles, timelines, and expected contributions.
  • Participate in technical committees, working groups, task teams, and workshops, providing inputs and ensuring follow-up on agreed actions.
  • Attend all MASAR supervision missions as the RA4 technical focal point.
  • Represent DCU’s coordination mandate at all Digital Transformation technical working groups and maintain proactive, technically substantive relationships with implementing agencies including UN agencies, development partners, private sector technology firms, telecom providers, universities, and others, as needed.
  1. Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification
  • Track all RA4-relevant MASAR DLRs and maintain a real-time DLR risk register; flag at-risk DLRs to the Program Manager and DCU Leadership with sufficient lead time for corrective action.
  • Monitor implementation progress across the broader digital transformation portfolio, maintaining oversight of milestones, deliverables, risks, dependencies, and corrective actions
  • Coordinate the preparation, consolidation, and quality assurance of DLR verification evidence, ensuring compliance with agreed verification protocols and readiness for independent verification reviews.
  • Review Verification reports submitted by the verification agency for the DLRs under result area 4.
  • Support monitoring, evaluation, reporting, verification, and learning requirements across digital transformation-related donor-funded programmes, ensuring timely provision of data, performance information, and evidence in accordance with donor requirements.
  • Support supervision missions, evaluations, audits, verification exercises, and technical assessments by ensuring data readiness and facilitating access to relevant information and stakeholders.
  1. Risk Management and Troubleshooting
  • Identify implementation risks, bottlenecks, and systemic constraints affecting RA4 and the broader digital transformation portfolio.
  • Provide timely solutions or mitigation measures and engage relevant directorates to resolve issues.
  • Escalate critical challenges to the Program Manager and DCU Deputy Director with clear problem statements and recommended actions.
  1. Knowledge Management and Institutional Strengthening
  • Facilitate knowledge exchange across MoE directorates and donor partners, ensuring that lessons learned, technical guidance, and best practices are captured and shared.
  • Support capacity-building efforts related to EdTech program management, digital pedagogy, AI-supported teaching, digital content development, school connectivity, device management, cybersecurity, data privacy, and DLR verification.
  • Promote institutionalization of MASAR RA4 processes and DCU digital transformation coordination mechanisms within MoE systems to strengthen long-term sustainability.
  • Document lessons from pilots and knowledge exchanges and ensure that they inform implementation manuals, technical standards, procurement documents, and training packages.

Duration and Location

Contract duration is 1 year with possible extension based on performance and availability of funding.

Full-time presence is required. The Senior Coordinator will be based at the Ministry of Education and Human Resources Development, Amman, Jordan.

Required Qualifications and Experience

  • Education: A bachelor's degree in Education, Digital Education, ICT, Computer Science, Public Policy, Economics, Development Studies, Engineering, or a related field. A master's degree is preferred, particularly in education policy, digital transformation, educational technology, public
  • Experience: At least 10 years of progressively responsible experience in education sector reform, digital transformation, EdTech implementation, programme management, or donor coordination, including at least 5 years in a leadership or coordination role involving multiple stakeholders.
  • Technical Skills: Deep understanding of digital education systems, school connectivity, device deployment, digital content, teacher digital pedagogy, AI-enabled education tools, data privacy, cybersecurity, child online protection, accessibility, and inclusive technology design. Strong background in results-based management, including work planning, monitoring progress, tracking indicators, maintaining risk registers, and preparing progress reports. Experience with PforR, DLI/DLR-based programmes, World Bank operations, or large-scale public-sector technology programs is a strong advantage. Familiarity with Jordan's education sector, digital government architecture, and the Economic Modernization Vision is desirable.
  • Stakeholder Engagement and Communication: Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, with a proven ability to engage and coordinate government officials, development partners, UN agencies, and private-sector stakeholders. Experience in facilitating workshops, leading working groups, and achieving consensus among diverse actors. Fluency in English and Arabic is required.
  • Political Economy and Organisational Skills: Strong political economy awareness with the ability to navigate complex multi-donor environments diplomatically. Self-driven, results-oriented, and capable of managing multiple simultaneous work streams. Demonstrated ability to produce high-quality, decision-ready briefings for senior leadership and meet tight deadlines.

Reporting and Institutional Arrangements

The Senior Coordinator shall report administratively to the MASAR Operational Program Manager and maintain a technical reporting line to the DCU Deputy Director for portfolio coordination functions. For day-to-day operations, the Senior Coordinator will work closely with designated focal points in the Ministry of Education and Human Resources Development, the World Bank task team, Digital Transformation donor programme teams, and DLR task team leaders as primary counterparts.

Submission 

Interested candidates are invited to submit their resume and any relevant certifications by the deadline specified in the announcement on the Ministry’s website, to the following email address: A.Orabi@moej.edu.jo 
Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted for an interview.

notice_text: M inistry of Education and Human Resources Development Modernizing Education, Skills, and Administrative Reforms (MASAR) Program Terms of Reference for:  Technical and Vocational Education and Training - TVET - Senior Coordinator Reference No.:  JO-MOE-566808-CS-INDV Program Background: The Modernizing Education, Skills, and Administrative Reforms (MASAR) Program for Results (PforR) is a transformative, system-wide reform initiative anchored in Jordan’s Economic Modernization Vision (EMV). The MASAR Operation is designed to support the Ministry of Education and Human Resources Development in addressing foundational bottlenecks in access, quality, and relevance of education, with a dual emphasis on equity and efficiency. The operation aims to strengthen institutional capacity while enabling measurable improvements in learning outcomes and employability, particularly through early childhood education and labor market-aligned technical and vocational education and training (TVET), and digital transformation in education. The program became effective in 2024, with a total financing envelope of USD 400 million, supported by the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD). It comprises two core components: Program-for-Results (PforR) : the principal financing instrument that disburses against verified achievement of results tied to government reform priorities. Investment Project Financing (IPF) : a complementary technical assistance (TA) component aimed at supporting the implementation of system-strengthening activities and accelerating the achievement of Disbursement Linked Indicators (DLIs). MASAR is structured around four interlinked Results Areas (RAs) that are strategically aligned with key education-sector transition points and cross-cutting governance reforms: RA1: Home to School – Expanding Access to Foundational Learning. This includes (i) increasing equitable access to KG2, particularly in under-served districts and refugee-hosting communities; (ii) enhancing the quality of early childhood education through a revised KG1-KG2 curriculum and quality assurance mechanisms; and (iii) improving foundational literacy skills for Grades 1–3 through targeted pedagogical interventions and a comprehensive implementation plan. RA2: School to Work – Increasing Access to Labor Market-Relevant TVET. MASAR seeks to improve the alignment of TVET with private sector needs by institutionalizing public-private partnerships, scaling apprenticeships, and expanding career guidance and employment pathways. This is complemented by the operationalization of an equivalency system that supports the portability and recognition of TVET qualifications, and enhanced use of learner trajectory data to inform student support services. RA3: Strengthening Sector Governance and Efficiency. The program supports the operationalization of a restructured governance model for the education sector and introduces reforms to human resource management, with a particular focus on teacher recruitment, deployment, and professional development policies. record.contact_address:

record.notice_text:
Ministry of Education and Human Resources Development

Modernizing Education, Skills, and Administrative Reforms (MASAR) Program

Terms of Reference for:  Technical and Vocational Education and Training - TVET - Senior Coordinator

Reference No.:  JO-MOE-566808-CS-INDV

Program Background:

The Modernizing Education, Skills, and Administrative Reforms (MASAR) Program for Results (PforR) is a transformative, system-wide reform initiative anchored in Jordan’s Economic Modernization Vision (EMV). The MASAR Operation is designed to support the Ministry of Education and Human Resources Development in addressing foundational bottlenecks in access, quality, and relevance of education, with a dual emphasis on equity and efficiency. The operation aims to strengthen institutional capacity while enabling measurable improvements in learning outcomes and employability, particularly through early childhood education and labor market-aligned technical and vocational education and training (TVET), and digital transformation in education.

The program became effective in 2024, with a total financing envelope of USD 400 million, supported by the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD). It comprises two core components:

  1. Program-for-Results (PforR): the principal financing instrument that disburses against verified achievement of results tied to government reform priorities.
  2. Investment Project Financing (IPF): a complementary technical assistance (TA) component aimed at supporting the implementation of system-strengthening activities and accelerating the achievement of Disbursement Linked Indicators (DLIs).

MASAR is structured around four interlinked Results Areas (RAs) that are strategically aligned with key education-sector transition points and cross-cutting governance reforms:

  • RA1: Home to School – Expanding Access to Foundational Learning. This includes (i) increasing equitable access to KG2, particularly in under-served districts and refugee-hosting communities; (ii) enhancing the quality of early childhood education through a revised KG1-KG2 curriculum and quality assurance mechanisms; and (iii) improving foundational literacy skills for Grades 1–3 through targeted pedagogical interventions and a comprehensive implementation plan.
  • RA2: School to Work – Increasing Access to Labor Market-Relevant TVET. MASAR seeks to improve the alignment of TVET with private sector needs by institutionalizing public-private partnerships, scaling apprenticeships, and expanding career guidance and employment pathways. This is complemented by the operationalization of an equivalency system that supports the portability and recognition of TVET qualifications, and enhanced use of learner trajectory data to inform student support services.
  • RA3: Strengthening Sector Governance and Efficiency. The program supports the operationalization of a restructured governance model for the education sector and introduces reforms to human resource management, with a particular focus on teacher recruitment, deployment, and professional development policies.
  • RA4: Digital Transformation in Education, to be introduced through the MASAR Additional Financing (AF), supporting digital and AI-enabled learning for students in Grades 4-12 and strengthening the institutional infrastructure needed for national-scale technology integration in education.

In addition to its core education objectives, MASAR embeds environmental and social sustainability principles across its implementation.

Ultimately, MASAR is designed to deliver measurable, inclusive, and sustainable improvements in Jordan’s education system. It expands access to early learning, strengthens foundational skills, improves graduate employability, strengthens digital skills, technology-enabled learning, and future-ready competencies, and reinforces institutional coherence through evidence-based policymaking. By supporting inclusive education and strengthening school-to-work transitions, the program directly contributes to Jordan’s long-term economic resilience and human capital development agenda.

Objectives of the Assignment:

The objective of this assignment is to provide strategic and operational support for the implementation of MASAR Result Area 2 and the coordination of the implementation of other projects supporting the Ministry of Education and Human Resource Development’s TVET development portfolio, ensuring achievement of Disbursement Linked Results (DLRs), alignment with national reform priorities, effective donor coordination, and timely delivery of evidence required for programme verification and disbursement.

The Senior Coordinator will support operational follow-up, troubleshoot bottlenecks, monitor implementation against the Annual Work Plan, and contribute to institutionalizing sustainable TVET governance, labour market alignment, and donor coordination mechanisms within MoE systems.

Specifically, the Senior Coordinator will:

  • Lead MASAR RA2 implementation, driving progress against all DLR milestones and ensuring that TA inputs are sequenced to deliver required results on time.
  • Serve as the coordination focal point responsible for tracking, consolidating, and supporting delivery of all RA2-related DLRs and associated verification evidence.
  • Support the timely achievement of MASAR DLRs by facilitating coordination and sequencing across relevant donor-supported programmes, ensuring that required inputs are aligned with DLR timelines.
  • Coordinate the DCU’s full TVET donor portfolio, ensuring strategic alignment with the ESP 2026–2030 and preventing duplication across programmes, to prevent misalignment between parallel donor interventions through structured division-of-labour processes.
  • Produce regular, analytically rigorous TVET portfolio and RA2 progress reporting for DCU leadership and MASAR operational program management
  • Identify portfolio gaps for unresourced TVET priority areas.

Scope of Work

  1. MASAR RA2 Planning and Implementation
  • Develop, update, and closely monitor annual action plans for RA2, ensuring alignment with MASAR’s overall results framework, DLR timelines, and MoE priorities.
  • Break activities into operational tasks with clear milestones, dependencies, and responsible units.
  • Support the preparation and review of annual work plans, budgets, and implementation schedules to ensure timely delivery of programme results.
  • Conduct periodic implementation reviews and recommend adjustments to activities, sequencing, resource allocation, and technical assistance arrangements to maintain progress toward DLR achievement.
  • Provide regular progress reports against implementation for result area 2 workplan under MASAR, including the preparation of MASAR's bi-annual progress reports.
  • Supports the Managing Director of TVET at MoE in the preparation of TORs for activities identified in the workplan
  1. TVET Portfolio Coordination and Donor Alignment
  • Maintain and analyse the TVET Projects Matrix as a strategic portfolio management tool, identifying gaps, duplication risks, sequencing challenges, and opportunities for synergies across interventions.
  • Advise DCU leadership on the prioritisation, alignment, endorsement, modification, and coordination of TVET initiatives to support implementation of the Education Strategic Plan (ESP) and national reform priorities.
  • Screen new TVET programme proposals and assess their alignment with sector priorities, existing interventions, and donor investments.
  • Facilitate division-of-labour arrangements among development partners and stakeholders, ensuring clarity of roles, responsibilities, expected results, and implementation timelines.
  • Identify un-resourced TVET priority areas and support resource mobilisation efforts through engagement with development partners and relevant stakeholders.
  • Provide regular progress reports against implementation of the DCU’s full TVET donor portfolio.
  • Maintain cluster meeting records and action trackers; ensure follow-through on agreed actions between meetings.
  1. Stakeholder Coordination and Representation
  • Serve as the primary coordination focal point for TVET-related reforms, ensuring effective collaboration among Ministry directorates, development partners, implementing agencies, and other stakeholders.
  • Coordinate regularly with relevant MoE directorates and external stakeholders to ensure clarity of roles, timelines, and expected contributions.
  • Participate in technical committees, working groups, task teams, and workshops, providing inputs and ensuring follow-up on agreed actions.
  • Attend all MASAR supervision missions as the DCU TVET/RA2 technical focal point.
  • Represent DCU’s coordination mandate at all TVET technical working groups and maintain proactive, technically substantive relationships with implementing agencies including UNESCO, ILO, GIZ, and others.
  1. Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification
  • Track all TVET-relevant MASAR DLRs and maintain a real-time DLR risk register; flag at-risk DLRs to the Program Manager and DCU Leadership with sufficient lead time for corrective action.
  • Monitor implementation progress across the broader TVET portfolio, maintaining oversight of milestones, deliverables, risks, dependencies, and corrective actions
  • Coordinate the preparation, consolidation, and quality assurance of DLR verification evidence, ensuring compliance with agreed verification protocols and readiness for independent verification reviews.
  • Review Verification reports submitted by the verification agency for the DLRs under result area 2.
  • Support monitoring, evaluation, reporting, verification, and learning requirements across TVET-related donor-funded programmes, ensuring timely provision of data, performance information, and evidence in accordance with donor requirements.
  • Support supervision missions, evaluations, audits, verification exercises, and technical assessments by ensuring data readiness and facilitating access to relevant information and stakeholders.
  1. Risk Management and Troubleshooting
  • Identify implementation risks, bottlenecks, and systemic constraints affecting RA2 and the broader TVET portfolio.
  • Provide timely solutions or mitigation measures and engage relevant directorates to resolve issues.
  • Escalate critical challenges to the Operational Program Manager and DCU Deputy Director with clear problem statements and recommended actions.
  1. Knowledge Management and Institutional Strengthening
  • Facilitate knowledge exchange across MoE directorates and donor partners, ensuring that lessons learned, technical guidance, and best practices are captured and shared.
  • Support capacity-building efforts related to TVET programme delivery, labour market alignment, and TVET qualification equivalency systems.
  • Promote institutionalization of MASAR RA2 processes and DCU TVET coordination mechanisms within MoE systems to strengthen long-term sustainability.

Duration and Location

Contract duration is 1 year with possible extension based on performance and availability of funding.

Full-time presence is required. The Senior Coordinator will be based at the Ministry of Education and Human Resource Development, Amman, Jordan

Required Qualifications and Experience

  • Education: A bachelor’s degree in Education, Public Policy, TVET, Economics, Development Studies, or a related field. A Master’s degree is preferred, particularly in education policy, international development, or labour market economics.
  • Experience: At least 10 years of progressively responsible experience in education sector reform, TVET systems development, programme management, or donor coordination, including at least 5 years in a leadership or coordination role involving multiple stakeholders.
  • Technical Skills: Deep knowledge of TVET systems, governance, qualifications frameworks, and labour market linkages. Strong background in results-based management, including developing work plans, monitoring progress, tracking indicators, and preparing progress reports. Experience with Programme for Results (PforR) or DLI-based programmes is a strong advantage. Familiarity with Jordan’s education sector, TVET system, and the Economic Modernisation Vision is desirable.
  • Stakeholder Engagement and Communication: Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, with a proven ability to engage and coordinate government officials, development partners, UN agencies, and private-sector stakeholders. Experience in facilitating workshops, leading working groups, and achieving consensus among diverse actors. Fluency in English and Arabic is required.
  • Political Economy and Organisational Skills: Strong political economy awareness with the ability to navigate complex multi-donor environments diplomatically. Self-driven, results-oriented, and capable of managing multiple simultaneous work streams. Demonstrated ability to produce high-quality, decision-ready briefings for senior leadership and meet tight deadlines.

Reporting and Institutional Arrangements

The Senior Coordinator shall report administratively to the MASAR Program Operational Manager maintain a technical reporting line to the DCU Deputy Director for portfolio coordination functions. For day-to-day operations, the Senior Coordinator will work closely with designated focal points in the Ministry of Education and Human Resource Development, the World Bank task team, TVET donor programme teams, and DLR task team leaders as primary counterparts.

Submission 

Interested candidates are invited to submit their resume and any relevant certifications by the deadline specified in the announcement on the Ministry’s website, to the following email address: a.abumtawea@moej.edu.jo
Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted for an interview.

notice_text: Specific Procurement Notice Template Request for Bids Small Works (One-Envelope Bidding Process)   Country: Lebanon Name of Project: Lebanon Emergency Assistance Project (LEAP) Contract Title: Damaged Roads Clearing and Restoration in South Lebanon - Bint Jbeil Caza. Loan No.: 9841 - LB                                                                                   RFB Reference No.: LEAP-SW2-Bint Jbeil   2. The Republic of Lebanon (hereinafter called “Borrower”) has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Lebanon Emergency Assistance Project (LEAP) and intends to apply part of the proceeds toward payments under the contract for “ Damaged Roads Clearing and Restoration in South Lebanon - Bint Jbeil Caza .  For this contract, the Borrower shall process the payments using the Direct Payment disbursement method, as defined in the World Bank’s Disbursement Guidelines for Investment Project Financing.   2. The Council for Development and Reconstruction (CDR) now invites sealed Bids from eligible Bidders for the Damaged Roads Clearing and Restoration in South Lebanon - Bint Jbeil Caza , consisting of providing restoration works.   3. Bidding will be conducted through National competitive procurement using a Request for Bids (RFB) as specified in the World Bank’s “ Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers - Sixth Edition, February 2025” , and is open to all Bidders as defined in the Procurement Regulations. The contract will be awarded to the Bidder offering the lowest evaluated cost to the Employer, subject that the selected Bidder meets the required qualification criteria, and the requirements as specified under paragraph 4 below.   4. Bidders submitting their bids, must ensure that the following criteria are met and included in their bid:  Financial capabilities requirements stipulated in Section III - Evaluation and Qualification Criteria - Eligibility and Qualification Criteria Paragraph 3.1 Average Annual Construction Turnover requirements stipulated in Section III - Evaluation and Qualification Criteria - Eligibility and Qualification Criteria Paragraph 3.2 Key Personnel stipulated in Section III - Evaluation and Qualification Criteria Paragraph 4. Equipment stipulated in Section III - Evaluation and Qualification Criteria Paragraph 5.     5. Interested eligible Bidders may obtain further information from the Council for Development and Reconstruction and inspect the bidding documents at the address given below from 9:00 to 15:00 hours (Beirut local time) from Monday till Friday .   6. Interested eligible Bidders may purchase the bidding documents. The bidding document in English may be purchased by interested eligible Bidders upon the submission of a written application to the address below and upon payment of a nonrefundable fee of One Hundred fresh US Dollars (US$ 100) . The method of payment will be in cash (fresh USD) . The document is to be picked up by a person duly authorized by the applicant. The cash is collected by the Tenders Department at CDR, and a receipt is issued to the person purchasing the bidding document at the time of payment.   7. Bids must be delivered to the address below at or before 12:00 noon Beirut Local Time on Thursday, October 29, 2026 .  Electronic Bidding will not be permitted.  Late Bids will be rejected. Bids will be publicly opened in the presence of the Bidders’ designated representatives and anyone who chooses to attend at the address below at 12:00 noon Beirut Local Time on Thursday, October 29, 2026 .   8. All Bids must be accompanied by a Bid Security of One Hundred Sixty Thousand fresh US Dollars (US$ 160,000) .   9. All Bids must be accompanied by a Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (SEA) and/or Sexual Harassment (SH) Declaration.   10. Attention is drawn to the Procurement Regulations requiring the Borrower to disclose information on the successful bidder’s beneficial ownership, as part of the Contract Award Notice, using the Beneficial Ownership Disclosure Form as included in the bidding document.   11. A Pre-Bid Meeting (Physical Presence) will be held on Friday, October 23, 2026 at 10:00 A.M. Beirut Local Time.                                                                                                    . Place: Council for Development and Reconstruction (CDR) Tallet Al Serail, Beirut Central District (BCD) First Floor CDR Board Meeting Room   12. The address referred to above is: Council for Development and Reconstruction (CDR) Tenders Department Tallet El-Serail, Room No. 1166 Beirut - Lebanon Telephone: +961 1 981431/2 - Facsimile: +961 1 981255 Web site address: www.cdr.gov.lb
