record.notice_text:
NATIONAL LOCAL GOVERNMENT FINANCE COMMITTEE

                      Governance to Enable Service Delivery (GESD) Project – GESD 2.0

                                                  Agreement No:  IDA-E6540

Individual Consultant- Project Engineer (2)

No: MW-NLGFC-563895-CS-INDIV/ MW-NLGFC-563897-CS-INDIV

                     

                                          Date of Issue: 20th August ,2026

  1. Background

 

The Government of Malawi (GoM) through the National Local Government Finance Committee (NLGFC) has received financing towards the cost of Governance to Enable Service Delivery (GESD) Project. The NLGFC intends to apply part of the proceeds of this financing to eligible payments under the contract for hiring two Project Engineer on a three - year contract renewable annually based on performance and availability of financial resources or mutually agreed by both parties.    

 

NLGFC therefore invites applications from suitably qualified and interested candidates to fill the position of two (2) Project Engineer tenable at the NLGFC Offices. The terms of Reference (TORs) for two (2) Project Engineer) are as follows:

 

2. The Objectives of the Assignment

The Project Engineer (Specialist) shall lead, coordinate and support local authorities and all relevant ministries, departments and agencies in the design and implementation of the project. The Project Engineer (Specialist) will lead and have approving authority for preparing and/or interpreting designs, bill of quantities (BoQs), tendering and engineering cost estimates prepared. The Project Engineer (Specialist) will work closely with relevant district authorities, including district engineers, other officers and specialists in the PIT, including safeguards, Project Coordinator, NLGFC, MoLGRD and other relevant stakeholders, including but not limited to supervision consultants. The Project Engineer (Specialist) will support monitoring of the sub-projects and will address and manage technical engineering questions in local investment projects implemented by the local authorities that are financed by GESD 2.0. 

 

  1. Duties and Responsibilities of the Project Engineer (Consultant)

 

The Project Engineers (Consultants) will be responsible for providing technical leadership and engineering oversight to ensure that project activities are planned, designed, implemented, monitored, and completed in accordance with approved specifications, quality standards, budget, schedule, and applicable regulations.

 

Specific tasks will include the following:

 

  1. Coordinate and support all engineering functions and activities related to infrastructure construction and rehabilitation in the local authorities, namely Department of Planning and Development and Department of Public Works;
  2. Support data collection for all proposed sub-project sites to aid development and customisation of architectural designs, production of BoQs and engineering estimates, tendering processes and ensuring that designs are in conformity with results of site-specific resilience and risk related investigations and analysis;
  3. Ensure timely and correct submission of information into the Public Management Information System (PMIS) by local authorities;
  4. Provide technical support to the Local Authorities in project selection, reviewing annual investment plans, works designs, BoQs, costs estimate, tendering, supervision and monitoring;
  5. Coordinate topographic surveys for the design of infrastructure to be developed under the Project;
  6. Support local authorities in conducting initial site investigation;
  7. Facilitate the production of location maps and sketches if necessary for all engineering sites that need maintenance and repair (selected as subprojects under GESD 2.0);
  8. Support and if necessary lead the review and approval of submissions by design engineers, including ensuring timely submission of the same;
  9. Support and if necessary lead design options stakeholder consultations with communities and relevant departments so that their inputs are incorporated in the designs to ensure acceptance and ownership of solutions to be developed;
  10. Conduct technical supervision of all construction works ensuring that the works are implemented to the required standards, within the assigned cost and time;
  11. Check Supervision Consultant’s work so as to conduct verification of contractors’ payment claims for works done;
  12. Manage changes to engineering constructions works ensuring that any changes have no adverse effect on the project and they are undertaken following project works change protocols, including documentation;
  13. Facilitate preparation of work plans and budgets for local investment projects to ensure relevance to outputs and outcomes of local investment project;
  14. Support the preparation of schedule of works and materials for project activities in collaboration with relevant stakeholders;
  15. Review and assess contractors’ and consultants’ payment certificates for engineering works
  16. Prepare and conduct training programs for Local Authority technical staff involved in contract and procurement management; and other related activities as directed by the PIT;
  17. Ensure compliance with all statutory and regulatory requirements;
  18. Liaise with other project specialists and officers, including safeguards, occupational health & safety, procurement, and advise the PIT on all construction Engineering technical related matters;
  19. Collect projects’ progress reports from the LAs, liaise with the monitoring & evaluation officer in the PIT in producing reports for project activities, consolidate them and submit them to PIT/PC, Executive Director and World Bank Task Team;
  20. Preparation and timely submission of monthly, quarterly and annual engineering project progress reports and other reports to the Project Coordinator, Executive Director and the World Bank Task Team.
  21. Facilitating the review of Annual Investment Plans (AIPs) for Local authorities and provide guidance on cost and time estimates.

 

  1. Deliverables

 

Deliverables for the assignment correspond to the duties and responsibilities above. Specifically, they will comprise:

 

  1. Timely review of AIPs submitted by local authorities, including review of cost and time estimates;
  2. Reviewed and approved engineering designs and drawings.
  3. Technical specifications and BoQs.
  4. Engineering project progress reports and other reports timely compiled
  5. Site inspection reports.
  6. Quality assurance and quality control (QA/QC) reports.
  7. Defects and corrective action reports.
  8. Monthly and quarterly progress reports, aligned with PMIS information.
  9. Physical progress monitoring reports.
  10. Work completion certificates.

 

  1. Performance Criteria

 

The following performance criteria will be used to assess the performance of the Project Engineer annually and based upon these assessments the contract with the project (GESD 2.0) may be continued or terminated:

  • 100% of required technical reports submitted on time.
  • At least 95% compliance with approved engineering specifications and quality standards.
  • Site inspections conducted according to approved supervision schedules.
  • 100% of contractor payment certificates reviewed and processed within agreed timelines.
  • All identified defects and non-compliance issues addressed within specified corrective action periods.
  • Minimal cost and schedule overruns attributable to technical deficiencies.
  • No major engineering failures or quality-related incidents.
  • Timely completion and handover of project infrastructure.
  • PMIS utilization by local authorities.

 

  1. Qualifications, Skills and Expertise

 

The candidate should meet the following minimum qualifications:

 

  1. Bachelor’s Degree in Civil Engineering/Architecture/Quantity Surveying
  2. Master’s Degree in Construction/Engineering related field and ;
  3. Registration with an approved professional body, such as Malawi Engineering Institution/Board of Architects and Quantity Surveyors
  4. A minimum of 8 years of relevant working experience;
  5. Excellent communications, writing/reporting skills;
  6. Proficiency in computer aided design packages (AutoCAD, ArchCAD, GIS etc)
  7. Proficient in the use of Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Microsoft Project etc.);
  8. Strong organizational, self-starting and communications skills;
  9. Experience working with government institutions and organizations; working experience with local authorities in Malawi is considered an advantage;
  10. Highly motivated and enthusiastic person with excellent planning, analytical, communications and interpersonal skills as well as a high level of diplomacy; and
  11. Excellent oral and written communication skills in English, as well as team participation and management skills

 

  1. Reporting Arrangements

 

The Project Engineer (Specialist) will primarily report to the Project Coordinator with a technical reporting line to the Director of Social and Economic Services at NLGFC for all technical matters, and will support local authorities’ in implementation of GESD 2.0 project.

 

  1. Location of Assignment

 

The Project Engineer (Specialist) will be based at the NLGFC offices in Lilongwe. The Project Engineer (Consultant) will occasionally be required to travel to local government authorities in Malawi where the Project is implementing its activities to engage with district officials to guide and improve project implementation.

 

  1. Duration of Assignment

 

The assignment is expected to span a total period of up to three (3) years, with annual performance reviews and contract extensions subject to satisfactory performance.

.

8.MODE OF APPLICATION

 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14. 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations of IPF Borrowers” dated September, 2025 (“Procurement regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest and A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultant (INDV) selection method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

 

Further information including the detailed Terms of Reference (TORs) can be obtained at the address below during office hours from 7:30 hours to 12:00 hours and from 13:00 hours to 16:30 hours except on Weekends and Public Holidays

 

9. SUBMISSION OF APPLICATIONS

Interested applicants who meet the above requirements should submit application letters together with concise Curriculum Vitae (CV), National ID, and copies of relevant certificates to the address below not later than 17.30 hours on Friday, 11th September 2026.

The National Local Government Finance Committee (NLGFC) is committed to diversifying Gender equality in its operations and strongly encourages women to apply for the above vacant position.

The Executive Director

National Local Government Finance Committee

Area 14, Red Cross Building

Presidential Way

P.O. Box 31162

Lilongwe 3

Or through the following email address:

recruitment@nlgfc.gov.mw/ ed@nlgfc.gov.mw

Only shortlisted applicants will be considered for further assessments.

record.notice_text:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

EDUCATION AND RESEARCH Specialist

 (CONSULTING SERVICES - INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT SELECTION)

Country                             Ghana

Project Title                      Learning and Evidence Agenda for Regional Collaboration in Eastern and Southern Africa (LEARN-ESA)

GRANT No.                        E7330TD

Project ID No.                    P516274  

Assignment Title               Education and Learning Specialist  

 The Association of African Universities has received financing from the World Bank towards the cost of the Learning and Evidence Agenda for Regional Collaboration in Eastern and Southern Africa (LEARN-ESA) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services for the engagement of an individual consultant as the Education and Research Specialist at the AAU Headquarters in Accra, Ghana.

Roles and Responsibilities

Under the direct supervision of the Director of Special Projects, the Education and Research Specialist will provide technical and academic leadership for the projects regional learning agenda and implementation research initiatives. The Specialist will manage relationships with regional research partners, research teams, and technical consultants, ensuring that all regional public goods and knowledge assets align seamlessly with country demands.

Functionally, the Education and Research Specialist will serve as the core technical anchor for Component 1 and Component 2 execution, collaborating closely with the Policy Specialist, M&E Specialist, and country networks to translate empirical evidence into actionable, system-wide basic education policy reforms across the six participating member states (Angola, Comoros, Ethiopia, Madagascar, Malawi, and Mozambique).

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following link: https://repository.aau.org/index.php/s/znpMttR39r6bxWa

The Association of African Universities now invites eligible individuals (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services.

Competency and Expertise

Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience and competencies to perform the Services as elaborated in the Terms of Reference.

Applications dossier

  1. A cover letter including a statement of interest and suitability for the position and an indication of the date on which the candidate is available to start work.
  2. A detailed curriculum vitae describing the candidate's professional experience and qualifications for the position
  3. Supporting documents for the qualifications listed in the curriculum vitae (copies of certificates)
  4. At least two (2) letters of recommendation, one of which must be from a country outside the candidate's country of origin

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.13, 3.14, and 3.16 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers Seventh Edition, September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), [Procurement in Investment Project Financing; Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services], setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest available on this link. https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099120102072534901/pdf/SECBOS-a43bff5f-35cb-48e0-9609-10773aaa8d12.pdf

A consultant will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultant Selection method set out in Section VII of the Procurement Regulations and the selection process outline under Section 4.5 of the Terms of Reference.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours 0900 to 1700 hours Monday to Friday per email to smkandawire@aau.org

Submission Instructions and Applications Deadline

  1. Applications and supporting documents must be submitted online at https://www.research.net/r/EduResS26 , no later than Monday 2nd November at 23:59 GMT .
  2. At least two (2) letters of recommendation must be sent directly by the reference persons , online at https://www.research.net/r/RefEduResS26  , with the subject line “Confidential Reference -  LEARN-ESA”, no later than Monday 9th November 2026 at 23:59 GMT.

Applications not complying with the submission requirements above may not be considered.

The AAU subscribes to the principle of equal opportunities. In line with its commitment to reflecting the diversity of the African academic world, applications from women are strongly encouraged.

notice_text: Request for Expressions of Interest (REoI) Individual Consultant Service as Gender and SEA/SH Expert (National) Country                     : Bangladesh Name of the Project : Sylhet-Charkhai-Sheola Highway Improvement Project under ACCESS PROGRAM  Credit No                   : IDA Credit 7786-BD Assignment Title       : Individual Consultant Service as Gender and SEA/SH Expert (National) Reference No             : Package No: SP-9   1.    The Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh (GoB) has received a credit from the International Development Association (IDA) towards the cost of the Sylhet-Charkhai-Sheola Highway Improvement Project under ACCESS Program. The RHD, an implementing agency of the Project intends to apply a part of the proceeds of this credit to eligible payments under the contract for which this Request for Expressions of Interest is invited. 2.    The Objective of this assignment is to seek the services of an experienced Individual Consultant to work as the Gender and SEA/SH expert to, support the PIU to ensure equitable distribution of benefits across gender, recommend measures for mitigating and managing any adverse gender impacts, including potential impacts related to GBV and SEA/SH. The detailed scope of the consultancy service is mentioned in the ToR. Detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) and other information will be available upon request from the address provided below, either through email or in person. The TOR can also be found at ‘Sylhet-Sheola Project’ corner of the RHD website (rhd.portal.gov.bd).   3.    The expected date for the commencement of services is January 2027. The assignment will have an input of Twenty-four (24) Man-Months, depending on the need of the Client and satisfactory performance of the Consultant. The Contract period shall be determined as per mutual agreement of both parties. The Contract period may be extended on mutually agreed terms if required as per rules and regulation of WB and GoB.  4.    The Consultant will be selected using Individual Consultant Selection (ICS) Method (Open-National) following the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (7th Edition, September 2025). The selected Consultant shall sign the contract with Project Director, Sylhet-Charkhai-Sheola Highway Improvement Project, RHD. Interested Applicants are required to provide information demonstrating that they possess the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the services. The selection criteria are – •    Educational Qualifications: The consultant should have an appropriate post-graduate degree in Social Science/Social Work/Anthropology/Mass Communication/Gender Studies/Women studies or equivalent qualification in a related field. Formal training/course on gender planning/analysis/management is preferred. •    Experience: At least 8 years of general work experience in the area of gender/social development/stakeholder management/grievance management etc., including 4 years of specific working experience on this type of management in development partner funded projects or reputed international organizations. The Gender expert should have specifically worked on preparation or implementation of social safeguards or gender assessments/management for at least 01 large scale Infrastructure development project. Familiarity with and demonstrated experience of applying tools for gender analysis or developing strategies for gender mainstreaming in development projects will be considered as added advantage. Applicants are required to submit their Expressions of Interest (EoIs), comprising a CV (including employment history with duties and responsibilities) and a forwarding letter describing briefly the reasons that the applicant considers him/her-self best suited to perform the assignment. 5.    The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to the Section III, para 3.13, 3.15, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, Seventh Edition, September 2025 ("Procurement Regulations"), setting forth the World Bank's policy on conflict of interest. 6.    Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours (09:00 AM to 04:00 PM Bangladesh Standard Time). 7.    The authority reserves the right to accept or reject any or all of EOIs. Expressions of Interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person, or by mail, or by fax, or by e-mail) by 1:00 PM (Bangladesh Standard Time), November 25, 2026.

record.notice_text:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (REOI) 

(INDIVIDUAL CONSULTING SERVICES) 

 

Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI) 

Digital RMI Project 

P171517 

 

Assignment Title:  

Reference No.: MH-DIDA-576425-CS-INDV Digital Unit: Government Technical Support Specialist/s 

(Majuro based position) 

 

The Government of the Republic of the Marshall Islands (the Government) is undertaking a major investment program supported by the World Bank under the Digital RMI Project (Project).  The development objective includes establishing the critical foundations for digital government services and the digital economy. 

 

To support the development of digital government services and a digital economy the Government, with World Bank funding support, has established a Digital Unit reporting into the Office of the Chief Secretary.  

The Project is under implementation and closes in August 2028. The Digital Unit is based in Majuro and currently comprises two Technical Support Specialists, with the Director position under open competitive recruitment. Work currently underway includes the migration of government users to Microsoft 365, an Azure landing zone, consolidation of government onto the rmi.gov.mh domain, a new government web portal, electronic signature and workflow tooling, and the first e-Services and Digital ID releases. 

 

The Director of the Digital Unit is now seeking to recruit a third technical support specialist staff member who will help progress the Digital Unit work program and support the rollout of the Microsoft platform, and applications as approved in the RMI Future State Roadmap Report.  The role involves working closely with relevant Ministry(s) to provide technical support for the implementation of and migration to the Microsoft platform and associated applications. 

 

 A description of the Digital Unit’s functions is set out in the position description in terms of reference, and a copy of the Future State Roadmap Report can be provided on request. 

 

The role is based in Majuro.  This is a full-time position and is for a contracted period from 1 January 2027 to 31 August 2028 (with the possibility of an extension), with a 3-month probationary period.  It is expected that the role will commence on or about 1 January 2027.  The remuneration will reflect the fact that this is a contracted role and not a permanent public sector role. 

 

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be supplied on request to the Project Officer galbert.robert@rmi.gov.mh. 

 

Division of International Development Assistance (DIDA) now invites eligible Individuals (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services.  Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services (attach curriculum vitae with description of experience in similar assignments, similar conditions, etc.). The criteria for selecting the Consultant are: 

 

Mandatory Requirements (pass /fail) 

The successful candidate shall:  

 

  1. Qualification (associate degree or equivalent, or higher) experience in Information Technology, Computer Science, or a related field ora minimum of 2 years of experience in technical support roles, preferably in a similar organizational context. 

 

  1. Proven expertise in administering networks, hardware, software, and operating systems 

 

  1. Advanced troubleshooting skills with a track record of effectively diagnosing and resolving complex technical issues. 

 

Additional Desirable Requirements: 

 

  1. Experience in implementing and supporting Microsoft Products (Microsoft 365 and Azure) 

 

  1. Supporting Cloud infrastructure – an understanding of cloud architecture and operating principles 

 

  1. Demonstrated experience in coordinating software procurement and managing licensing tracking systems. 

 

  1. Strong communication and interpersonal abilities, with a knack for conveying technical concepts clearly. 

 

  1. Previous experience in conducting training sessions and facilitating knowledge transfer among team members. 

 

 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraph 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers dated November 2020 (“the Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.  

 

Expressions of interest must be delivered in written form to the address below (in person, or by e-mail) by no later than 5pm 20 November 2026 (RMI time). 

 

Galbert Robert 

Project Officer 

RMI Digital Unit 

to galbert.robert@rmi.gov.mh

notice_text:   REPUBLICA DE MOÇAMBIQUE MINISTÉRIO DAS OABRAS PÚBLICAS, HABITAÇÃO E RECURSOS HÍDRICOS DIRECÇÃO NACIONAL DE GESTÃO DE RECURSOS HÍDRICOS PROGRAMA REGIONAL DE RESILIÊNCIA CLIMÁTICA PARA ÁFRICA ORIENTAL E AUSTRAL (P180171)   Solicitação de Propostas Pequenas Obras (Processo de Concurso de Um Envelope)   País: Moçambique Nome do Projecto: Projecto Regional de Resiliência Climática Título do contrato: Fornecimento e Instalação de Equipamento Hidroclimatológicos em 3 Lotes Empréstimo N.º/Crédito N.º/Subvenção N.º: IDA-E1950 Número de referência da SDP: MZ-DNGRH-549566-GO-RFB   A Direcção Nacional de Gestão de Recursos Hídricos recebeu financiamento do Banco Mundial para custear o Projecto Regional de Resiliência Climáctica , e pretende aplicar parte dos fundos para pagamentos ao abrigo do contrato para Fornecimento e Instalação de Equipamento Hidroclimatológicos em 3 Lotes 2.    A Direcção Nacional de Gestão de Recursos Hídricos (DNGRH), convida os Concorrentes elegíveis a apresentarem Propostas seladas para o Fornecimento e Instalação de Equipamento Hidroclimatológico em 3 Lotes: LOTE I:         Estações Climaticas e Telemetria, Escalas Hidrométricas, Equipamentos de Medição de Caudal e Topográfia Digital; Equipamento remoto de transmissão e comunicação de dados, Kits de Primeiros socorros;   LOTE II:        Equipamento de águas subterrâneas, kits de qualidade da água, Equpamento de GPS, hardware de informática para processamento de imagens fotogramétricas .   LOTE III:      Veículos Aéreos Não Tripulados para levantamento topográfico (Drones), Sistema de Posicionamento Global Portátil (Equipamentos GPS), Equipamentos de transmissão e comunicação remota de dados, e Hardware de Tecnologia da Informação para Processamento Fotogramétrico   Com previsão de início em Novembro de 2026 e conclusão Março de 2027 . 3.      O processo será conduzido através de concurso nacional usando uma Solicitação de Propostas (SDP), conforme especificado no “Regulamento de Aquisições para Mutuários de IPF” do Banco Mundial Julho de 2021 (“Regulamento de Aquisições”), estando aberto a todos os Concorrentes elegíveis conforme definido no Regulamento de Aquisições. 4.      Os Concorrentes elegíveis interessados podem obter mais informações junto do Departamento de Aquisições e analisar o Documento de Concurso durante o horário de expediente das 07:30 às 15:30 no endereço abaixo indicado . 5.      O Documento de Concurso em língua portuguesa pode ser adquirido pelos Concorrentes interessados mediante a apresentação de um pedido escrito no endereço abaixo O documento será enviado por correio electrónico e/ou levantamento físico no endereço baixo indicado. 6.      As propostas devem ser entregues no endereço abaixo. A Apresentação de Propostas por via electrónica não será permitida. Propostas Tardias serão rejeitadas. As Propostas serão abertas publicamente na presença dos representantes designados dos Concorrentes e de qualquer pessoa que decida participar, no endereço abaixo em 24 de Setembro de 2026, pelas 10:00. 7.      Todas as Propostas devem ser acompanhadas por Garantia Provisória no valor de Lote I: 750.000, 00 MT Lote II: 450.000, 00 MT Lote III: 700.000, 00 MT 8.      Chama-se a atenção para o Regulamento de Aquisições que exige que o Mutuário divulgue informações sobre a propriedade efectiva do concorrente seleccionado, como parte do Anúncio de Adjudicação de Contrato, utilizando o Formulário de Divulgação da Propriedade Efectiva, tal como incluído no Documento de Concurso. 9.      Aos concorrentes que baixarem o Documento de Concurso directamente do Portal da UFSA, ( https://www.ufsa.gov.mz) favor de enviar o e-mail para o procurement.prrc@gmail.com , para efeitos de envio dos esclarecimentos a serem solicitados pelos concorrentes 10.    O endereço acima referido é:   Nome do local: Ministério de Obras Publicas, Habitação e Recursos Hídricos, Departamento de Aquisições Nome do representante: Chefe do Departamento Endereço: Av. Karl Max, n0 606, Cidade de Maputo, Moçambique Email: procurement.prrc@gmail.com Website: www.dngrh.gov.mz           Emitido em: 25 de Agosto de 2026

REPUBLICA DE MOÇAMBIQUE

MINISTÉRIO DAS OABRAS PÚBLICAS, HABITAÇÃO E RECURSOS HÍDRICOS

DIRECÇÃO NACIONAL DE GESTÃO DE RECURSOS HÍDRICOS

PROGRAMA REGIONAL DE RESILIÊNCIA CLIMÁTICA PARA ÁFRICA ORIENTAL E AUSTRAL (P180171)

 

Solicitação de Propostas

Pequenas Obras

(Processo de Concurso de Um Envelope)

 

País: Moçambique

Nome do Projecto: Projecto Regional de Resiliência Climática

Título do contrato: Fornecimento e Instalação de Equipamento Hidroclimatológicos em 3 Lotes

Empréstimo N.º/Crédito N.º/Subvenção N.º: IDA-E1950

Número de referência da SDP: MZ-DNGRH-549566-GO-RFB

 

A Direcção Nacional de Gestão de Recursos Hídricos recebeu financiamento do Banco Mundial para custear o Projecto Regional de Resiliência Climáctica, e pretende aplicar parte dos fundos para pagamentos ao abrigo do contrato para Fornecimento e Instalação de Equipamento Hidroclimatológicos em 3 Lotes 2.    A Direcção Nacional de Gestão de Recursos Hídricos (DNGRH), convida os Concorrentes elegíveis a apresentarem Propostas seladas para o Fornecimento e Instalação de Equipamento Hidroclimatológico em 3 Lotes:

LOTE I:         Estações Climaticas e Telemetria, Escalas Hidrométricas, Equipamentos de Medição de Caudal e Topográfia Digital; Equipamento remoto de transmissão e comunicação de dados, Kits de Primeiros socorros;

 

LOTE II:        Equipamento de águas subterrâneas, kits de qualidade da água, Equpamento de GPS, hardware de informática para processamento de imagens fotogramétricas.

 

LOTE III:      Veículos Aéreos Não Tripulados para levantamento topográfico (Drones), Sistema de Posicionamento Global Portátil (Equipamentos GPS), Equipamentos de transmissão e comunicação remota de dados, e Hardware de Tecnologia da Informação para Processamento Fotogramétrico

 

Com previsão de início em Novembro de 2026 e conclusão Março de 2027.

3.      O processo será conduzido através de concurso nacional usando uma Solicitação de Propostas (SDP), conforme especificado no “Regulamento de Aquisições para Mutuários de IPF” do Banco Mundial Julho de 2021 (“Regulamento de Aquisições”), estando aberto a todos os Concorrentes elegíveis conforme definido no Regulamento de Aquisições.

4.      Os Concorrentes elegíveis interessados podem obter mais informações junto do Departamento de Aquisições e analisar o Documento de Concurso durante o horário de expediente das 07:30 às 15:30 no endereço abaixo indicado.

5.      O Documento de Concurso em língua portuguesa pode ser adquirido pelos Concorrentes interessados mediante a apresentação de um pedido escrito no endereço abaixo O documento será enviado por correio electrónico e/ou levantamento físico no endereço baixo indicado.

6.      As propostas devem ser entregues no endereço abaixo. A Apresentação de Propostas por via electrónica não será permitida. Propostas Tardias serão rejeitadas. As Propostas serão abertas publicamente na presença dos representantes designados dos Concorrentes e de qualquer pessoa que decida participar, no endereço abaixo em 24 de Setembro de 2026, pelas 10:00.

7.      Todas as Propostas devem ser acompanhadas por Garantia Provisória no valor de

  • Lote I: 750.000, 00 MT
  • Lote II: 450.000, 00 MT
  • Lote III: 700.000, 00 MT

8.      Chama-se a atenção para o Regulamento de Aquisições que exige que o Mutuário divulgue informações sobre a propriedade efectiva do concorrente seleccionado, como parte do Anúncio de Adjudicação de Contrato, utilizando o Formulário de Divulgação da Propriedade Efectiva, tal como incluído no Documento de Concurso.

9.      Aos concorrentes que baixarem o Documento de Concurso directamente do Portal da UFSA,(https://www.ufsa.gov.mz) favor de enviar o e-mail para o procurement.prrc@gmail.com, para efeitos de envio dos esclarecimentos a serem solicitados pelos concorrentes

10.    O endereço acima referido é:

 

Nome do local: Ministério de Obras Publicas, Habitação e Recursos Hídricos, Departamento de Aquisições

Nome do representante: Chefe do Departamento

Endereço: Av. Karl Max, n0 606, Cidade de Maputo, Moçambique

Email: procurement.prrc@gmail.com

Website: www.dngrh.gov.mz

notice_text: REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (CONSULTING SERVICES - INDIVIDUAL SELECTION)   UNITED REPUBLIC OF TANZANIA SUSTAINABLE RURAL WATER SUPPLY AND SANITATION PROGRAM (SRWSSP) PHASE II   Assignment Title: Consultancy Service for Engagement of an Individual Consultant to Provide Technical Expert Services in Water Resources Management   Reference No. TZ-MOWEM-576846-CS-INDV   The Revolutionary Government of Zanzibar (RGoZ), through the United Republic of Tanzania, has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of Sustainable Rural Water Supply and Sanitation Program (SRWSSP) Phase II and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.   Objective of the Assignment The overall objective of this assignment is to provide sustained technical support to the Ministry of Water, Energy and Minerals in strengthening water resources management systems in Zanzibar.   Specifically, the assignment aims to: Improve understanding of water resources availability and utilization Strengthen monitoring, data management, and decision-making systems Promote sustainable and equitable allocation of water resources Enhance climate resilience and environmental protection Strengthen institutional capacity for effective water governance The outputs of this assignment will be used to inform Future water resources and WASH investments in Zanzibar; strengthening of regulatory and abstraction control mechanisms; climate and drought preparedness planning; and coordination with development partners and the private sector, including utilities and major water users. Success of the assignment will be measured by improved availability of water resources information; informed and enhanced decisionmaking on water resources allocation, planning, abstraction and protection; strengthened institutional capacity and well-aligned practices; and increased readiness to manage climate and drought risks in water resources management.   Specific Tasks of the Consultant The Consultant will act as a Technical Advisor and Lead Expert , strengthening the institutional capacity of the Division of Water Resources Management by supporting analysis, providing technical guidance, undertaking capacity development endeavours and coordination, while implementation and daytoday data collection remain the responsibility of relevant institutions. The Technical Advisor shall support the Division of Water Resources Management through undertaking the following tasks: Undertake capacity appraisal for the division and identify strategic areas of support Conduct a comprehensive assessment of water resources, including groundwater and surface water systems. Review existing policies, laws, and strategies related to water resources management. Assess current water abstraction, usage patterns, and demand projections. Evaluate the status of aquifers, recharge areas, and catchment zones. Identify risks related to climate change, pollution, and over-extraction. Develop strategies for sustainable water resources management, including conservation and protection measures. Conduct consultations (physical and virtual) with experts and stakeholders at national, regional (Eastern & Southern Africa), and international levels to identify and promote best IWRM practices applicable to Zanzibar. Support Technical Assistance on drafting of new Water and Sanitation Act. record.notice_text:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES - INDIVIDUAL SELECTION)

 

UNITED REPUBLIC OF TANZANIA

SUSTAINABLE RURAL WATER SUPPLY AND SANITATION PROGRAM (SRWSSP) PHASE II

 

Assignment Title: Consultancy Service for Engagement of an Individual Consultant to Provide Technical Expert Services in Water Resources Management

 

Reference No. TZ-MOWEM-576846-CS-INDV

 

The Revolutionary Government of Zanzibar (RGoZ), through the United Republic of Tanzania, has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of Sustainable Rural Water Supply and Sanitation Program (SRWSSP) Phase II and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

 

Objective of the Assignment

The overall objective of this assignment is to provide sustained technical support to the Ministry of Water, Energy and Minerals in strengthening water resources management systems in Zanzibar.

 

Specifically, the assignment aims to:

  • Improve understanding of water resources availability and utilization
  • Strengthen monitoring, data management, and decision-making systems
  • Promote sustainable and equitable allocation of water resources
  • Enhance climate resilience and environmental protection
  • Strengthen institutional capacity for effective water governance

The outputs of this assignment will be used to inform

  1. Future water resources and WASH investments in Zanzibar;
  2. strengthening of regulatory and abstraction control mechanisms;
  3. climate and drought preparedness planning; and
  4. coordination with development partners and the private sector, including utilities and major water users.

Success of the assignment will be measured by improved availability of water resources information; informed and enhanced decisionmaking on water resources allocation, planning, abstraction and protection; strengthened institutional capacity and well-aligned practices; and increased readiness to manage climate and drought risks in water resources management.

 

Specific Tasks of the Consultant

The Consultant will act as a Technical Advisor and Lead Expert, strengthening the institutional capacity of the Division of Water Resources Management by supporting analysis, providing technical guidance, undertaking capacity development endeavours and coordination, while implementation and daytoday data collection remain the responsibility of relevant institutions. The Technical Advisor shall support the Division of Water Resources Management through undertaking the following tasks:

  • Undertake capacity appraisal for the division and identify strategic areas of support
  • Conduct a comprehensive assessment of water resources, including groundwater and surface water systems.
  • Review existing policies, laws, and strategies related to water resources management.
  • Assess current water abstraction, usage patterns, and demand projections.
  • Evaluate the status of aquifers, recharge areas, and catchment zones.
  • Identify risks related to climate change, pollution, and over-extraction.
  • Develop strategies for sustainable water resources management, including conservation and protection measures.
  • Conduct consultations (physical and virtual) with experts and stakeholders at national, regional (Eastern & Southern Africa), and international levels to identify and promote best IWRM practices applicable to Zanzibar.
  • Propose mechanisms for improving water resources monitoring, data collection, and information systems.
  • Support development of regulatory and institutional frameworks for effective water governance.
  • Support Technical Assistance on drafting of new Water and Sanitation Act.
  • Prepare and present technical reports and recommendations to the Ministry.

 

The Ministry of Water, Energy and Minerals now invites eligible expert to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are:

 

  • At least Master’s Degree in Water Resources Engineering, Hydrology, Environmental Engineering, or related field.
  • At least 12 years of experience in undertaking Water Resources Management projects.
  • Proven experience with international donor-funded programs (World Bank, AfDB, etc.).
  • Demonstrated completion of at least three (3) comparable assignments as an individual consultant or team leader.
  • Experience in national-level assignments. Must have participated in at least 1 assignment of a similar nature in Tanzania (mainland or Zanzibar)
  • Competency in water resource management analytics (especially groundwater), capacity development, team building, policy analysis, reporting, and stakeholder engagement.
  • Registered by the relevant registration and professional boards.
  • Fluency in written and spoken English; working experience in Water Sector in Zanzibar and knowledge of Kiswahili is a strong advantage.

 

The attention of interested consulting firms is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers”, Seventh Edition, September 2025, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. Consulting firms intending to submit an Expression of Interest shall not have any conflict of interest or unfair competitive advantage and must comply with the provisions of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations.

 

The Consultant will be selected in accordance with the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, Seventh Edition, September 2025, using the Individual Consultant Selection method through an open national competitive process.

 

(The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be Obtained through website: https://majismz.go.tz/publications or upon asking through Email: abubakar.bakar@majismz.go.tz  copy to hidayat.vuai@majismz.go.tz

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hour, 07:00 to 03.30pm East African Time.

notice_text:   REPUBLIQUE DU NIGER Fraternité-Travail-Progrès MINISTERE DE L’ECONOMIE ET DES FINANCES INSTITUT NATIONAL DE LA STATISTIQUE ETABLISSEMENT PUBLIC A CARACTERE ADMINISTRATIF DIRECTION GENERALE PROJET D’HARMONISATION ET D’AMELIORATION DES STATISTIQUES EN AFRIQUE DE L’OUEST ET DU CENTRE (PHASAOC) - CREDIT IDA 73140 NE 182, rue de la Sirba - BP 13416 Niamey - NIGER • Tél. : (227) 20 72 35 60 • Fax : (227) 20 72 21 74 • https://www.ins.ne • E-mail : ins@ins.ne   AVIS DE SOLLICITATION DE MANIFESTATION D’INTÉRÊT   SELECTION D'UN CABINET POUR LE RECRUTEMENT DU PERSONNEL COMPLEMENTAIRE DU BCR DANS LE CADRE DU 5 EME RGPH     CONTEXTE ET JUSTIFICATIONS    Dans le cadre de la mise en œuvre des activités du Projet d’Harmonisation et d’Amélioration des Statistiques en Afrique de l’Ouest et du Centre (PHASAOC), notamment la réalisation du Cinquième Recensement Général de la Population et de l’Habitat (RGP/H), l’Institut National de la Statistique (INS) a mis en place le Bureau Central de Recensement (BCR), organe technique chargé de la planification, de la coordination et du pilotage global des activités du recensement. Au regard de l’ampleur des opérations, de la charge de travail administrative et logistique pour le fonctionnement du BCR ainsi que des besoins en ressources humaines au BCR, il est nécessaire de recruter sous contrat à durée déterminée, quinze (15) démographes/Ingénieurs Statisticiens Economistes (ISE), six (06) Ingénieurs des Travaux/Pratiques Statistiques (ITS/IPS), trois (03) Techniciens Supérieurs de la Statistique (TSS), (9) comptables, deux (02) assistants administratifs, cinq (5) logisticiens, dix (10) chauffeurs et deux (02) manœuvres. Par ailleurs, il est prévu le recrutement de deux gardiens pour assurer la sécurité des sites et des matériels qui y seront entreposés, dans le cadre des travaux de construction des sièges de l’Institut National de la Statistique (INS) et de l’Ecole Nationale de la Statistique (ENSTAT). Ces recrutements visent, d’une part, à garantir le bon fonctionnement du BCR et à soutenir l’exécution efficace des activités préparatoires et opérationnelles du RGP/H et, d’autre part sécuriser les sites destinés aux travaux de construction des sièges de l’INS et de l’ENSTAT.   OBJECTIFS Objectif général L'objectif principal est de doter le Bureau Central de Recensement (BCR) d'un capital humain qualifié et opérationnel afin d'assurer une exécution fluide, rigoureuse et dans les délais de l'ensemble des activités du 5ème RGP/H. Objectifs spécifiques •             Renforcer l'expertise technique en matière de conception, d'analyse des données, de cartographie et de traitement statistique. •             Optimiser la gestion financière et comptable des ressources allouées à l'opération de recensement. •             Assurer un appui administratif et logistique rigoureux pour la gestion des flux de matériels, de la documentation et du déploiement sur le terrain. •             Garantir la mobilité et la manutention sécurisées des équipes et des équipements sur toute l'étendue du territoire •             Assurer la sécurité des sites destinés à la construction des sièges de l’INS et de l’ENSTAT.     LES RESULTATS ATTENDUS   Les résultats attendus de la mise en œuvre de cette activité sont : Sur le plan technique : Les méthodologies, les questionnaires, l'analyse des données et la production des rapports thématiques du 5ème RGP/H sont exécutés selon les standards internationaux de qualité. Sur le plan financier : La gestion des budgets est transparente, les pièces justificatives sont rigoureusement tenues et les rapports financiers sont produits à bonne date. Sur le plan administratif : l'archivage, le suivi des courriers et la gestion des ressources humaines du BCR sont assurés de manière fluide. Sur le plan logistique : L'approvisionnement, le stockage et le déploiement du matériel de recensement sont correctement gérés. Sur le plan opérationnel : Le déplacement des équipes d'encadrement et la manutention des équipements sont sécurisés et effectués dans le respect des calendriers établis ; Les sites destinés aux travaux de construction des sièges de l’INS et de l’ENSTAT sont sécurisés. ORGANISATION ET MÉTHODOLOGIE Un bureau de recrutement sera choisi pour appuyer la Direction Générale de l’Institut National de la Statistique (INS) dans le recrutement des candidats aux différents postes. Les profils recherchés pour les différents postes sont consignés dans le tableau ci-dessous. Profils Nbre Cat. Diplôme requis Expérience Durée du contrat Démographe 13 A1 Master professionnel en Démographie – Bac +5 - 12 mois ISE 2 A1 - - 12 mois IPS 6 A2 ITS/IPS - 12 mois TSS 3 A3 TSS - 12 mois Comptable 9 A3 Au moins un BTS d’État en comptabilité, finance, administration des affaires ou domaine connexe 2 ans minimum 4 mois Logisticien 5 A3 Bac +2 en Logistique, Transport 2 ans minimum 6 mois Assistant administratif 2 A3 Administration et Gestion des Ressources Humaines 2 ans minimum 6 mois Chauffeur 10 4ème catégorie CFEPD 2 ans minimum 12 mois Manutentionnaire 2 1ère catégorie CFEPD 2 ans minimum 6 mois Gardiens 2 2ème catégorie CFEPD 2 ans minimum 12 mois   Le recrutement sera assuré par un cabinet spécialisé, conformément aux exigences et procédures applicables. Les agents recrutés seront rémunérés suivant la grille salariale applicable au personnel contractuel de l’Institut National de la Statistique (INS).   PRISE EN CHARGE La prise en charge du recrutement et des salaires des agents concernés sera assurée par le « Projet d’Harmonisation et d’Amélioration des Statistiques de l’Afrique de l’Ouest et du Centre (PHASAOC) », avec un financement de la Banque mondiale (BM).     MÉTHODE DE SÉLECTION ET DÉPÔT DES PLIS :   Le dossier de manifestation d’intérêt devra comprendre les pièces suivantes :   Une lettre de manifestation d’intérêt signée par le représentant habilité du cabinet ; Une présentation générale du cabinet précisant notamment sa raison sociale, son statut juridique, son année de création, son adresse, ses domaines d’intervention et ses principales activités ; Une présentation de l’expérience générale du cabinet dans le domaine du recrutement et de la gestion des ressources humaines ; REPUBLIQUE DU NIGER

Fraternité-Travail-Progrès

MINISTERE DE L’ECONOMIE ET DES FINANCES

INSTITUT NATIONAL DE LA STATISTIQUE

ETABLISSEMENT PUBLIC A CARACTERE ADMINISTRATIF

DIRECTION GENERALE

PROJET D’HARMONISATION ET D’AMELIORATION DES STATISTIQUES EN AFRIQUE DE L’OUEST ET DU CENTRE (PHASAOC) - CREDIT IDA 73140 NE 182, rue de la Sirba - BP 13416 Niamey - NIGER • Tél. : (227) 20 72 35 60 • Fax : (227) 20 72 21 74 • https://www.ins.ne • E-mail : ins@ins.ne

 

AVIS DE SOLLICITATION DE MANIFESTATION D’INTÉRÊT

 

SELECTION D'UN CABINET POUR LE RECRUTEMENT DU PERSONNEL COMPLEMENTAIRE DU BCR DANS LE CADRE DU 5 EME RGPH

 

 

  1. CONTEXTE ET JUSTIFICATIONS 

 

Dans le cadre de la mise en œuvre des activités du Projet d’Harmonisation et d’Amélioration des Statistiques en Afrique de l’Ouest et du Centre (PHASAOC), notamment la réalisation du Cinquième Recensement Général de la Population et de l’Habitat (RGP/H), l’Institut National de la Statistique (INS) a mis en place le Bureau Central de Recensement (BCR), organe technique chargé de la planification, de la coordination et du pilotage global des activités du recensement.

Au regard de l’ampleur des opérations, de la charge de travail administrative et logistique pour le fonctionnement du BCR ainsi que des besoins en ressources humaines au BCR, il est nécessaire de recruter sous contrat à durée déterminée, quinze (15) démographes/Ingénieurs Statisticiens Economistes (ISE), six (06) Ingénieurs des Travaux/Pratiques Statistiques (ITS/IPS), trois (03) Techniciens Supérieurs de la Statistique (TSS), (9) comptables, deux (02) assistants administratifs, cinq (5) logisticiens, dix (10) chauffeurs et deux (02) manœuvres.

Par ailleurs, il est prévu le recrutement de deux gardiens pour assurer la sécurité des sites et des matériels qui y seront entreposés, dans le cadre des travaux de construction des sièges de l’Institut National de la Statistique (INS) et de l’Ecole Nationale de la Statistique (ENSTAT).

Ces recrutements visent, d’une part, à garantir le bon fonctionnement du BCR et à soutenir l’exécution efficace des activités préparatoires et opérationnelles du RGP/H et, d’autre part sécuriser les sites destinés aux travaux de construction des sièges de l’INS et de l’ENSTAT.

 

  1. OBJECTIFS

Objectif général

L'objectif principal est de doter le Bureau Central de Recensement (BCR) d'un capital humain qualifié et opérationnel afin d'assurer une exécution fluide, rigoureuse et dans les délais de l'ensemble des activités du 5ème RGP/H.

Objectifs spécifiques

•             Renforcer l'expertise technique en matière de conception, d'analyse des données, de cartographie et de traitement statistique.

•             Optimiser la gestion financière et comptable des ressources allouées à l'opération de recensement.

•             Assurer un appui administratif et logistique rigoureux pour la gestion des flux de matériels, de la documentation et du déploiement sur le terrain.

•             Garantir la mobilité et la manutention sécurisées des équipes et des équipements sur toute l'étendue du territoire

•             Assurer la sécurité des sites destinés à la construction des sièges de l’INS et de l’ENSTAT.

 

 

  1. LES RESULTATS ATTENDUS

 

Les résultats attendus de la mise en œuvre de cette activité sont :

  • Sur le plan technique : Les méthodologies, les questionnaires, l'analyse des données et la production des rapports thématiques du 5ème RGP/H sont exécutés selon les standards internationaux de qualité.
  • Sur le plan financier : La gestion des budgets est transparente, les pièces justificatives sont rigoureusement tenues et les rapports financiers sont produits à bonne date.
  • Sur le plan administratif : l'archivage, le suivi des courriers et la gestion des ressources humaines du BCR sont assurés de manière fluide.
  • Sur le plan logistique : L'approvisionnement, le stockage et le déploiement du matériel de recensement sont correctement gérés.
  • Sur le plan opérationnel : Le déplacement des équipes d'encadrement et la manutention des équipements sont sécurisés et effectués dans le respect des calendriers établis ;
  • Les sites destinés aux travaux de construction des sièges de l’INS et de l’ENSTAT sont sécurisés.
  1. ORGANISATION ET MÉTHODOLOGIE

Un bureau de recrutement sera choisi pour appuyer la Direction Générale de l’Institut National de la Statistique (INS) dans le recrutement des candidats aux différents postes.

Les profils recherchés pour les différents postes sont consignés dans le tableau ci-dessous.

  1. PRISE EN CHARGE

La prise en charge du recrutement et des salaires des agents concernés sera assurée par le « Projet d’Harmonisation et d’Amélioration des Statistiques de l’Afrique de l’Ouest et du Centre (PHASAOC) », avec un financement de la Banque mondiale (BM).

 

 

  1. MÉTHODE DE SÉLECTION ET DÉPÔT DES PLIS :

 

Le dossier de manifestation d’intérêt devra comprendre les pièces suivantes :

 

  • Une lettre de manifestation d’intérêt signée par le représentant habilité du cabinet ;
  • Une présentation générale du cabinet précisant notamment sa raison sociale, son statut juridique, son année de création, son adresse, ses domaines d’intervention et ses principales activités ;
  • Une présentation de l’expérience générale du cabinet dans le domaine du recrutement et de la gestion des ressources humaines ;
  • Une liste des principales missions similaires réalisées au cours des cinq (5) dernières années, précisant notamment le nom du client, l’objet de la mission, la période d’exécution et les principales prestations réalisées ;
  • Les justificatifs des références similaires déclarées, notamment les contrats, attestations de bonne exécution, certificats de service fait ou tout autre document permettant d’en vérifier l’authenticité ;
  • La liste du personnel clé proposé pour l’exécution de la mission, accompagnée de leurs curriculums vitae (CV) à jour ;
  • Les copies des diplômes et attestations de formation du personnel clé proposé ;
  • Une note méthodologique succincte présentant l’approche envisagée pour la recherche, la présélection, l’évaluation et la présentation des candidats aux différents postes ;
  • Les documents administratifs requis permettant d’attester de l’existence légale et de la régularité du cabinet, conformément à la réglementation en vigueur et aux exigences applicables au projet ;
  • Tout autre document permettant d’apprécier les qualifications, l’expérience et la capacité du cabinet à réaliser la mission.

 

Les dossiers de candidature doivent être déposés au plus tard le 4 Novembre 2026 à 16 H00, heure locale de Niamey (TU+1) :

Sous plis fermés à l’INSTITUT NATIONAL DE LA STATISTIQUE (INS) Projet d’Harmonisation et d’Amélioration des Statistiques en Afrique de l’Ouest et du Centre (PHASAOC) BP : 13 416 Niamey – Niger Téléphone : (227) 20 72 35 60,

2 -ème étage porte 212 ; En portant sur l’enveloppe la mention : « SÉLECTION D’UN CABINET POUR LE RECRUTEMENT DU PERSONNEL COMPLÉMENTAIRE DU BCR DANS LE CADRE DU 5ÈME RGP/H ».

Le Cabinet sera sélectionné en accord avec les procédures définies dans le « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets (FPI) » Révision de Septembre 2023 puis en février 2025.

 

 

 

LE COORDONNATEUR

The successful Bidder shall complete the supply of the Goods, including delivery to the Final Destination as specified in the Bidding Documents and the completion of all Related Services, within 180 days from the date of contract signature and notification of the Contract.

3.       Bidding will be conducted through open national Bidding (LIB) procedures as specified in the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers for Goods, Works, Non-Consulting services” dated February 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), and is open to the following eligible Bidders or their authorized local representatives as follows:

- Huawei or their authorized local representatives

- TP-Link or their authorized local representatives

- CICT Mobile or their authorized local representatives

4.         Bids will be evaluated in accordance with the evaluation process set out in the bidding documents. The selection of acceptable bids will be dependent on 100% compliance with Mandatory criteria identified in the technical specification document.  For this contract, the lowest evaluated substantially responsive Bid shall be selected for award.

5.         Interested eligible Bidders may obtain further information from the Council for Development and Reconstruction and inspect the bidding document during office hours from 9:00 to 15:00 hours from Monday till Friday at the address stated at the end of this Specific Procurement Notice (SPN).

8.         All Bids must be accompanied by a Bid Security of Thirty Thousand US Dollars (US$ 30,000).         

9.         Attention is drawn to the Procurement Regulations requiring the Borrower to disclose information on the successful bidder’s beneficial ownership, as part of the Contract Award Notice, using the Beneficial Ownership Disclosure Form as included in the bidding document.
